Title: MC MBSE Ansys SAM 25R1 BETA H1 Baseline: Cameo imported project treats Integer elements as String variables
Message: MC MBSE Ansys SAM 25R1 BETA H1 Baseline: Cameo imported project treats Integer elements as String variables Attached are a screenshot showing what this looks like in the MC MBSE spawned from the Ansys SAM web interface, as well as the Cameo project I used to import into Ansys SAM.  Basically, I was running into some issues with getting an analysis set up to test against the current iteration of Ansys SAM, when I opted to dig in deeper to how the Ansys SAM MC MBSE interface was treating some of the Systems Model Elements. When I compared the variable type in Cameo ("Integer") to how those variables were showing in the MC MBSE as brought up by Ansys SAM ("String"), this felt like a bug to me.  Reproduction steps: 1) Open a new project in Ansys SAM 2) Choose the SysMLv2 option 3) Choose to import a file 4) Choose the mdzip attached to this issue 5) Finish importing and create the project. You can also click here, where I did the above and I believe it's publicly accessible to other users? https://sam-testing.ansys.com:9050/orgs/MyOrga/projects/468e83e0-00ed-4f53-acbe-75863889af89 6) From there, I used the "File" menu to "Open in ModelCenter", which brings up MC MBSE for Ansys SAM (you need to have the relevant installers set up). Dragging in those System Model Elements that I referenced and seeing how MC MBSE displayed them as String variables is how I saw the issue.

Title: Missing options in Edit Layout Component dialog box
Message: Missing options in Edit Layout Component dialog box When originally adding a layout component (LC) to a mechanical design, the option exists to map variables in the source layout to LC instance parameters.  This is done in the Variable Mapping tab of the Insert Layout Component dialog box: The same functionality is seen in the Edit Layout Component dialog box and, while you cannot revert target values originally mapped to instance parameters , you can choose to map additional variables that you didn't previously: The Parameters tab of the Insert Layout Component dialog box includes an option to create local variables of any LC instance parameters.  It also allows the user to specify which type of local variable to create (Design or Project): However, the Edit Layout Component dialog box does NOT include the local variable options.  Presumably, this means that, if users decide to edit the LC to map additional variables to instance parameters, they cannot create local variables of those additional parameters.  This forces users to either delete and recreate the LC or, if possible, manually define local variables with the same name as the instance parameters.  I'm not sure if these separately defined local variables would function fully in the same manner as those created automatically by the Insert Layout Component dialog box. This limitation of editing functions/options seems unnecessary and rather arbitrary to me.  Ideally, users should be free to tweak any property of an LC they are editing.  I would further argue that it should be possible to revert previously defined instance parameters and to also automatically delete the associated local variables, assuming the user had chosen to create them.  The limitations violate basic usability practices, and the differences between the LC creation and editing processes feel unnecessary. I've attached an archive ( Bug 1144782.aedtz ) of a simple cartoonish LC, which includes geometry variables in the source layout suitable for mapping to variables for testing purposes. Post 2025R2

Title: Missing F1 help codes for two pair of dialog box tabs in Icepak
Message: Missing F1 help codes for two pair of dialog box tabs in Icepak Two tabs of the Insert Layout Component and Edit Layout Component dialog boxes are assigned F1 codes for context sensitive help as follows: Property  tab:  2909118 (decimal), 0x2C63BE (hex) Board tab:  2909133 (decimal), 0x2C63CD (hex) The F1 code for each tab is the same for both the Insert LC and Edit LC dialog boxes. These two codes, in hexadecimal form, should be represented within the Modeler file used for context-sensitive help for commands associated with the 3D Modeler or in the Icepak file used for Icepak-specific IDs.  Each code should be correlated to a help ID string, something like  HID INSERTOREDIT LC BOARD TAB ICEPAK , for example. Title: Desktop installer: The master setup file does not give an option to run Console installer and ignores default YAML template
Message: Desktop installer: The master setup file does not give an option to run Console installer and ignores default YAML template There are basically two issues: The master file at the root of the package doesn't provide an option to run the installation in console mode. To do that, you need to navigate to Product > Deployment and use . However, I am not sure whether this way is officially recommended. When launching the desktop installer via , it doesn't recognize the installation parameters.yaml Scenario: Download a full Ansys Minerva installation package for 25R2. Unzip it. In the root folder, you can see a file and a YAML template named  installation parameters.yaml  Double-click the file. Expected: It should give the user options to choose from Console and Desktop installers, knowing the fact that Desktop installer can only be used for small/single-node installations. Current: It runs the desktop installer, by default, leaving no option to run the Console installer. In the Desktop installer, you expect to see the option values prefilled using the  installation parameters.yaml, but all options appear empty.

Title: Maxwell2D Documentation Clarification for Machine Options Report Quantities
Message: Maxwell2D Documentation Clarification for Machine Options Report Quantities In the attached project, the average and rms machine options report is used to calculate RMS quantities for the phase voltage.  There is some confusion regarding the method the calculations are using, the request is to add clarification on the algorithm used for the listed quantities.  In this particular example to clarify which RMS calculation method is used, trueRMS, fundamentalRMS?  It doesn't seem to be either: The report shows terminal voltage and the following in the legends and tables: Top legend: TrueRMS (square root of average sum of squares) and the fundamental RMS (fundamental harmonic magnitude over sqrt(2)) from trace characteristics.   Middle Table: The fundamental RMS from the FFT. Bottom Table: The Machine Options AvgPhaseVoltage. The AvgPhaseVoltage waveform doesn't agree with other calculation method.  When there is not harmonic distortion they do agree.  Some clarification of the method used would be helpful in the documentation to help diagnose any potential user error.

Title: Additional Information in Motor-CAD manual Especially skewing In Motor-CAD
Message: Additional Information in Motor-CAD manual Especially skewing In Motor-CAD while answering a question on skewing in Motor-CAD, I found the documentation in the help to be quite sparse. It would be nice, if you add some more information / formulas and maybe also a reference for point 1) and 2). 3) is a more general enhancement request. 1) ASM circuit skewing method. The following two methods are completely undocumented. I assume they can be found in these books, but it would be nice if the formulas are stated in the help. C.G. Veinott, Theory and design of small induction motors, McGraw-Hill, New York, 1959 R. Richter R – "Elektrische Maschinen" Springer, 1954 2) The article "cointinuous skew" in the help is a bit confusing, since the Continuous Skew Method setting can only be found under Defaults > Default Settings. It would be nice if this could be either written in the help, or if there was a setting in the regular GUI. --- 3) In general I find the "Default Settings" menu in general lacks documentation. Some settings are also available in the "normal" GUI, like: While other settings, such as the skew -> Harmonic setting mentioned above, is not available in the normal GUI. And then there are many settings that lack explanation in general. E.g. here is an extreme case with 0 (?) documentation or reference in the help what these settings refer to.

Title: Unexpected Elemental Mean with dropped nodes
Message: Unexpected Elemental Mean with dropped nodes The elemental mean for quadratic elements with dropped nodes yields unexpected values. It looks like Mechanical interpolates to midside nodes that are not dropped and then averages over all the non-dropped nodes. Here is a concrete example:   An example can be viewed in the attached workbench project: Open system A6 Check the single element result:   This result can be analyzed with the the following dpf script: ``` from ansys.dpf.core import Model, locations, Scoping, operators import numpy as np rst = r"Static structural Elements files\dp0\SYS\MECH\file.rst" model = Model(rst) element id = 5742 stress op = model.results.stress() stress op.inputs.requested location(locations.elemental nodal) stress op.inputs.mesh scoping(Scoping(location=locations.elemental nodal, ids=[element id])) field = stress op.eval()[0] data = field.data[:,0] conn = model.metadata.meshed region.elements.connectivities field.get entity data by id(element id) # Connectivity indicates, this is Prism element with Q,R,T and Y,Z,A nodes dropped # See: https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/account/secured?returnurl=/Views/Secured/corp/v232/en/ans elem/Hlp E SOLID186.html print(conn) # midside node values of non-dropped nodes U,V,X midside = [(data[3]+data[4])/2, (data[4]+data[5])/2, (data[5]+data[3])/2] average mech = (np.sum(midside) + np.sum(data))/9 average res exp = (np.sum(data))/6` print("Average Mechanical:", average mech) print("Average Result Explorer:", average res exp) ``` Output: [1577 1753 1674 2418 2433 2420   -1   -1   -1 4589 4599 4588   -1   -1    -1] Average Mechanical: 352332.5138888889 Average Result Explorer: 269718.4583333333 Modify the file path to point to the correct rst file. The average mech value reproduces the value shown in Mechanical. Mechanical Post; Triaged

Title: Optislang defaults to beta pyconsole rendering Fluent 'execute commands' and expressions useless as the pyconsole doesn't read in the scheme console commands
Message: Optislang defaults to beta pyconsole rendering Fluent 'execute commands' and expressions useless as the pyconsole doesn't read in the scheme console commands @Bernd Buettner  and I have found a bug while working on a time critical project for AstraZeneca which requires end users with little to no simulation experience to be able to use sensitivity analysis functions within optislang. When trying to run a Fluent VOF with species tracer case in optislang, the automated patches set up in the execute commands section in fluent (removing the need for journal files to help end users) cannot be read in as the fluent session opened in optislang defaults to the beta pyconsole and the commands are then invalid which means the fluid and the tracer are not patched in and the simulation is then completely incorrect. There is an expression set within the case that helps to set the rsd value for the patched tracer that stops the variable being set to 'Not a Number' because of the tracer not being patched in yet which we can track whether it's working by checking the transcript file and seeing if it gets evaluated to 'Not a Number' or not - this is also not respected in 25r1. The expressions issue seem to have been fixed in 25r2 from what we can tell with the transcript files alongside respecting the iteration number the patches are supposed to be used in, which has improved from 25r1 which would try read in the commands at iteration 1 despite them being separated out (due to possibly another bug but within Fluent for the execute commands). We've found a workaround which is using Fluent parametric workflow with optislang used for the creation of design points within fluent but the customer does not want to be using workarounds, especially with the involvement of complicated journal files etc due to the capability of the end users. We've been in contact with @Tejal Deepak Prabhu  who has looked through the evidence and reached out to other colleagues who confirmed this needed to be logged as a bug.  I have shared the case file (permission to be used internally but not external use due to the impeller being customer's geometry) with Tejal and a screenshot of the commands issue. I cannot upload the case file to this bug due to the size. This bug being fixed is critical to AZ user adoption of optislang as this case was supposed to be used to push internally for its usage. Title: Mesh Fusion Results Disagreement with Explicit Solve in 3DL, also Slower and More RAM?
Message: Mesh Fusion Results Disagreement with Explicit Solve in 3DL, also Slower and More RAM? Google's quantum team was seeking to improve solve speed by parallelizing a model across their cluster.  They wanted a way to break out different meander resonators, solve them in parallel, and stitch the answer back together.  Their model is shown in the image below. The red line represents a CPW with feed at the left end, and the green line represents a half-wave open circuited CPW resonator that is coupled to by the portion where red and green both exist side-by-side.  I drew metal squares over all of the 8 meander resonators  (that each have many rounded bends and therefore take a lot of mesh) so that they would not be included in the model.  The diagonal black lines are to indicate that the meanders will not be part of the solve.  In other words, start simple.  The test is to first see how we can break a simple transmission line model into parts before going for the more complex design including the resonators. The response for the explicit model, with just the feed transmission line and single half-wave resonator, has an S11 resonance around 4.5GHz, presumably from the half-wave resonator.  The various S11 traces shown below are for Mixed Order single frequency adapt, Mixed Order broadband adapt, and First Order broadband adapt (from right to left). One important detail is that because full reflection is experienced, traditional convergence was not working well, so I forced 15 adaptive passes.  The mesh looks as expected, with the transmission lines being meshed well. My first attempt at using mesh fusion has not been able to match.  I had two comparison cases: 1) Mesh fusion, 2) Mesh fusion with parallel adapt.  Both were set up with dividing lines like:   The mesh looks like the below:   But the S11 response is much wider, shifted in frequency, and has an extra dip.  When compared (turquoise is mesh fusion using mixed order elements, the others are explicit), the results are not matching.  Quantum applications require precise narrow band resonances to be found, so these wide dips offset in frequency are a no go. I noticed this that fields from a discrete sweep are not available for plotting with mesh fusion (defect), so I cannot plot to visualize what the dips are from.  The mesh fusion first order solution is the green trace below that shows no resonance:   The solve time using mesh fusion was much slower (~20x) and used substantially more RAM (~10x) than the explicit case.  The below is for Mixed Order.                  Explicit                Mesh Fusion (no parallel refinement) Time        2min33sec               56min RAM         3.1GB                      32.1GB   Is there something wrong with my setup or assumptions?  The real model including resonators would have a dramatically higher element count.   The designs to compare are highlighted below.  Setup1 for each is the mixed order setup.

Title: Prevent closed loops between Motion Definitions and Reference Frames
Message: Prevent closed loops between Motion Definitions and Reference Frames The motion definition can be defined using a reference frame definition, and now (as of R25.1) a reference frame definition can be defined using a motion definition. We should ensure that the code detects when such definitions refer to each other in a closed loop and not allow it / warn the user through a pop-up dialog. For example, if you have a motion definition named md1 that is defined using a reference frame named rf1 , we should make sure that rf1 is not defined using md1 .  We should also prevent  loops made out of larger numbers of these definitions, such as: rf1 is defined using md1, which is defined using rf2, which is defined using md2, which is defined using rf1. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 RC Alfa: Issues with Parsing Binary Output File Variables in Nastran 2023
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 RC Alfa: Issues with Parsing Binary Output File Variables in Nastran 2023 Using the old MSC Nastran Training documents as a reference, I encountered issues when wrapping both an old legacy .op2 file from the training materials and a freshly generated .op2 file using Nastran 2023. The training document mentions that for parsing the binary output file variable, the first sub-category is the "Result Type" dropdown. In the current QW, the "Displacement" category is gone, replaced by cryptically named items like "Element Step=1" or "Node Step=1". More familiar item names like "Node Thickness" and "Position" are present, but using "Step=1" as the Result Type allowed me to select the other sub-categories referenced in the training document to filter down the variables. Despite this, the training expected only one variable left after filtering, but I had two. Additionally, if you deselect the binary output file variable and then click back on it again, the "selection criteria" doesn't set itself to the parameters used to find/filter that variable as expected, leaving the "Variables List" pane empty. Steps to Reproduce: Wrap both an old legacy .op2 file from the training materials and a freshly generated .op2 file using Nastran 2023. Attempt to parse the binary output file variable using the "Result Type" dropdown. Observe that the "Displacement" category is gone, replaced by cryptically named items like "Element Step=1" or "Node Step=1". Use "Step=1" as the Result Type to select other sub-categories referenced in the training document. Note that the training expected only one variable left after filtering, but two variables are present. Deselect the binary output file variable and click back on it again. Observe that the "selection criteria" doesn't set itself to the parameters used to find/filter that variable, leaving the "Variables List" pane empty. Expected Result: The "Displacement" category should be present in the "Result Type" dropdown, and filtering should result in only one variable as expected. The "selection criteria" should retain the parameters used to find/filter the variable when reselected. Actual Result: The "Displacement" category is gone, replaced by cryptically named items. Filtering results in two variables instead of one. The "selection criteria" doesn't retain the parameters used to find/filter the variable when reselected, leaving the "Variables List" pane empty. mcaft

Title: Resolved SOEC model, intialization and patching bug
Message: Resolved SOEC model, intialization and patching bug An attempt to patch the protonic potential, does not work reliably, It is a matter of luck to be able to reproduce this error.  To reproduce this defect, please follow these steps. Load in the attached case and data files on a single core in Windows in double precision. Initialize the case with standard initialization. 3. Have a look at the protonic potenial distribution. 4. This does not make sense an attempt to repatch the value to 0.5 in the catalysts and in membrane sometimes work some time it does not. 5. After initialization the mole fraction of steam is 1 regardless of the initialzation value. Effectively, the workaround is to patch these values to 0 first and then to the desired values, and even then there is no 100 guarantee that everything is going to be assigned consistently. Please find the source of this incredibly frustrating bug. I think it has been fixed in PEMFC and in the unresolved SOFC modules a long time ago, but not in FC&E.  Without this smart patching the solution blows up even with almost all options being switched off and  despite electrochemical activity being reduced by 2 orders of magnitude. Suggestions for the smart initialization: Species distribution to be spread in accordance with the inlet conditions for species and applied for the channels, GDL's and catalysts. "Anode" electronic potential to be set to 0 across all zones except the cathode side and membrane. "Cathode" electronic potential to be set to the nominal value taken from the cathode terminal Membrane electronic potential to be set to 0 The protonic potential to be set to the value of one half of the prescribed potential difference e.g. (1.1-0)/2 0.55 in the catalysts and in the membrane and 0 value everywhere else. The velocity field either to be set 0 in case of the standard initialization or to the hybrid initialization values. so no action is required for it. Hope this helps, but please fix this spurious assignment of the species distribution and the distributions for the potentials that you are able to see in the attached files. I would consider this defect as being critical. It is counter-intuitive and labour intensive to come up with the decent initialization at present. Kind regards, Aleksey.l

Title: Torque-Speed Curve Convergence Issue with IM Lab Link (2025R2 Testing)
Message: Torque-Speed Curve Convergence Issue with IM Lab Link (2025R2 Testing) Hi @Sarah Woodrow  , @Etienne Kaiser  , @Sufei Li , I need to report this bug I found while trying the latest release of the IM Lab Link. I followed the following workflow: Created the Motor-CAD model using the template e5, nothing has been modified. Did the export to Maxwell and created the Maxwell model. Enabled the Lab Maxwell link and did Setup Model, Analyse Model and Import Model. Calculated performance maps. Everything worked fine, no errors and the LUT have been imported successfully with reasonable values. The issue occurred when I calculated the torque vs speed, the model has convergence problems, like this: Here the comparison with the calculation using Motor-CAD LUTs: I'm not concerned about the different performance, just the convergence errors, which can't be solved by playing with the initial slip. I have checked all the LUT and compared with the ones calculated by Motor-CAD with the native FEA Advanced method in Lab: There is a bit of discrepancy between the two software, but it is fine, since we are using two different solvers and it shouldn't cause convergence errors in Motor-CAD. The only suspicious thing is that the stator phase inductance and magnetizing inductance from Maxwell are very close, almost equal, when they should differ like the ones calculated with Motor-CAD code. What need to be checked is if Ls and Lm value very close to each other can be annoying for Motor-CAD post-processing. Meanwhile I need to check what the Maxwell API does and the reason why these two LUTs are so similar.  I have attached some files for reference: LUT Comparison.m collects the LUTs data from the Lab Link and from Motor-CAD FEA Advanced Lab. MCAD export ANSYSEM 2D.aedtz is the Maxwell model already solved. MCAD model.mot is the Motor-CAD model with the Lab link setup. MCAD ref.mot is the same model but solved with M-CAD native lab. collects the LUTs name in Motor-CAD

Title: Deleting a project from the Project Manager only removes the .aedt file (not results or aedb subfolders)
Message: Deleting a project from the Project Manager only removes the .aedt file (not results or aedb subfolders) When started, AEDT creates a new file ("Project x ").  Occasionally, I'll use this new project to perform a quick test or to capture some images for the documentation.  When done, I right-click the project name in the Project Manager and choose Delete Project Permanently from Disk , thinking it's gone from my drive.  However, the next time I launch AEDT, the new project number has been incremented.  The reason is that the previous one has not been properly cleaned up from the drive.  The Project x. aedtresults  folder and  Project x. aedb folder (when applicable) remain behind and have to be deleted manually using Windows File Explorer. There's no point in keeping these orphaned folders when a project is deleted.  The deletion routine should perform a comprehensive cleanup of files and related subfolders.

Title: Fluent case file refresh button not working
Message: Fluent case file refresh button not working In many situations, when there is a modification in the fluent case file used for 2-way coupling simulations, the user needs to click the refresh button to make those changes affect the application, such as when the fluent time step is changed. However, most of the times (I would guess 9 out of 10), the refresh button has no effect. The workaround is to delete the fluent validation.cache file, reopen the project, and click the refresh button again.  I think when clicked, the refresh button should trigger the same thing that is triggered when a fresh .cas file is loaded. Steps to reproduce the behavior: Load a .cas file for a 2-way Fluent simulation Open the .cas file and change the time step Overwrite the .cas file and close Fluent Click the refresh button Check the timestep in the Solver tab (compare the output interval)   QA Process

Title: Liquid Bridge + CGM causing overlap detection at inlet
Message: Liquid Bridge + CGM causing overlap detection at inlet I have detected the following behavior when testing the liquid bridge module with tutorial 18. I decreased the particle size of the Wet Additive in order to have more particles. When injecting the particles without CGM, it works as expected, if I reduce the particle size 10x and use a CGM of 10, no particles will be injected with a warning of overlap detected at the inlet. Steps to reproduce: Open attached case and run for a few outputs. See that injects particles normally Delete results, select the Wet Additive particle, decrease its size 10x and input a CGM Scale Factor of 10. In theory, the final parcel should be the same size as the particle without CGM. However, if we run the case, it won't inject the particles due to overlap detection at the inlet Delete the results, disable liquid bridge and try to run with CGM - Particles injected normally as well I tested with 25R1.0 and 25R2 DEV from May 20th with the same behavior.  Development; QA Process; Triaged

Title: Sensitivity not working with Linked Parameters
Message: Sensitivity not working with Linked Parameters I was trying to run a thermal sensitivity study on a BPMOR machine, noticed that using Linked Parameters to link 2 variations (each with 4 occurrencies) does not produce any result. Removing the linked parameter, thus running 4x4=16 variations, does work. The problems is not model specific, as I was able to reproduce it also on the default BPMOR (see attached model and vvf file of the sensitivity). I also noticed that, despite I want the "Gap Shaft-Axle [F]" parameter to depend on the "Gap Shaft-Axle" and set the linked parameters in the below way from GUI and mouse: when I confirm my choice with mouse click, first the list of available parameters returns to the very top and when I scroll down to the parameters I did set I find that the selection of linked parameter has been "shifted up" by one row, not the one I had selected (also, it makes no sense that the parameter is both master and slave!): Clearing the Linked parameter, saving the mot file and setting it up again (making the variation on "Front" depend on the active gap) leads to successful visualization of the link, but still pressing "Run Parameter Study" takes no time and results are not available: I feared this might be related to the thermal module of BPMOR, so I run a similar test on the e10 template for an e-mag sensitivity, playing with the shaft diameter (files attached), but I obtain the same lack of results and "shifting up" of the linked param (this time the clear/save/link strategy did not work): Again, removing the parameter link and running the full factorial of combinations did produce results:

Title: [Beta] First re-solve of simulation with monitored value convergence solved and saved in previous version uses numerical convergence

Title: Resource leak in rep_scheduler library
Message: Resource leak in rep scheduler library The code in function SetDataFileSecurityAttributes() in file core/lib/AnsoftCOML/schedulers/rep scheduler/ contains a resource leak in an error case. If the pSD pointer variable contains the address of data successfully allocated by the LocalAlloc call, but the result variable is set to false due to a failure of a later function call within this function, then sa.lpSecurityDescriptor is not set to pSD and LocalFree is never called on the pSD pointer. The fix is to call LocalFree() on this pointer before returning from this function if the result variable is false.

Title: Twin Builder 2025R1: Simulation Fails with only a VHDL-AMS Constant Block
Message: Twin Builder 2025R1: Simulation Fails with only a VHDL-AMS Constant Block This issue is specific to the customer's environment and is difficult to reproduce in our environment. I have been discussing it with the Twin Builder Expert Teams. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ■Issue I am currently facing an issue that seems to occur only in my customer's environment, and I am having difficulty analyzing the root cause. Here is a summary of the phenomenon: The simulation always fails when a VHDL-AMS model is included in the project. TR analysis fails even when the project contains only a single Const block (VHDL-AMS). The following error message is returned: Error 13362 – Fatal error during initialization of simulator <SECM> >>Initialize If he run the project with only an SML block, the simulation completes successfully. Compiling the VHDL-AMS model alone also succeeds without any errors. Executing "Update definitions" for the model does not help. The customer is using Twin Builder 2025R1 on a low-spec PC via Remote Desktop. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ■Comments from @Vel Ambalavanar   Just to make sure - it is not only the const block - any VHDL component in the schematic giving this error? This fatal error message means something got crashed. But one thing is very strange - the error number and the message following that do not tally. Actually 13362 should correspond to Prepare ( Fatal error during preparation of simulator <SECM>.  >> Prepare ). The correct number for the fatal error during Initialize is 13363. So there must be something really corrupted. Could you please ask the customer to double check that number and the message?  Could you please ask the customer to try with a version other than 25.1, if available? Also please check if it is possible for the customer to uninstall, delete everything, and reinstall (clean install) 25.1? We will investigate what could be the root cause for this. Probably the next steps could be sending some custom DLLs with more log messages to get a clue. We will keep you posted. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ■Reply Regarding the components that trigger the error: So far, I have only confirmed the issue with the CONST block and thermal components in VHDL-AMS. My customer hasn’t tested other components yet, but I am planning to suggest a few simple ones to the customer so he can try those as well.   Below is the full error message. In my previous message, I omitted some parts, but the following additional errors are also appearing: Error 10523 and 10533.     I will also ask the customer to try a different version of Twin Builder, and to perform an uninstall and clean reinstall if possible. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ■Customer testing The customer has confirmed that an error occurs even with a simple electrical circuit and only a Sine block. Attachment: VHDL test.aedt Best regards, Naoya Hashiguchi 2025 R2 SP04

Title: An error occurred when trying to use the toolkit（such as LTI,RSROM, etc.）
Message: An error occurred when trying to use the toolkit（such as LTI,RSROM, etc.） ■Description of the issue I got an error as below when I try to use Thermal model identification tool.  ※I replaced my PC within the past month, so I suspect the issue might be environment-related. The previous PC didn’t have this problem. -------------------------------------------- *Global - Messages   [error] TypeLoadException: 親が存在しないため、アセンブリ System.Private.CoreLib, Version=6.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e の型 System.Object を読み込めませんでした。  In file "C:/Program Files/ANSYS Inc/v251/AnsysEM/syslib/Toolkits/TwinBuilder/Thermal Model ", line 2 ---- While executing script: C:/Program Files/ANSYS Inc/v251/AnsysEM/syslib/Toolkits/TwinBuilder/Thermal Model English: TypeLoadException: Could not load type 'System.Object' from assembly 'System.Private.CoreLib, Version=6.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e' because its parent could not be found. -------------------------------------------- ■Reference information from @Christophe Petre   I have had that issue some time ago, and could fix it by modifying the PATH environment variable. Please refer to the following bugs on similar topics : Bug 969212: Error while launching Toolkits on some machines. - Boards , Bug 771838: Could not load type 'System.Object' from assembly 'System.Private.CoreLib' - Boards , Bug 886932: Ironpython scripts produce error: Could not load type system.Private.CoreLib Version 6.0.0.0 - Boards . ■Investigation I tried to remove powershell environment, but it doesn't work.  I've been doing various debugging, but it seems that PowerShell 7 is not installed on my system. ■Workaround This is the .NET environment information from my system. batch file -------------------------------------------- @echo off set DOTNET ROOT= set PATH=C:\Windows\system32;C:\Windows start "" "C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\AnsysEM\" -------------------------------------------- ●set DOTNET ROOT= This command temporarily disables the DOTNET ROOT environment variable, which is one of the reasons the .NET 6/7/8 runtime might be used. By clearing this variable, TwinBuilder and IronPython are prevented from mistakenly using the .NET Core runtime. After applying the batch file, I confirmed that the toolkit is now working properly. ■Consideration I found that using statements like clr.AddReference("System.Windows.Forms") may cause issues on modern PC environments where .NET 6, 7, or 8 is installed. Since .NET 6+ is now bundled with Windows 11 and Visual Studio 2022 or later, this kind of script may behave unexpectedly unless it's specifically isolated from the .NET Core runtime. To avoid future problems, I believe it's important to consider a fundamental redesign of the script so that it is compatible with .NET 6/7/8 environments. Best regards, Naoya Hashiguchi 2026 R1 Must Fix

Title: Polarization convention issue in Speos BSDF plugins
Message: Polarization convention issue in Speos BSDF plugins DESCRIPTION: Data : "Simplify large document at much as possible" not yet Notes : See part 8) here:  Definition of polarization and incident angle.docx I found 2 places indicating we rely on the i(kr-wt) convention not the one I was hoping for both are located in the polarization plate: once to apply the phase shift due to ordinary and extraordinary indices there is also a "shortcut" where the user can state what kind of polarizer he wants (i.e a right circular polarizer for example) and the matrices there are the ones for i(kr-wt) There is a third place where I couldn't make sure which one it is where we apply the phase shift due to TIR but sign should be important there too. And I suspect this convention should be at play in the birefringent material as well. Everywhere else, things look pretty convention agnostic (either using real valued matrices or depolarization)   So clearly the issue is located where I call the plugin: since it uses i(wt-kr) I should conjugate the Jones vectors before I send them to the plugin and conjugate them again when I get them back. Title: Problems with convergence targets in user-defined defaults for Refine
Message: Problems with convergence targets in user-defined defaults for Refine In Settings > Physics there issues with some of the convergence targets for Fluid Flow simulations in Refine (Fig. 1). Engineering convergence (target engineering convergence) and solution stopping criterion (target stopping criterion) changes are only passed to the solver if the Simulations Options for convergence are opened in the 2nd simulation created after the change. They are also passed in a new Disco session when the Simulation Options are opened. Monitored value convergence (target convergence, monitors) live-gx solver log reports that the convergence type is user halt but then gives the numerical residual target (Fig. 2) the solver uses the default value rather than of the edited user defaults if the simulation options in the ribbon are left unopened if a simulation is created in a Disco session with the monitored value option set (requires restart), a changed target appears in the 2nd simulation if a simulation saved in a session, in which the monitored value option has been set as the default (restart required)and the default target has been changed (before or after restart), that value appears against target engineering convergence in Simulation Options (Fig. 3) As examples, I have attached 4 projects based on the same model.  Each was created in a Disco session with a different Stop on option selected (after a restart).  I created different projects for each because the option is not changed by changes to that selected in defaults.   Fig. 1:  User defaults for Refine in Settings > Physics Fig. 2:  Part of live-gx solver log when monitored value convergence is specified in the user defaults but simulation options not opened in the ribbon Fig. 3:  New value of monitored value target appears against engineering convergence for re-opened project Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: ENERSOL,,DENE & ENERSOL,,WEXT results in full harmonic analysis compared to theoretical external mechanical power
Message: ENERSOL,,DENE & ENERSOL,,WEXT results in full harmonic analysis compared to theoretical external mechanical power Hi, The attached MAPDL input file models a simple cantilever beam with SOLID185. A full harmonic sweep is performed with a constant unit force (pure real) applied to the tip. In POST26, ENERSOL,,DENE & ENERSOL,,WEXT are used to read the time averaged per cycle energy into variables. These are multiplied by variable 1 (frequency) to get time averaged damping and external power. I then use APDL to evaluate the tip averaged mechanical power applied to the tip of the cantilever. I evaluate equation 15.5.2 in  15.5: Power in an AC Circuit - Physics LibreTexts , assuming this relationship for electrical systems holds for mechanical ones as well by substituting force for voltage and velocity for current. The equation is: My Ptip calculation only equals the ENERSOL results if, in the equation above, I use SQRT(2)/2 (instead of 0.5). I can use either coefficient by commenting only one of the two following lines in the input file: !prod,13,12,,,Ptip,,,0.5 ! DIVIDE BY 2 TO GET TIME AVERAGED MECHANICAL POWER APPLIED TO TIP prod,13,12,,,Ptip,,,sqrt(2)/2 ! DIVIDE BY SQRT(2)/2 TO GET TIME AVERAGED MECHANICAL POWER APPLIED TO TIP My understanding is that for harmonic response analyses the ENERSOL results are time averaged values. But is the result supposed to be pure real? If you look at attached power.out, which the input file creates automatically, you'll see the at ENERSOL results are at phase 45 degrees, suggesting that the real and imaginary parts are equal. I'm reminded of some change in conventions for reporting power in EMAG analyses long ago. I could have easily made a mistake in my coding or interpretation of the expression used to calculate time averaged power. But even if I did, the 45 degree phase in the ENERSOL results could probably use some explanation in the Help. Thanks for your time! Bill

Title: ModelCenter 25R1: Moving an Excel Component dialog to a second monitor triggers “Pipe is broken” I/O exception and causes ModelCenter to crash
Message: ModelCenter 25R1: Moving an Excel Component dialog to a second monitor triggers “Pipe is broken” I/O exception and causes ModelCenter to crash Steps to Reproduce Using a laptop connected to a monitor, open ModelCenter on the external (larger) monitor. In the Workflow Map , click the Excel icon to open its dialog. Dialog appears on the laptop screen and is sized correctly. Drag the Excel dialog to the external monitor. Dialog text and icon become extremely large and truncated. Expand the Properties drop-down. A pop-up error appears – close both the pop-up and the dialog. Click the Excel icon again (dialog opens on the laptop screen). Expand Properties again and immediately drag the dialog to the external monitor . An error notification flashes and the Excel dialog closes automatically. Click the Excel icon a third time → ModelCenter Error dialog appears: Closing this dialog allows expanding nodes in Component Tree , but editing any value or selecting other workflow items triggers the same error with additional context: Attempting to close the file produces a final error dialog: Application must be terminated; unsaved changes are lost. Expected Result Excel dialog should remain usable after being moved between monitors and when its properties are expanded—no exceptions, no UI corruption. ModelCenter should not crash or display I/O “Pipe is broken” errors. Actual Result Dialog resizes incorrectly on secondary monitor, then throws System.IO.IOException – Pipe is broken . Subsequent operations in the same session trigger additional errors and ultimately force ModelCenter to crash.

Title: Missing faces on geometry import due to graphics card driver
Message: Missing faces on geometry import due to graphics card driver On the customer’s PC, importing .stp or .catpart files into Ansys Discovery results in missing faces in the geometry . I tested the same files on my end, but the issue is not reproducible, the models import correctly without any missing geometry. After further investigation, we concluded that the issue is related to graphics card . The customer confirmed that when trying the same files on a different PC (NVIDIA Quadro K2200), the import worked as expected. The problematic system uses an NVIDIA Quadro P2000, Driver version 32.0.15.7324  and the CATIA file version is V5. Steps already tried (unsuccessful): Updated graphics drivers Ran the CAD Configuration Manager (Reader Mode) Reset AppData folder Toggled anti-aliasing, rendering and other import options in Discovery Installed the latest service pack Some actions temporarily helped the faces reappear, such as switching to Lightweight Mode or using the Enclosure tool in meshing. However, these workarounds were not practical for the customer’s workflow, as Lightweight Mode limits access to key tools like Cleaning.  Please find the geometry file:  \\tfsattach\TFSProd\Attachments\1310xxx\1310593

Title: Workbench Archive 'without results' does not consider Sherlock rst files
Message: Workbench Archive 'without results' does not consider Sherlock rst files The issue was reported by a customer for release 2025R1 - the problem is still reproducible in 2025R2. I've attached an example wbpz archive in the bug report for easier reference. When archiving a Workbench Project without results, the rst files should not be there. This does not seem to be the case for Sherlock rst files, which continue to exist in the generated wbpz file. This may lead to unnecessary size accumulation in the final file. The only workaround I've found is to manually delete the RSTs from the Sherlock directories prior to archiving the model.

Title: Issue with Thin Body in Stacker Meshing Workflow – Custom Rendering Quality Settings
Message: Issue with Thin Body in Stacker Meshing Workflow – Custom Rendering Quality Settings Hi,  I am working on a project for one of our customers where a thin body is causing issues during meshing with the stacker workflow. The body is a simple annular disc geometry with a diameter of 210 µm and a thickness of 0.05 µm. Due to its extreme thinness compared to its other dimensions, it is recognized as a non-stackable body in stacker meshing. This results in the following warning during the Flatten Volume step: If I proceed past this warning, the Mechanical crashes after the following message during the Output step (while completing the workflow: A member of the development team suggested using custom rendering quality settings in Discovery to improve the faceting of this thin body. With certain settings, the body was successfully recognized as stackable, and the stacker mesh completed without issues. However, when the customer attempted to repeat the analysis, the stacker mesh failed — likely because they were using different custom settings. Unfortunately, Discovery does not save these custom rendering quality settings within the project file. If another project is opened with different settings, the previous configuration is lost. As a result, I no longer have the exact settings that previously allowed the mesh to succeed. I reviewed the documentation but could not find detailed guidance on what the Surface Tolerance, Normal Tolerance, and Max Edge Length parameters mean, nor how they specifically affect faceting and, ultimately, meshing. I would appreciate:  Guidance on achieving a successful stacker mesh workflow for this thin geometry Documentation or detailed explanation of the custom rendering quality settings, especially the parameters mentioned above, and how they influence faceting and meshing outcomes Any help would be greatly appreciated. Title: MDE: Parameter report processing errors
Message: MDE: Parameter report processing errors When processing filetypes that are producing EKM reports, we should be able to configure whether or not we want to: Return our transformed report Return both the EKM report and our transformed report With Case 1, the MDE-transformed report will be used in Minerva. Case 2 results in the EKM report getting transformed on the Minerva side. The MDE transform should be enhanced and have more information, so ideally, we want to use the MDE-transformed report. However, we would like the option to configure between the two options. Note: when using VCollab to create parameter reports, this falls into Case 1 - only a parameter report is returned.   Work was completed for this before, but I have discovered issues with that initial implementation - there are cases where we are transforming reports when we should be processing them (processing = cleaning up and enhancing) and vice versa. This issue was found when testing a custom extractor that produced a .metadata report. MDE was processing .metadata files that are created from custom extractors as ekm reports. This was causing the .metadata file produced from the custom extractor to be overwritten with an invalid report. I checked in a fix for the above issue, and that fixed the custom extractor but broke something else - we are now incorrectly processing parameter reports.  To fix: Report processing/transforming should be fixed for all file types, including custom extractors, and the EKM-report-returning logic should be reworked to work as expected.

Title: Getting Different Results with LiveGX and Fluent Solvers in Refine Mode (25R1) for Compressible Flow Problem
Message: Getting Different Results with LiveGX and Fluent Solvers in Refine Mode (25R1) for Compressible Flow Problem I have a case from Cummins (Customer Confidential) where they are running a compressible flow simulation in Discovery Refine mode. The issue arises when setting the fidelity to the maximum (100%) on the slider bar—whether using the "Determine Size Automatically" option or the "Curvature" and "Curvature & Proximity" options with predefined settings. At this fidelity level, with LiveGX solver; the total pressure details monitor plot starts oscillating, and the results deviate significantly from those obtained with the Fluent solver. Additionally, as the mesh is further refined by reducing the maximum element size, the LiveGX solver produces even higher total pressure values—up to 10 times greater than those from the Fluent solver. Interestingly, when the fidelity is set to the default value (slider at the middle position) or 75%, the LiveGX solver produces total pressure values closer to those obtained with the Fluent solver. Regarding the mesh, it meets the minimum orthogonal quality requirement of 0.15, with good skewness and aspect ratios, and there are no apparent issues. I tested with both Poly and Tets meshes, and the behavior remains the same. It seems something unusual is happening with the LiveGX solver, but I’m not sure what. I have attached the .dsco file here. Please take a look, and any insights would be greatly appreciated.

Title: Difference between details plot and final value of monitor when Refine LiveGX CPU solver run on 4 processors
Message: Difference between details plot and final value of monitor when Refine LiveGX CPU solver run on 4 processors For some simulations there is a problem with the final value of a force monitor on a fluid-solid interface shown in the engineering insights window when the CHT simulation is solved in Refine with the LiveGX CPU solver on the default number of processors, which is 4. I have seen the issue with the mixer tee sample model if the fluid region has been split into 2 bodies.  It is also more marked with a tet mesh than with a poly mesh.  If a face of the fluid body is split, rather than the body itself, then the final value is OK I have attached 3 projects that contain CHT simulations based on the mixer tee sample model.  The inlet velocities have been increased to more realistic values so that the force is greater than 1N.  There are 2 monitors for the z component of force, Z Force 3 is on the fluid side of the interface while Z Force 4 is on the solid side.  For the Refine stage the LiveGX CPU solver is selected and the convergence option is Monitored value so that the monitor values are written to the solver log file. Mixer Tee.dsco - no splits Split Mixer Tee.dsco - fluid body split SplitFace Mixer Tee.dsco - face of fluid body split The images below show the results obtained with the various models.  All, apart from those shown in Fig. 4 were for simulations run on a tet mesh.  I have uploaded zipped working directories to  \\Cdcw16rally02\TFSProd\Attachments\1260xxx\1260651 Fig. 1 shows that if there is no split then the final value of the force agrees with the details plot when the simulation (Mixer Tee.dsco) is run in 4 processors. The difference when  Split Mixer Tee.dsco  with the split body is run on 4 processors is clear in Fig. 2.  The value in the details plot is similar to the values obtained with the unsplit model but the final value is significantly lower. Fig. 3 shows the output when Split Mixer Tee.dsco is run on 1 processor.  The final values agree with the details plot. In Fig. 4 the values when the simulation in  Split Mixer Tee.dsco is run on 4 processors and a poly mesh is shown.  The final value is not identical to the details plot but it is more similar than that obtained with a tet mesh.  Poly meshes often match up better between bodies than tet meshes. Finally in Fig. 5 we see the output from the simulation in  SplitFace Mixer Tee.dsco where the face rather than the body has been split.  The values are the same.  This result could also point to a relationship to the mesh. Fig. 1:  No Split, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is the same as the final value Fig. 2:  Split body, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details monitor is different from final value Fig. 3:  Split body, tet mesh and 1 processor - last value of details plot is the same as the final value Fig. 4:  Split body, poly mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is similar to the final value Fig. 5:  Split Face, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is the same as the final value DiscoveryCromwell; Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Unable to select Location of Convection(Default) condition, making it difficult to make changes
Message: Unable to select Location of Convection(Default) condition, making it difficult to make changes In Structural-thermal or even CHT there is a Convection (Default) condition in the Tree. It is scoped to the remaining , un-scoped faces after the user defines structural/Fluid and thermal conditions.  If the user then wants to select the faces under this default condition, currently they cannot. The faces do get highlighted in the UI after picking the Condition from the Structure Tree. However, the selection cannot be preserved , neither by creating a Named Selection nor to another Load, constraint or even Mesh local refinement  This is a problem as not only does it make harder for user to use this selection for other objects like Fidelity Refinement, but it is also hard to change Convection to say HeatFlux or temp. Manual selection of all required faces may be necessary which may be error prone especially for models with large number of faces.   OTOH , this works well for the default 'Stationary Wall (Insulated)' for a Fluid-thermal simulation only. Meaning after RMB>Edit from the Tree, the scoped faces are highlighted. Then, the thermal condition can be flipped from insulated to anything else. Also, the NM panel is active enabling the user to save the locations. Attaching example *.dsco sessions :  \\tfsattach\TFSProd\Attachments\1289xxx\1289604 Structural:Therrmal ❌ CHT, Convection Default  ❌  (NOTE: Ignore the circled INACTIVE area on the HUD in this image) Fluid Thermal, stationary wall ✅

Title: JLT - Analysis step: crash when exporting the raw participants' answers for Pairwise Comparison project
Message: JLT - Analysis step: crash when exporting the raw participants' answers for Pairwise Comparison project DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : After fixing this bug: Bug 1301944: JLT - Pairwise Comparison: crash during conduction  I tried to analyze the test, and JLT crashed when exporting the "raw participants answers" Data: Pairwise Comparison-crash JLT analysis.zip Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Open the attached JLT analysis project with JLT (file: Pairwise Comparison Hargrove.jta) Go to File > Export Analysis data > Export raw participants answers Give a name to the file to save, then click Save button -> crash Expected behavior: Data is exported as expected, no crash CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): Same as the related bug. There is a confusion between sound ID and position of the sound in his storage vector. Solution : In  QString fac Export MatrixSoundsNotationsPC::GetFormatedData()  we must change the source code  from   ``` for (int l iSoundIdx = 0; l iSoundIdx < l nbSound; l iSoundIdx++) { // Get sound name auto l SoundName = m gene TestAnalysis->get m gene ValidatedTest()->get m gene TestSetup()->GetProcedure(PROCNUM)->GetSound(l iSoundIdx)->GetUserNameW(); l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l SoundName)); } ``` to ``` std::vector<int> l iSoundIDs = m gene TestAnalysis->GetSoundsIDsOrderedAlphabetical(false); for (int l iSoundIdx = 0; l iSoundIdx < l iSoundIDs.size(); l iSoundIdx++) { // Get sound name auto l SoundName = m gene TestAnalysis->get m gene ValidatedTest()->get m gene TestSetup()->GetProcedure(PROCNUM)->GetSound(l iSoundIDs[l iSoundIdx])->GetUserNameW(); l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l SoundName)); } ``` and from ``` // matrix for (int l iRow = 0; l iRow < l nbSound; l iRow++) { // Get sound name auto l SoundName = m gene TestAnalysis->get m gene ValidatedTest()->get m gene TestSetup()->GetProcedure(PROCNUM)->GetSound(l iRow)->GetUserNameW(); l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l SoundName)); for (int l iCol = 0; l iCol < l nbSound; l iCol++) { l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l notation(l iRow, l iCol))); } l FormatedText.append("\n"); } ``` to ``` // matrix for (int l iRow = 0; l iRow < l iSoundIDs.size(); l iRow++) { // Get sound name auto l SoundName = m gene TestAnalysis->get m gene ValidatedTest()->get m gene TestSetup()->GetProcedure(PROCNUM)->GetSound(l iSoundIDs[l iRow])->GetUserNameW(); l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l SoundName)); for (int l iCol = 0; l iCol < l nbSound; l iCol++) { l FormatedText.append(QString("%1;").arg(l notation(l iRow, l iCol))); } l FormatedText.append("\n"); } ``` Note that  l iSoundIDs is already defined above. Impacts : medium. QA Validation: Doc: Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: [Battery Wizard] FMU Problems in Model Exchange Mode
Message: [Battery Wizard] FMU Problems in Model Exchange Mode This phenomenon has been reproduced in R251 and R252. ■ Steps to Reproduce Open the attached AEDT file or the pre-installed example Cell model located at: C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v252\AnsysEM\Examples\Twin Builder\Applications\Battery Wizard In Project Manager , right-click Models > BatteryCell and select Export as FMU . Select Model Exchange as the Type. Note: The issue does not occur when using Co-Simulation . This may not fall within the scope of our product, but when loading into Simulink, an error occurs. When importing the current FMU into Simulink, the pin arrangement is the same as for a CS FMU. However, since the automatically generated terminals named N and P end up having identical names, it seems Simulink cannot handle them properly. While this may be a Simulink-related issue, I also believe it is not ideal that the FMU output from Twin Builder automatically generates two terminals both named N or P . It may be better to implement a mechanism in which automatically generated Conservative pins in the FMU are assigned distinct names—such as N in and N out —to avoid potential issues in other software as well. ↑Error message (English translation): The bus object 'N' of 'BatteryFMU test/FMU' does not exist. Please create the bus object manually in the base workspace or in the Simulink Data Dictionary, or use fmudialog.createBusType('BatteryFMU test/FMU') . Cause: The Simulink.DataType object 'N' is not in the scope of 'BatteryFMU test/FMU'. Component: Simulink | Category: Block error Best regards, Naoya Hashiguchi

Title: Prism: Inconsistent Mesh (and Results)
Message: Prism: Inconsistent Mesh (and Results) Out of 20 identical runs (through ARM), I got 18 identical passing results, then two (identical to each other) results that failed with about 1.4% error. Upon inspection of the two cases, the failed results showed a mesh that is approximately twice as large.  By inspecting model.stats and model.meshdesc, I found that vias were not affected. Each body had approximately twice as many elements in the failing cases compared to the passing ones. The earliest difference between both cases appears to be the b2ab file. Looking closer into that, the EDT debug hfss TxLinesMain... debug log shows that b2ab is initially identical in size between passing and failing runs. Then there appears to be some kind of refinement/healing process that causes a very modest increase in b2ab size for passing runs, but nearly doubles the size of the b2ab file for the runs that are failing.

Title: EnSight: Calculator: IntegralSurfaceEx accepts custom vector of nodal values
Message: EnSight: Calculator: IntegralSurfaceEx accepts custom vector of nodal values Nodal x,y,z values can currently be used as components of a custom vector and used in calculations with elemental values in the IntegralSurfaceEx function. This is not meant to be the case, as only elemental values should be possible. For example, this was done by creating a variable NodalVelocity, and creating NodalVelocity[X], NodalVelocity[Y], NodalVelocity[Z] variables. These variables can then be used as components in a custom vector. This was tested in the can combustor case, calculated over the full domain.

Title: Error about section numbers when using an Emag licence and conducting a magnetostatic analysis inside Workbench 2025 R2
Message: Error about section numbers when using an Emag licence and conducting a magnetostatic analysis inside Workbench 2025 R2 Dear Colleagues ( @Asifali Kotwal  ) The error we get is: The SECNUM command is either not available for this version of Ansys or the appropriate product was not selected for this session.     This happens because of the new ds.dat formatting as of 2025 R2. In the new format parts also have dedicated section numbers that are printed out in the ds.dat file. Title: NVH Toolkit: Nodes Filtering using EquidistantNodes/EquidistantSensorNodes criteria is not time-efficient
Message: NVH Toolkit: Nodes Filtering using EquidistantNodes/EquidistantSensorNodes criteria is not time-efficient The model to reproduce the issue is located here:  \\cdcw16rally02\TFSProd\Attachments\1321xxx\1321678 Use the script attached to reproduce the issue. It reproduces what is done behind the scenes in the add-on. For both "MAC Calculator" and "Pre-Test Calculator", whenever the "Minimum Distance Between Nodes" value is changed: the following steps are taken to extract the nodes using EquidistantNodes or EquidistantSensorNodes filtering criterion: STEP 1: Extract the nodes from region Ids in case where Faces are selected. In case where nodes are selected, we store the node ids. This step is taking around 1 second with the model attached where around 15 000 faces are selected. This is OK. STEP 2: The node ids from the previous step are used to create a Nodal Named Selection that will be selected as input in the next step. This step is taking more than 60 s which is not time efficient .  STEP 3: Create a Worksheet Named Selection where we add the Nodal Named Selection (created in the previous step) as input and set the filtering criterion. This step is taking 77 s which is not time efficient . STEP 4: Store the filtered node ids and delete both Named Selections. Could you provide a python API that does not require the creation of Named Selections? We pass in the following variables: list of node ids from STEP 1, filtering criterion ( EquidistantNodes or EquidistantSensorNodes), distance value and distance unit. The output will be the list of filtered node ids. Note that the attached script performs STEP 1 to STEP 3 and the created Named Selections are left in the tree (for investigation if needed). The time taken by each step is also captured.

Title: UI Responsiveness Bottlenecks in Large SATCOM Array Models (>10,500 Ports) with Link-to-Source Design in SBR+ Solution Type
Message: UI Responsiveness Bottlenecks in Large SATCOM Array Models (>10,500 Ports) with Link-to-Source Design in SBR+ Solution Type Customer case (Viasat). This model highlights UI responsiveness and workflow bottlenecks when simulating large Ka-band SATCOM arrays (>10,500 ports) using the HFSS SBR+ solution type with Link-to-Source Design. Key Details: Full model (~10,500 excitations): AEDT responsiveness becomes a critical limiting factor (long GUI wait times, frequent unresponsive states) observed in 25R2 and still present in 26R1 (09/03 build). Workarounds tested: Link-to-Source with “Link as Composite Port” option (proposed workaround): Consolidates ~2,048 Tx ports into one and ~8,450 Rx ports into one. Improves responsiveness but only partially addresses scalability and does not fully capture customer’s characterization goals. Link-to-Source without “Composite Port” option: GUI freezes when trying to assign excitations as Tx/Rx due to the large number of ports. Customer requests: Ability to compute only S(Rx,Tx) terms (exclude reciprocal S(Tx,Rx)) to reduce runtime and memory requirements. Usability enhancements to improve port assignment: • Enable “shift-select” functionality for bulk assignment of excitations (Rx/Tx, on/off). • Extend Rx/Tx selection capability to hybrid models using the IE solver or SBR+ when configured as Hybrid and Arrays solution types. Impact: Large-array workflows are critical for SATCOM/ISR-class systems. Issue is highly visible with strategic accounts (e.g., Viasat), with likely relevance to other customers working on similar problems. Addressing this would significantly improve usability and scalability for enterprise-level array design. Attachments: GUI responsiveness screenshots. Confidential customer model. Ideas & Recommendations: Implement a “Load from File” option (similar to Edit Excitations) to allow assigning Tx/Rx elements directly from a .txt or .csv file, enabling bulk updates without GUI bottlenecks. Title: [PR] Joule Heating with CHT: Problems with overlaps
Message: [PR] Joule Heating with CHT: Problems with overlaps -fJouleHeatingCHT This bug contains two examples of cases in which there are overlaps in simulations with overlaps. In the first faces are shared between contacts and a fluid-solid interface. In the second there is a boundary condition on a solid face of the fluid-solid interface of a CHT simulation with Joule Heating.   Overlapping contacts and fluid-solid interface In Refine, simulations with overlaps between the fluid-solid interface and contacts are treated differently when Joule Heating is included in a CHT simulation compared with when it is not.   This is illustrated by simulations in the attached project, Yazaki (confidential) 7342-9563-51-C22-A188 With Fluid Region ReducedGeom.2 SetUp1.dsco The project contains 3 simulations, of which only the first and third are of interest here CHT Only SID informational message that 37 faces are shared between the f-s interface and contacts in both stages Status in both stages in Not started, i.e. is valid Can be solved in both stages (Joule Heat Only) Joule Heat Add Fluid, which was created by duplicating the Joule Heat sim and then adding fluid conditions SID informational message that 46 faces are shared between the f-s interface and contacts in both stages Status in Not started in Explore and Cannot be solved in Refine It can be solved in Explore The overlaps in the simulations in "Yazaki (confidential) 7342-9563-51-C22-A188 With Fluid Region ReducedGeom.2 SetUp1" can be removed by reducing the max. detection distance for the contacts by 2 orders of magnitude and imprinting the touching faces of the two solid thermal bodies.  I have attached the modified simulations in: Yazaki (confidential) 7342-9563-51-C22-A188 With Fluid Region ReducedGeom.2 SetUp1 NoOverlaps.dsco. Once the overlaps have been removed, the simulation Joule Heating with CHT simulation can be solved in Refine Fails with an error in Explore the Example 1 LiveSolver log file, attached, contains messages that contact pairs have been removed. Boundary conditions on solid face of fluid-solid interface of CHT simulation with Joule Heating The attached project, Bar CHTJouleH 2Sims.dsco, contains two CHT with Joule Heating simulations. The SID is different if the overlapping condition is electrical rather than thermal.  Although the SID state with the electrical condition appears valid, it cannot be solved. Simulation 1 - Voltage 2 is located on the interface In Explore Voltage 2 is marked as Ignored in the tree and there is a SID message In Refine Voltage 2 is not marked in the tree and there is no SID message The SID state is Not started in both stages In both stages the solve fails   I have attached the Example 2 Live Solver and Artemis2 logs Simulation 2 - Insulated 4 is located on the interface (similar to bug 1328480 ) In Explore Insulated 4 is marked as Ignored in the tree The informational message appears in the SID There is also an error message about the overlap In Refine Insulated 4 is not marked in the tree The only SID message is error message about the overlap In both stages the SID is Cannot solve.

Title: Include googletest libraries in populate-runtime
Message: Include googletest libraries in populate-runtime There is a need to have Google Test as a separate project, which compiles into an executable.  Currently, Google Test libraries are shared libraries and reside under `3rdparty`. To run the executables, one needs to set `PATH` to point to `GOOGLETEST BINDIR`.  Recommend to include the libraries in `populate-runtime`, which avoids the need to set `PATH` by users.

Title: Scaling / Unit conversion issues while parameter units are changed and updated
Message: Scaling / Unit conversion issues while parameter units are changed and updated This is coming from a regression tests, the arm address for which is :  DM:WB2/WB2 PARAMETERS/WB2 PARA MNGMT 020 The test is erroring out since 24 Jan 2024 because of mesh failure and the mesh failures might be happening because of the unit conversion / scaling issue I am seeing.  Steps : Take a Mechanical Model system on project schematic page Browse to this model ( \ARM\ARM v242\Parts\DM145\PM 10 MICRON.agdb ) and Edit in DesignModeler. As soon as you open the model , parameters are promoted on schematic page and the bus is available Now go to schematic page and change the first parameter (Extrude..) to 0.15 mm and update the Geometry cell.  Go inside the DM and notice "Part 1" dimensions i.e. Volume (len, width, depth)

Title: Mesh Fusion producing poor meshes in AEDT Icepak 25R1
Message: Mesh Fusion producing poor meshes in AEDT Icepak 25R1 In 25R1 MF is meshing the attached models with no manual mesh regions created, but is either solving with a visibly poor mesh or is ignoring the objects in the model and not solving on all 3 levels of mesh fusion (3, 4 and 5). The attached spreadsheet was a thorough testing of all levels in 24R2 Classic and AEDT Icepak and 25R1 AEDT Icepak to show the trends. There is also a separate bug being corrected in 25R1 for the original model import so the model cannot be compared to the Classic meshing there. While the 1 by 1 model is running, the mesh is a basic bleeding mesh and only may be getting good results due to the dense mesh count created in the fluid in the bleeding (may have been lucky there) so please look into that mesh as well for region creation. Add To Regression; Mesh Fusion

Title: Discover History Tracking Script Error with different OS Region Settings
Message: Discover History Tracking Script Error with different OS Region Settings Hello, When one changes the Windows OS Region Format to one that the default decimal symbol is comma (",") the History Tracking for "Extract Volume" tool generates the following script: # Start Parameters self.Options = VolumeExtractOptions() #Validation Local, ScriptOptions, self.Options.SeedPoint = face3.EvalProportion(0,500008332455082, 0,500008452730343) #Validation Local, ScriptSeedPoint, self.Options.MergeCreatedVolume = False #Validation Local, ScriptMergeCreatedVolume, self.Options.ImprintCappingEdges = False #Validation Local, ScriptImprintCappingEdges, self.Options.CreateShareTopology = False #Validation Local, ScriptCreateShareTopology, self.Options.Tolerance = MM(0) #Validation Value, 4, -1.7976931348623157E+308, 1.7976931348623157E+308, True, , self.Selection = FaceSelection.Create(face1, face2) #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 14, -1, 0, ScriptSelection, , ScriptBodyFaceEdgeSelectionError self.SecondarySelection = face3 #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 12, -1, 0, ScriptSecondarySelection, , ScriptFaceSelectionError # End Parameters result = VolumeExtract.Create(self.Selection, self.SecondarySelection, self.Options) Normally with had to get this (We get this for English( United States) format) : # Start Parameters self.Options = VolumeExtractOptions() #Validation Local, ScriptOptions, self.Options.SeedPoint = face3.EvalProportion(0.500008332455082, 0.500008452730343) #Validation Local, ScriptSeedPoint, self.Options.MergeCreatedVolume = False #Validation Local, ScriptMergeCreatedVolume, self.Options.ImprintCappingEdges = False #Validation Local, ScriptImprintCappingEdges, self.Options.CreateShareTopology = False #Validation Local, ScriptCreateShareTopology, self.Options.Tolerance = MM(0) #Validation Value, 4, -1.7976931348623157E+308, 1.7976931348623157E+308, True, , self.Selection = FaceSelection.Create(face1, face2) #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 14, -1, 0, ScriptSelection, , ScriptBodyFaceEdgeSelectionError self.SecondarySelection = face3 #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 12, -1, 0, ScriptSecondarySelection, , ScriptFaceSelectionError # End Parameters result = VolumeExtract.Create(self.Selection, self.SecondarySelection, self.Options) The EvalPropotion arguments generated with comma separator and  the generated code fails. To reproduce the issue change the Region Format to Swedish (default decimal symbol=",", open Discovery, create a dummy body and run the Extract Volume tool with History Tracking Open.  Please review the attached video for the exact steps to reproduce the issue. Thanks in advance. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: iemit crash on save results after deleting system
Message: iemit crash on save results after deleting system In iemit create three default systems.  Run.  Delete the second system.  Save. Title: Assorted DLL errors for Fluent and MAPDL
Message: Assorted DLL errors for Fluent and MAPDL Hi team, Two of our channel partner testers are facing the issue while installing the 2025 R1. They are getting a message which says one of the .dll file is missing. I have shared couple of videos ( Instalation issue ), one is a recording of the AFT meeting where the user (sgierth@cadfem.de) showed the issue they are facing when opening the app after installation and the other one another user (acourage@4cad.fr) recorded the entire installation. Thanks, Bappa I got this message from Matt: Just looking at the file shared by the users, there could be conflicting QT files in the C:\Windows\System32 directory, but who knows. These are all new messages for new versions, we have no prior KMs related to these. Qt5Widgets is in many places, so where is it failing, we haven’t seen that message before.   We have seen a Qt5gui error which is similar, and the solution is to search for any files under C:\Windows folder and subfolders.  Move those files to a backup folder (say C:\Qt backup) or rename those files. Try to run.   For the Fluent error for mkl intel thread., this is definitely something developers need to address.  We have seen something similar with MAPDL regarding mkl intel , and that solution was to rename file to original in C:\Windows\System32. So, we can’t just start poking at files to see what file might be the fix, Fluent developers must take on this task directly. They will likely want more details on the issue, perhaps some more detailed logging. Since this is AFT there should be no problem getting developers involved to work directly with the end user to find the cause.   Ultimately, I doubt these are bugs in our code, but conflicts on the end customers’ systems, but only developers can truly tell us where that dll call is coming from and what might cause it to fail.   Thank you, Matt Thanks, Bappa

Title: AVX L&S - Standalone Volvo wheel radius is wrong
Message: AVX L&S - Standalone Volvo wheel radius is wrong DESCRIPTION: The wheel radius for the Volvo in Standalone mode is wrong. It is set at 0.38, whereas it should be at 0.369. Data : This bug concerns Volvo standalone data available in C:\ProgramData\OPTIS\Program\Library\Cars\Volvo Car Option. The bug exists probably since the data were created. Notes : In VRX, the front axle height is computed from the wheel radius. The LightingSystem node is placed with respect to the middle of the   front axle, at radius level. The difference between the current radius level and the expected one (1.1cm) may impact Illuminance Sensors values. Notes for devs: In .cab/.act/.wheel files in  C:\ProgramData\OPTIS\Program\Library\Cars\Volvo Car Option wheel radius for Volvo is 0.38. Additionally: there are several .cob .act for the Volvo in this folder, and at this time it is not clear whether they are all used (some of them can be here for backward compatibility). Note that .cob file path is referenced in .vrxproj file, so removing a .cob file may break existing project. the way the wheel radius is defined in these files is sometimes relative, sometimes absolute in these various files In VRX code, there are plenty of '0.38' hard coded values duplicated. The Volvo Car defined for Cosim mode has a correct wheel radius (C:\ProgramData\OPTIS\Program\Library\CoSimulation Library\Assets\Dynamic). Steps to reproduce: Open a standalone project with default parameters. Select Car Tab and open car properties => The wheel radius is 0.38 Expected behavior: The wheel radius should be 0.369. Title: Continuous skew factor not correctly addressed in Mech NVH analysis
Message: Continuous skew factor not correctly addressed in Mech NVH analysis I ran an E-NVH analysis in Mech using the e9 template and noticed that the calculated torque was well below the requested torque, for all calculated operating points. This has to do with the stator continuous skew method and factor, as demonstrated below. Procedure Open the e9 template or the attached model with Motor-CAD v2025.1.0.9. The Harmonic and Rotor flux method is enabled BUT with the Flux Skew Factor set to 1 I am assuming in that demonstration that this amounts to using the original Harmonics method. Lab models are then built.  A warning specifies that a Flux skew stator of 1 will be used as the Rotor flux and Harmonics method is not supported by Lab. The NVH analysis is run for contant torque operation as shown below: When going back to EMag the Skew factor has been updated, although the option was disabled We end up with Calculated torque values being much lower than Requested torque values, although the opposite behaviour should be expected considering Lab and EMag torques are, as of today, still of different nature (mechanical and electromagnetic resp.) After swithing to the Harmonics method and rerunning the NVH analysis, results are as expected: The skew factor has also been reset to 1.
