Title: Success of phase change of water on replay of script depends on steps used to set up materials in CHT simulation
Message: Success of phase change of water on replay of script depends on steps used to set up materials in CHT simulation A script is recorded for the set up of a CHT simulation with 2 flow paths, one containing water and the other air.  The simulation is solved in Refine and then the state of the water is changed from liquid to gas.  The behaviour of the simulation on replay of the script depends on the steps involved in the set-up of the physics. - the work flow involves an extra step of setting both paths from water to air and then one of the paths is assigned water again the change of state is not successful on replay of the script.  Instead the HUD for water includes options for liquid, gas and solid (Fig. 1 -  the workflow is simpler in that one of the fluid paths is set from water to air the change of state is successful on replay of the script and the HUD for water contains on liquid and gas The solve in Refine does not appear to be necessary in this case. I have attached the 2 scripts and the project that they open. On further investigation I'm not convinced that the failure is entirely down to the sequence of steps.  I have seen a given script sometimes fail and sometimes not.   For example, the script NoFan NoSolve , which is a modification of , has produced both state change to gas and only 2 states in the HUD - 2States 20250106.1840.3856.7z state not changed from liquid and 3 states in the HUD - 3States 20250106.1846.2072.7z Fig. 1:  - state of water does not change from liquid to gas and HUD includes 3 states Fig. 2:  - state of water has changed to gas and HUD shows only 2 states

Title: Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing project resulting in unexpected CAD quality differences.
Message: Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing project resulting in unexpected CAD quality differences. Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing DSCO project.  There is a distinct quality difference between the plugin and the reader.  The user in this case always needs the plugin to be used, and not automatically default to the Stride READER.  Any of the CAD plugins (Creo or NX etc) may be used to confirm this issue.  Let's use Creo as our example  Open Creo and let it idle.  Open a new Discovery  In Discovery, File > Open > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt   Observe Creo, and observe that base s.prt is active, and the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates plugin was used)  In Discovery, File > Insert > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt     Observe Creo, and observe that sh cap.prt is now active, and the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates plugin was used) File > Save the Discovery model, Test.dsco Exit Discovery Exit Creo  Open Creo and let it idle.  Open Discovery and resume Test.dsco  In Discovery, File > Insert > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt   Observe Creo, and observe that no parts are active, the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates Stride READER was used) The Discovery log file proves this: Checking CCM for C:\Test\sh cap.prt Stride Convert Start : 8:11 AM Stride Convert Completed : 8:11 AM It seems as if when Discovery is resumed, the "Checking for APM" FAILS to detect that CAD is running, and instead defaults to the Stride reader. Further, I believe the geometry Open / Insert should FAIL if the plugin cannot be activated, and not automatically fall back to the reader (Due to the CAD quality issues mentioned above)

Title: factorization time in parallel (e.g. -th 8) increases with iteration number
Message: factorization time in parallel (e.g. -th 8) increases with iteration number simple transient case defined on the Pellizzari mesh (thin and long domain), with free surface.  The setup is simple: thin filament with a high viscosity, under gravity, with heat exchange; free surface and surface tension.  The motivation is having a large model with a minimum amount of non-linearities.   Files are available in \\CDCW16RALLY02\TFSProd\Attachments\1242xxx\1242505  . When running with AMF and -th 8, the factorization time increases with the iteration number: it starts at about 50, and is already larger than 250 s after about 20 iterations.  The calculation time for the matrix construction is about constant, around 230 s. When running with 1 proc for the factorization, the data suggest a slight increase (possible affected by the occurrence of another competing job). When running with MUMPS, the elapsed time for factorization is about constant and around 40 s. Files for the simulation are attached, as well as the raw data for the graph shown hereafter. The first part of the first curve here above can probably be discarded (excess probably due to another competing job).  Combining both first and second curves provide a more realistic picture, I presume. Found with 25R2, but might already exist before...

Title: [AMI] AMI erroring out during post-processing
Message: [AMI] AMI erroring out during post-processing [Update June 11 2025]: Materialise provided a log with our version with additional logging. See the attached . If we can't reproduce, let's see if we can come up with suggestions of things to try based on the new error message. Materialise are running into errors with what appears to be all simulation types on some specific machines. Attached are input files and logs    from one example   (file* from MAPDL run have been deleted before sharing to save space). Below are some additional details It was originally only erroring on calibration simulations but now happening for thermal and inherent strain as well One person was having the issue, but after clearing program data it is running okay again Erroring during post processing step - it's creating the hdf results folder but isn't adding any contents Issue began happening with the switch to 251 (ran okay in 4.1.0.8 Magics version, fails with 4.1.1.1) See more comments from Materialise below Feedback from Materialise investigation: Daniela Betzl commented 3. Apr. (edited) : I've done more tests with different Sim 4.1 versions with cleaning up the Program Data folder (deleting Materialise/SimulationPlugin subfolder) before each installation. I've tested 4.1.0.8 (with AMI v242 from June 24), 4.1.0.27 (with AMI v251 from Nov 24) and 4.1.1.1 (with AMI v251 from Feb 25).    The calibration run successfully for 4.1.0.8 and 4.1.1.1. For 4.1.0.27 the calibration failed, but because of the comma bug as my computer language is currently set to German (see  Bug 1257389 : Thermal simulation failing due to comma used as Windows decimal separator setting).   To double check I also tested the upgrade scenario:  Deleted the SimulationPlugin folder in Program Data/Materialise and installed 4.0.1.1 first. Ran calibration successfully. Then installed, without deleting the SimulationPlugin folder, 4.1.1.1 and ran calibration again, with success. And then installed 5.0.0.17, restarted the computer (due changed environment variable) and ran the calibration. Also for this version it was successful.   It seems that some of the files in the Program Data (probably the calibration profiles) may got corrupted during (re-)installation and causes this issue? But it's still unclear if this is really the case. But deleting the program data folder manually before an installation helps.   I've also run the calibration separately via command line with a successful calibration. The same error occurs like before, so I guess this is not related to the issue. Andrii Nekrashevych commented 4. Apr. @Daniela Betzl   @ Jan-Patrick   Juergens I tried to investigate the problem on my PC   Downgrade: From 5.0.0.17 to 4.1.1.1.  with  cleaning up the Program Data folder and computer restart -  Job failed From  4.1.1.1.   to 4.1.0.27.  with  cleaning up the Program Data folder -  Job failed From  4.1.0.27. to 4.1.0.8  with  cleaning up the Program Data folder 4.1.0.8 -  Job passed Upgrade: From  4.1.0.8 to 4.1.1.1.  without  cleaning up the Program Data folder -  Job failed Installation on a clean PC  (without previously existing Program Data folder): 4.1.1.1.  Job failed My investigation shows that it isn't related to the Program Data folder. It looks like after ver 4.1.0.8, after the AMI update, something went wrong.   Also, on a clean PC all folders related to Simulation were not present before.  Daniela Betzl commented 7. Apr. : Update: I have also checked the behaviour on VMs with 4.0.1.1 and 4.1.1.1. The calibrations were successful, too. But as Andrii has used Sim 4.0.0.589, I've tested the upgrade scenario 4.0.0.589 -> 4.1.1.1 ,too. In this scenario, the calibration has failed in 4.1.1.1 for the same step as in his case. I assume it's probably because of the duplicated calibration profiles in ProgramData subfolder: The profiles were renamed with 4.0.1.1. So I deleted SimulationPlugin folder in ProgramData and reinstalled 4.1.1.1. After that, the calibration was successful again. It's strange that this workaround doesn't work for Andriis situation. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Temperature output result is not correct with 2D General Axis symmetric analysis in Ansys Mechanical.
Message: Temperature output result is not correct with 2D General Axis symmetric analysis in Ansys Mechanical. 2D general axisymmetric elements with user-defined material field variables break the temperature output when reviewing results. Other results, such as stress and displacement, are not impacted. I mentioned some conversation of the user below, which will help you to understand the problem clearly.  The nodes isolated by the ID should have a magnitude of 3000F, with the rest of the body having a uniform temperature of 100F. The temperature gradient is applied via the command snippet lines 9:15. Thermal conditions 1:3 apply the uniform temperature of 100°F.   This issue also exists in APDL, so ANSYS is incorrectly pulling values from the RST value for temperature results of a 2DGA element with user-defined field variables in the materials deck. Another way to isolate this issue is to simply swap materials used for all components to be structural steel. Upon using a more traditional material deck, the BFE temperature output to the 2DGA elements behaves as expected.   The material deck was purposefully adjusted so that low radius + high temperature should be stiff, low radius + low temperature should be soft, and large radius + high/low temperature should be stiff. The expected dimple on the right hand side of the block is the expected deformation outcome due to the compressive axial pressure applied to the cylinders. As a resultant, it is my current conclusion that the 2DGA element with this material deck is doing everything correctly, and it is simply the temperature output that is broken. I have attached the model with a video recording in which I explained everything. Please let me know if this help.

Title: Missing Documentation of Stacking Factor's Influence on Iron Losses
Message: Missing Documentation of Stacking Factor's Influence on Iron Losses Hello. This is a documentation bug. The default (and reccomended) method to consider the stacking factor of electric steel laminations for the FEA analysis is the saturation method. Using this method, the BH curve of the materials assigned to the core is manipulated. This is done in the background and is well documented in the help. However, in addition to triggering a correction of the BH-curve used, activating the Stacking Factor (saturation) model also triggers a correction of the iron loss coefficients of the material. After double-checking with @Mircea Popescu , it seems that the corrected iron loss coefficients when a stacking factor kst is defined are calculated as: For Bertotti Model (Classical and Maxwell):     Keddy eq = Keddy iron/(kst)  and  Kexc eq = Kexc iron/sqrt(kst) For Bertotti Model (Classical):    Kh eq = Kh iron/(kst^(alpha-1)) For Bertotti Model (Maxwell):    Kh eq = Kh iron/(kst^(alpha-1)) =    Kh eq = Kh iron/(kst^(2-1)) =    Kh eq = Kh iron/(kst) I suppose hat for the Steinmetz iron loss model the correction for the eddy current component would be analogous : Keddy eq = Keddy iron/(kst) I am not sure about the  hysteresis component. Could you please double-check the code, identify the correction applied and update the manual? I think that a good place to put this information would be at the end of this section and add a link to this page in the section above, where the stacking factor model is explained. Something in the lines of "When Stacking Factor (saturation) model is active, the iron loss coefficients are corrected to account for the stacking factor of the core as described in ...."   Thanks in advance and best regards, Daniel @Nicolas Riviere

Title: Missing documentation for Radial Ducts Length Calculation methods
Message: Missing documentation for Radial Ducts Length Calculation methods This issue originates from the SR 00128723 and ER ELE-I-2160, and was already discussed with @Mircea Popescu and @Daniel Bachinski . When modelling radial ducts for the rotor and or the stator, different methods are available for addressing the geometric and magnetic machine length calculations, as shown below on the Default Settings page (note that the highlighted settings will only appear if you enabled upfront the Radial Ducts from the Geometry page). It would be suitable to add in the Help Manual a brief description of the methods (Original and Improved) for the settings highlithed below. Magnetically, it seems that the radial ducts can be treated like insulation between laminations, by calculating either an equivalent axial length or stacking factor. The manual should clearly explain how the radial ducts and insulation material effects combine to calculate magnetic properties of the steel. This will ultimately help to understand how material parameters should be adjusted in Maxwell to align with Motor-CAD modelling formulation. Thanks!

Title: Explore deformation at lower values differs
Message: Explore deformation at lower values differs I have a customer case, where the deformation values on the lower end of the legend differ a lot in Explore stage.  In the above example, the higher end values (red in color), closely match with Refine, Mechanical as well as Optistruct (the application customer uses, and wants to compare the results with). Where as the values on the lower end (Blue in color) on the same location differ a lot. These values are small in value, and the difference does not seem like a lot, but in percentage it in order of 50+%. Is this due to the size preview being bigger than the deformation? On the bug discussion, here are the few additional points that came up. 1.  At what resolution are you testing? What GPU is being used? Ans:  I am running it at the highest fidelity (100%, standard) on a 16GB VRAM. During the run, it was reaching 12-14GB of VRAM usage. The size preview is at 0.2mm. (The user likely has a smaller GPU). The higher value is within a 5% error margin, and the behavior matches well, but the user also checks the lower values on the pot side of the caliper, which is part of their practice. Therefore, it’s important for them to see that match as well for them to adopt Discovery. 2. Observation by Matthew:  I'm concerned that the simulations they are comparing between Discovery, Mechanical, and Optistruct are not the same.  The deformation shape is different.  If you look at the "ribs" on top of the device, they have minimal deformation in Mechanical but medium deformation in Discovery.  I think there is some disagreement in loads/boundary conditions. Ans: T he Refine and Mechanical ones are transferred from the same Explore run. I do not think there could be any difference in the boundary conditions as such. 3. As per Rabii:  I think this is a bug about pressure condition. results are fidelity dependent: with a voxel size= 0.49mm discplacement is wrong. Do let me know if any more information is needed. We have also tried using Force (using the area where we are applying the load, and the pressure value), those results also differ significantly, and do not match well with Optistruct.

Title: When Real & Imaginary is selected for AC source, the Real part = 0 should not be allowed
Message: When Real & Imaginary is selected for AC source, the Real part = 0 should not be allowed For voltage and current sources when user chooses the AC values as real  & imaginary radio button as follows Zero value should not be allowed. Because in the netlist when it converts to AC PHASE it creates a division by zero as follows: INTERN E E1 N1:= GND , N2:= net 1 (EMF:= 1, PARTDERIV:= 1, SPC:=0, AC PHASE := ATAN((3)/ (0) )*(180/PI), AC MAG := SQRT((0)^2+(3)^2));

Title: Disco collab: comments are not cleared if a simulation is deleted
Message: Disco collab: comments are not cleared if a simulation is deleted Issue: If a simulation is deleted, comments added on that simulation are not cleared from the comments panel. Similarly, the section that says 'All simulations' still includes the deleted simulation. That should also be cleared.  To repro, Save a new file to the cloud Create a simulation and duplicate it Add a comment in the physics tree in the duplicate simulation Delete the duplicate simulation Open the comments panel, and you will still see the deleted comment. Expand the section that says simulation, and you will still see the duplicate simulation name.  This has to be cleared instantly.  If I reopen this file, I see the comment from the  duplicate simulation deleted You can find the comments section panel here

Title: Why INITIALIZE_RIGID_BODIES() (and subsequently, TSTEP3) is called when only an elastic Lagrange part is used in the model?
Message: Why INITIALIZE RIGID BODIES() (and subsequently, TSTEP3) is called when only an elastic Lagrange part is used in the model? When running for an elastic Lagrange part using the reduced integration HEX solver the initialization for time step follows the routines: GET SOUNDSPEED TSTEP3 but later in initialization, TSTEP3 is called again from INITIALIZE RIGID BODIES routine. This is something needs to be investigated: Why INITIALIZE RIGID BODIES is called when only an elastic part is used in the simulation..?  Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Long automation alert box while opening an old version file or large project file with ongoing update

Title: LM_PROJECT and IDLE - Heartbeats after CLIENT_ACTIVE call do not have LM_PROJECT value set on Windows
Message: LM PROJECT and IDLE - Heartbeats after CLIENT ACTIVE call do not have LM PROJECT value set on Windows ARM test idle-003 shows this issue on Windows.  This test does the following: Sets idle timeout in the FNP options file.  Sets: "INCLUDEALL PROJECT test project" in the options file. Checks out licenses with the LM PROJECT=test project value set. Makes and idle call and let the licenses go idle.  Makes an active call to check back out the licenses. At this point is where the defect occurs... After the active call, ACL starts back up the FNP heartbeats for the license feature that went idle but it does not pass the LM PROJECT value "test project". Because of this the heartbeats fail to reacquire the license, and the client go into LOST mode. In LOST mode the first RECHECKOUT attempt does pass the LM PORJECT value so it able to checkout.  The issue as stated above is the heartbeats cannot reacquire   the license correctly because it is missing the LM PROJECT value when going to FNP.  ThirdParty

Title: UI does not show a correct band plot when modifying a radio with scripting
Message: UI does not show a correct band plot when modifying a radio with scripting I testing this on the EDT v26.1 certified build with EM Installer dated on 08/28/2025, UI does not show a correct band plot when modifying a radio with scripting. This defect occurs only when doing it through scripting ( Scripting Only ). No issue with performing manually.  Here is the plot between scripting and non-scripting * From scripting, if I manually disable/enable Harmonics, it will show a correct plot. To reproduce this defect ( Scripting ): Launch EDT, add EMIT design Select Tools > Open Command Window Type these command: oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject() oDesign = oProject.GetActiveDesign() oModule = oDesign.GetModule("EmitCom") oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("SchematicEditor") radio id = oModule.CreateEmitComponent("Radio", "New Radio", "Radios") oEditor.ZoomToFit() band id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, radio id, "Band") rx spetral id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, band id, 'Rx Spectral Profile') oModule.SetEmitNodeProperties(0, rx spetral id, ['Enabled=false']) tx spetral id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, band id, 'Tx Spectral Profile') harm id = oModule.CreateEmitNode(0, tx spetral id, 'Harmonics', 'Custom Tx Harmonics') oModule.SetEmitNodeProperties(0, harm id, ['Harmonic Table Units=Relative']) harm table = '2;-50' oModule.SetTableData(0, harm id, harm table) oProject.Save() Open a Radio configuration.  Select a Band node. You will get a result shown above. These are steps to do manually on the EDT: Launch EDT and add EMIT design Add a radio in the schematic window. Open a radio configuration Expand a Band node and disable " Rx Spectral Profile " Right click on " Tx Spectral Profile " and select "Add  Custom Tx Harmonics" Change " Harmonic Table Units " to  Relative Select Add  Row and insert these value Select Band node again to see a Band plot.  Scripting

Title: SAS - [regression] Changing number of microphones after loading signals removes all loaded signals from Sound Power Level module
Message: SAS - [regression] Changing number of microphones after loading signals removes all loaded signals from Sound Power Level module DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : SAS - [regression] Changing number of microphones after loading signals removes all loaded signals from Sound Power Level module Data: Reproducible:   always Steps to reproduce: In the Sound Power module select the option "Load signals one by one". Default number of microphone is 20, don't change it yet. Start selecting signals one by one in the list, load some signal. Change the Number of microphones from 20 to other number. The signal list becomes blank, all loaded signals are removed. -->   BUG User has to load all signals again. Similar bug Bug 1120841: SAS - Sound Power Level: changing number of microphones after loading signals removes all loaded signals   was filed in 2025 R1. Expected behavior: Loaded signals should not be removed after changing the number.   CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause   (if regression include [regression] in the title):  Solution :  Impacts : QA Validation: Doc: 9/9/2025 8:35 AM Bug filed on "BAT - SAS - Sound Power Level module" Comments: SAS Build: 2026.1.0.4201 Step no. Result Title 1. Passed Prerequisite: Sound Pro License. Attached sound files. 2. Passed Objective: Test the Sound Power Level module 3. Passed Start a new session of SAS. Go Modules --> Sound Power Level Expected Result Interface for the new module is opened without any error. This has three main sections. • Microphone positions • Calculation parameters • Results 4. Passed Verify that the first section has following options. Expected Result All options are present and translated in English. • Dropdown to select Hemisphere/Half-hemisphere • Checkbox to Display/Hide schematic • Radius number • Load all signals • Select signals one by one 5. Passed Select the checkbox to Display/Hide schematic. Expected Result Schematic for Hemisphere should be displayed which is the default choice. 6. Passed Change to Half-hemisphere from the dropdown. Expected Result The schematic display should change to Half-hemisphere from Hemisphere. 7. Passed Change the Radius from 1 m to any other non-integer. Expected Result The display should not change as it shows generic schematic with “r”. 8. Passed Switch back to Hemisphere. Then uncheck the Display/Hide schematic. Expected Result Schematic should back to Hemisphere and radius value should remain same. After unchecking, schematic should be hidden. 9. Passed Default choice for signal selection is “Load all signals”. Select the checkbox for “Load signals one by one”. Expected Result Option to define number of signals for analysis, and option to select signals in the list should open up. 10. Passed Switch back to “Load all signals”. Load all the wav files attached. Expected Result All signals loaded without any error. 11. Passed Focusing on next section “Calculation Parameters”. It has two areas one for Background and Room noise correction and second for Environmental corrections. Expected Result Verify that Background and room noise section has following properties. • K1- Background noise correction • K2- Room noise correction • Checkbox to enable room dimension • Mean Sound Absorption coefficient • Room dimension values: Length, Breadth, Depth 12. Passed Similarly verify the other subsection for environment corrections. Expected Result Following properties should be available • C1- Environmental correction • C2- Environment correction • Checkbox to enable Environmental conditions • Temperature • Atmospheric pressure 13. Passed Change Radius to 1.2 m, K1 and K2 to 2 dB and 3dB respectively. Similarly change C1 and C2 4dB and 5 dB. Expected Result All signals loaded and all properties defined now. 14. Passed Click on “Compute”. An info message is displayed first “Calculation in progress”. Expected Result Once finished, “Calculation complete” should be displayed. Sound Power Level corresponding to Octave band and third octave band should be displayed. 15. Passed Click on export plots for Octave and Third Octave bands for sound power level. Expected Result Both Octave and Third octave plots are displayed. Verify the values are comparable in both plots. 16. Passed Add cursors in both the windows. Expected Result Verify the cursor shows correct values as per the selected frequency/band. 17. Passed Click on “Export Curves” and select the location to save the file. Expected Result Open and verify that the file has all the parameters like Radius, Number of Microphones, K1, K2, C1, C2, Mean Sound Absorption coefficient, Temperature, Static Pressure and octave/third octave frequency and dB values. 18. Passed Go to Microphone positions section and select the “Load signals one by one” radio button. Expected Result Option to edit number of signals and list to select the signals should be opened. 19. Failed Select the attached signals one by one. Then change the number of signals to 9. Expected Result All signals are loaded one by one. Loaded signals are not removed after changing the number of microphones. 20. None Select the Room Dimensions checkbox. Expected Result K2 value should be read only and automatically set to 8.4707 dB due to Radius value set in step#13. Mean Sound Absorption Coefficient and Room Depth/Height/Width fields should be enabled; their default values are set to 1. 21. None Change Mean Sound Absorption Coefficient 3.5 & Room Height/Width/ Depth to 1.5/2.3/1.4 m respectively. Radius is already set to 1.2 m in step#13 above Expected Result After changing the Room dimensions, K2 should change to 2.0126 dB. 22. None Now select the check box for “Weather conditions” checkbox. Expected Result Temperature and Static Pressure becomes editable having value 23 degree and 101.325 kPa. C1 and C2 should become read only having values -0.127 dB and 0.0033 dB. 23. None Change the Temperature and Pressure values to see changes in C1 and C2. Finally set Temperature to 25 degree C and pressure to its default value 101.325 kPa. Expected Result C1 should be set to -0.112474 dB and C2 to 0.04714 dB. 24. None We have changed all the parameters from previous calculation. Expected Result Due to changed parameters, verify that an asterisk is displayed in the title of Sound Power module and the info message in Results section is changed to “Calculation done(Parameters have changed)”. 25. None Click on compute. Once the calculation is complete export the csv file. Expected Result Open the csv file and verify that all parameters set in Sound Power module are in sync with exported values in csv file. 26. None Save the project file *.spw with any name. Click on new in the Sound Power module. Expected Result Project file saved at desired location. After clicking new, all the settings and loaded files in module should be reset. 27. None Open the saved project again. Expected Result Project opened without any error. All settings and signals maintained. Octave, third octave curves exported without any error. 28. None Switch from Hemisphere to half-hemisphere. Expected Result All other settings are maintained as before. 29. None Compute the sound power and save the project. Expected Result Sound Power level is computed, and project saved at desired location. 30. None Close the Sound Power module and open again. Resume the saved project. Expected Result Project resumed without any error. Test Configuration: All Applicable Platforms

Title: Rotor Back Iron heat dissipation not displayed in the output tab
Message: Rotor Back Iron heat dissipation not displayed in the output tab A mismatch between Dissipation TVent Total and sum of individual table values has been identified.   This discrepancy comes from a postprocessing bug.  The Rotor Back Iron to Through Ventilated Fluid heat dissipation is not listed in the table. However, it is being included in the total summation. That is why the Dissipation TVent Total is a little bit higher. This migth be worked out by summing the powers shown in the Schematic manually. By doing so, it has been noticed that these values are missing from the table. The screenshot below shows two of the three resistances. If the Rotor Back Iron to Through Ventilated Fluid heat dissipation  values from the schematic are added to the v alues in the Dissipation table, it equals the Dissipation TVent Total.

Title: Discovery custom beam profiles get transferred to Mechanical as new ones upon dimension change
Message: Discovery custom beam profiles get transferred to Mechanical as new ones upon dimension change In 2025R2 Discovery, some custom beam sections are created of type Disk. These sections are then transferred to the downstream Mechanical system accordingly. Assume a change is made to a dimension of the cross section in Discovery. The properties of the cross section are changed accordingly in Discovery (used to be a bug in 2025R1). Now, when updating the geometry in Mechanical, the cross section is imported as a new one and re-assigned as the active cross section of the line body. This behavior theoretically works fine, but practically adds to the data that Mechanical has. What is many changes are made to the Discovery geometry for testing - we would then have an accumulation of beam profiles in Mechanical for no reason, as they wouldn't be used. I would expect that the beam profile definition gets overwritten in Mechanical - same as it happens in Discovery (no addition of new profiles upon dimension change).

Title: Generic Connector: CLI Crashes on Invalid or Incomplete Option Usage Instead of Providing User-Friendly Errors
Message: Generic Connector: CLI Crashes on Invalid or Incomplete Option Usage Instead of Providing User-Friendly Errors 🔁 Reproducible Scenarios ❌ Scenario 1: Invalid --auth:mode value %ANS MINERVA CLI% --auth:mode --help Result: System.InvalidOperationException: Failed to convert configuration value at 'auth:mode' to type ... ---> System.ArgumentException: Requested value '--help' was not found. ❌ Scenario 2: --interactive used without a value %ANS MINERVA CLI% --help --interactive Result: System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.    at Ansys.Minerva.IntegrationFramework.Common.Utility.FindInteractiveMode(String[] args, ...) ❗ Expected Behavior The CLI should not crash or throw raw exceptions. It should detect invalid or missing values and return a clear, user-friendly error , such as: Error: Missing value for --interactive. Valid values are: None, Console, Graphical. or Error: '--help' is not a valid value for --auth:mode. Valid values are: Explicit, Impersonate, Refresh Token, Windows, Browser. Ideally, it should also suggest: Use '%ANS MINERVA CLI% help ' for more information. ✅ Suggested Fixes Add input validation for all CLI options. Catch and handle exceptions like ArgumentException, IndexOutOfRangeException, and InvalidOperationException. Provide fallback help messages when invalid input is detected. Consider implementing a generic help parser that can intercept malformed input and redirect to appropriate help content. 📎 Additional Notes The CLI currently handles unknown verbs gracefully (e.g., Verb '--path' is not recognized.), which is a good pattern. This behavior should be extended to invalid option values as well.

Title: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh volume fails for larger global size factor
Message: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh volume fails for larger global size factor For the GE Vernova turbine blade , hybrid meshing fails for the hub after setting the global size factor to 2: Volume meshing failed. The shroud hybrid mesh was successful. See attached state file and Prime files. For the pmdb see the linked defect. Note that the overall meshing time is more than two hours.

Title: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh has significant mismatch in boundary layer elements
Message: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh has significant mismatch in boundary layer elements For the GE Vernova turbine blade , hybrid meshing on the shroud end shows significant mismatch between the hex mesh and the unstructured mesh where the boundary layer expansion in the hex mesh is large due to the blade concave curvature (common for turbine blades). This causes extreme stretching of the mesh elements and low mesh quality. Other than reducing the number of inflation layers in the unstructured zone, I see no other workaround. This is most likely an enhancement request, but I'm recording it here for now. See linked bug for files.

Title: PyModelCenter: Cannot create a DOETool component programmatically
Message: PyModelCenter: Cannot create a DOETool component programmatically Unable to create and configure a DOE Tool component from pyModelCenter. See the following teams message for more information: I'm having issues actually making an example script setting up a DOE though. Is there some trick to setting one up programmatically, or even from the GUI? If you drag/drop a DOE component straight into ModelCenter, it comes in with no variables, so I can't really set anything. It seems like you have to add some design variables through the DOE GUI before it works. Maybe it's just an issue with the DOE Tool component plug-in. I think it should probably do what the OptTool does. I'm using an example script that creates an Optimization. Or maybe it isn't allowed. I see some other plug-ins doing the same thing, like the RSMToolkit or Excel. Steps to Reproduce: Download the attached python script Change the path to the DOE component to point to the path on your local devbox You can uncomment the code or just run through to see the issue. I don't know if the commented-out code actually works. I made it based off of an example in pyModelCenter, so I suspect it should be close. Either way, after running this you should see a new model with two components. One will be the DOE with nothing available. Trying to interact with it, such as setting the algorithm, will fail.

Title: DPM-Blocking + Ideal Gas violating conservation of energy
Message: DPM-Blocking + Ideal Gas violating conservation of energy I am testing this case in which a particle at 90 deg C is placed inside an air container with all walls and initial temperature equal to 90 deg C. The container has one opening with 0 (gauge) pressure.  The expected behavior is to observe a constant temperature throughout the simulation. However, this is what is happening: Rocky 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + Porous Media formulation Rocky 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking: The fluid temperature increases indefinitely, causing the particle temperature to increase. Rocky 25.2.0 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking: Same as 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking Rocky 25.2.0 + Incompressible Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking:  Behaves as expected.  Rocky 25.2.0 + Ideal Gas + Eulerian Multiphase:   Works In summary: Ideal gas + Porous media ✅ Ideal gas + DPM Blocking ❌ Ideal Gas + Eulerian Multiphase   ✅ Incompressible Ideal Gas + Porous Media ✅ Incompressible Ideal Gas + DPM Blocking ✅ The project files are attached. Title: Fluent users should have the flexibility to retain their chosen working directory throughout the session.
Message: Fluent users should have the flexibility to retain their chosen working directory throughout the session. We are in the process of organizing our V&V tests using a structured folder setup for CFD simulation types. Our goal is to provide customers with ready-to-run test cases, where they can simply execute the provided journal files without needing to modify the setup. Please find attached a sample test case for your reference. The folder structure is organized as follows: Pre-Processing: Contains all input files Solve: Stores case and data files Post-Processing: Stores output files Reports: Stores generated reports However, we’ve encountered an issue: Fluent does not retain the working directory specified by the user in the Fluent launcher. Steps to Reproduce: Download the attached sample test. Launch Fluent. In the Fluent launcher, set sample test as the working directory. Select Meshing mode and PyConsole (Beta). Run Run1 Meshing from the Pre-Processing folder. Expected behavior: Fluent should maintain sample test as the working directory. Observed behavior: Fluent changes the working directory to Pre-Processing. This behavior disrupts the intended automation flow and may confuse users. We believe users should have the flexibility to retain their chosen working directory throughout the session. Could you please look into this issue?

Message: Optimization - Selected measures are lost after updating the simulation DESCRIPTION: Data : \\tfsattach\TFSProd\Attachments\1280xxx\1280401 Notes : [TVK] Since the  Commit cdfd6a92 : Merged PR 567569: Integration of automation APIs for Canon ## Integration of automation APIs for Canon. What's more annoying is that if you select n number of bodies and convert to solid, if 1 body fails the whole selection fails.  I've attached a smaller example Muscle Data Convert2Solid Prob2.dsco with just a few bodies.  If you select all the bodies and RMB->Convert to Solid you'll notice it takes some time and then everything fails to convert due to the one problematic body.  I would think it should convert the bodies it can and just skip the bodies that fail.  For the real model which has 100s of bodies this makes it a bit tricky to convert all the bodies... Title: Preserve variable separator rows when importing/exporting variable dialogue, and other variable dialogue suggestions
Message: Preserve variable separator rows when importing/exporting variable dialogue, and other variable dialogue suggestions This submission is copied and pasted from ELE-I-2481 , which was determined to be a defect. To organize variable lists, labeled separator rows in the variables dialogues are frequently used. The variable dialogue export/import process does not preserve the separator rows. As a result, when the export/import process is done, the resulting variable dialogue looks disorganized and more difficult to read. The example shown below is simple, so does not demonstrate the real importance. For most most customer designs, separators are very helpful for usability/readability. Original Export Imported into other design (missing separators) 1) Please ensure that the variable dialogue export/import looks identical to the original source, including separators. 2) The default save directory for exporting the variable dialogue is PersonalLib > 3D Components, which does not make sense to me because variable sets tend to be tied to specific projects, not 3D components. The default export/import directory should be the same directory as the selected project if the project is already saved to disk. If the project is not yet saved to disk, the user should be prompted to save the file to disk. The directory browse option should have a button option to "Last Variable Export Save Location", which should be preserved within and between AEDT sessions. This option is in case the user wants a quick way to specify an alternative location for saving variable sets. 3) The design variable export dialogue has two options a) "Include referenced project variables", which seems to only export design variables, so should probably be labeled "Include design variables" b) "Include all project variables", which exports design and project variables, so might be better labeled "Include both design and project variables"? The attached project is what I used for testing. The project has both project and design variables and separators in both dialogues.

Title: Layer Stackup Dialogue Units Do Not Match Units Selection Without Manual Toggle
Message: Layer Stackup Dialogue Units Do Not Match Units Selection Without Manual Toggle With AEDT 2025.2 open: 1) File > Import > AutoCAD > PCB-112685-HDR-XX J1.dxf 2) Import stackup and options > PCB 112685 HDR XX.tech > Open 3) Override AutoCAD file units > in 4) OK 5) Layout > Layers The stackup units are inches. The total height is in inches. The layer thicknesses and elevations are in mm, but should be in inches. Toggling the Units field away from "in" to another unit, then back to "in" makes the stackup display in inches: That the stackup thicknesses and elevations do not respect the units without toggling the units field manually seems like a defect.

Title: Opening .aedt File That is Already Open - Cancel Option Ignored - Many Clicks to Exit Process
Message: Opening .aedt File That is Already Open - Cancel Option Ignored - Many Clicks to Exit Process 1) Open an aedt project in AEDT instance 1 (you can use the attached, but it should not matter which .aedt file is used) 2) Open the same file in AEDT instance 2 Sometimes, you will see the below warning, which should be clicked "No": But sometimes that dialogue is not triggered for some reason.  If the user chooses "Yes", then you will see the following asking whether the user wants to wait.  I assume that clicking "OK" is to allow time to close the other instance and "Cancel" means to stop trying to open, so I usually click "Cancel".  However, clicking "Cancel" does not stop the file from attempting to load.  After a few seconds: I click "Cancel" a second time, then see: I click "OK", then see: I click "OK" again.  So there are a total of four separate pop-ups and clicks required to exit when the user does not want to open the project. If the same file is attempted to be opened again, the initial screen giving the Yes/No choice is not longer present.  The sequence of four pop-ups are immediately seen.  If second design is added to the project, then the click count goes from four to six .  It appears that two "Cancel" clicks are required per design, plus two final clicks.  So if a user has 10 designs present, it is expected to take 22 clicks to cancel the process.

Title: MCD 25R2 Golf: Creo plug-in leaks temporary directories when run
Message: MCD 25R2 Golf: Creo plug-in leaks temporary directories when run The CAM Creo plug-in leaves some temporary folders laying around after it is run. Steps to Reproduce: Download the attached file. Create a new workflow. Drag the Creo plug-in into analysis view. On the Initialize PACZ window, choose 'No Files Needed'. On the Add a New Component window, keep the Save Style as Expanded PACZ Folder and specify a name (or accept the default name) and press OK. Browse to & select the tool densityset.prt file and click Open. Select All variables and click OK to close the Select Variables window. Click the Apply button and close the Creo Plug-In window. Run the workflow. Save the workflow. Close ModelCenter. In File Explorer, go to the PACZ folder that was just created. Observe that it has a temporary directory (e.g. 2bc9ac4d-0631-4f95-b89f-bf3882b34374) in it. Go into the temporary directory and observe that it is empty. Environment Details: OS version: Windows 11 Application version: ModelCenter Desktop v2025 R2 Golf Java:  Java 17 Expected vs. Actual Behavior: Expected Behavior: The temporary directories should be cleaned up automatically after the Creo plug-in is run. Actual Behavior: The temporary directories remain in the PACZ folder even after the Creo plug-in is run and closed.

Title: PyAnsys Sound/DPF Sound/SAS - Unit inconsistencies for RPM profiles (and other issues more or less related)
Message: PyAnsys Sound/DPF Sound/SAS - Unit inconsistencies for RPM profiles (and other issues more or less related) DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : There are several inconsistencies in how the unit of an RPM profile is handled throughout SAS, DPF Sound and PyAnsys Sound Data: 2 files attached:   accel with rpm.wav   Bug RPM Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: In SAS, save a wav file with an associated RPM profile In the attached .py script, modify the wav file path (line 6) to use the saved file (or use the wav file attached) run the script (bug 1)  >> Stored profile unit: tr/min => 'tr/min' shouldn't be stored as a unit               >> isolate orders - Warning... (=> ok in that case)                 >> New profile unit: RPM (bug 2) >>  isolate orders - Warning... => no warning should be produced here, the unit is correct (setting rpm unit using Homogeneity enum)                 >> New profile unit: rpm (bug 3)  >>  isolate orders - Warning... =>   no warning should be produced here, the unit is still technically correct (trying to set rpm unit using int - 117 - or str - "dimensionless") (bug 4)  >> ValueError: Unit setter supports either string or tuple (Homogeneity, str) => should be allowed (trying to set rpm unit with just "rpm", comment out previous part to reach this) (bug 5)  >> FieldDefinition SetUnit error : -Unknown exception occurred- : Ideally should also be allowed (should detect that this is dimensionless and proceed accordingly), but at least the message should be somewhat helpful to understand what to do  (setting order list as anything else than a field, comment out previous parts to reach this) (bug 6)  >> isolate orders:19<-error code 4:DPF error - runtime error: dpf core function call; The requested Data format is not valid for this pin, required is "field" while available is "int32" => error ok, but  incriminated pin is not indicated  Expected behavior: bug 1: unit stored in the wav file created by SAS should be rpm or RPM, also after reading the wav file with PyAnsys Sound bug 2: no warning should happen here bug 3: no warning   should happen here bug 4: no error, it is possible to specify a dimensionless unit without having to import the Homogeneity enum bug 5: Helpful error message (such as "'rpm' is not recognize as an SI unit. Try setting it as a dimensionless unit using  `(Homogeneity.dimensionless, 'rpm')`." bug 6: incriminated pin should be clearly indicated in the error message CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): Solution : Impacts : QA Validation: Doc:

Title: PyAnsys Sound / SAS - the class SoundComposer has no project name
Message: PyAnsys Sound / SAS - the class SoundComposer has no project name DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : This class:  SoundComposer — PyAnsys Sound  is the main class for working with a Sound Composer project with PyAnsys Sound. However, a project has name in SAS, but this name does not exist in PyAnsys Sound, which causes several problems: when a project is loaded from a file, its name cannot be found when a project is created in PyAnsys Sound, then saved into a .scn file, then open in SAS, there is no name displayed in the GUI side effect: the name cannot be set in SAS' GUI workaround: if the Sound Composer GUI is maximized, then reduced, the text field to set the project's name is now working correctly Data: Sound Composer project file: SoundComposer-WhatIfScenario-Motor-Gear-HVAC-Noise (SMA modifications).scn Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Bug 1:  Load a Sound Composer project in PyAnsys Sound Print the project -> no name is displayed Display its name -> not possible (no command to do this) This name should be the same as the one displayed in SAS:  from   ansys . sound . core . sound composer   import   SoundComposer sound composer project   =   SoundComposer ( project path = "SoundComposer-WhatIfScenario-Motor-Gear-HVAC-Noise (SMA modifications).scn" ) print ( sound composer project ) Bug 2: Try to display or set the name of the project -> not possible, no member nor method of SoundComposer allows to set or access the name of the project. Bug 3: Save the Sound Composer project above sound composer project . save ( project path = "My Saved SoundComposer Project.scn" ) Reopen it in SAS -> no title is displayed in the GUI -> the title cannot be edited in the GUI (NB: is the window is maximized, then it works again) Expected behavior: When loading a .scn file in PyAnsys Sound, the name of a Sound Composer project is read,  and accessible. When working with a Sound Composer project in SAS, the project name can be set, modified, displayed. When saving a Sound Composer project with PyAnsys Sound, the name is saved in the scn file, so that opening this file in SAS or PyAnsys Sound allows to get this name. (in other words: in class "SoundComposer" add a @property called "name", a @setter, and use it in load and save methods. Optionally it would be a good idea to add an argument "name" in the constructor) CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): Solution : Impacts : QA Validation: Doc:

Message: Imprint splits curves and does not track objects (result.GetCreated[IDesignCurve]() not supported) Imprinting curves on a face splits them at any intersections. Title: Ansys Motion coupled case with excessive overlap when using Automatic Communication Step Size
Message: Ansys Motion coupled case with excessive overlap when using Automatic Communication Step Size A customer reported he was detecting particles crossing the geometries in an Ansys Motion - Ansys Rocky coupled case. After investigating customer setup, I initially tought the issue arised from the excessive refinement of the triangles in certain geometries or due to relatively low YMs (1e+07 Pa for Particles and 1e+09 Pa for Walls). However, even after restoring triangle tesselation to its original size and increasing YM (I even tried with 1e+09 Pa for particles and 1e+11 Pa for walls), I still was seeing excessive overlap messages and particles crossing walls.  One point is that the behaviour always started at 3.55s of simulation, no matter the parameters:   I don't know if this is a coincidence or not, but it coincides with the moment of higher rotational accelaration of the geometry: When I changed the Communication Step Size control in the MBD FMU module to Solver Step Size, then the case is running without excessive overlaps (even with 1e+07 Pa as Particles YM) and already passed the "critical point". But it slows down simulation pace. Steps to reproduce: Open attached case ( \\CDCW16RALLY02\TFSProd\Attachments\Rocky\1314390 ) and run Check that at 3.55s of simulation, the particles will accelerate and start leaking from the geometry (Increasing YM 100x did not help) Changing Communication Step Size control to Solver Step Size in the MBD FMU module and run Check that the particles stop "exploding" and simulation is slower. Development; Triaged

Title: 3D Layout - Layer Stackup Wizard Etching Calculation Convention Inconsistent with 3D Layout Model Editor
Message: 3D Layout - Layer Stackup Wizard Etching Calculation Convention Inconsistent with 3D Layout Model Editor Layer Stackup Wizard etching profile is inconsistent to 3D Layout Modeler. For instance, see attached project.  If you open layer stackup wizard and compute the desired trace width for 85ohm differential impedance, you would get trace width of .07mm.  However, this number is misleading, as it is the underside value (i.e. the shorter "etched" width for the trace).  The expected value is .105mm.  It is also inconsistent with the 3D Layout modeler window,   This only becomes obvious when exporting the design to Q3D:  I think general convention would be that a user would be expecting the line dimensions to be the maximum, and that etching would result in one side being less wide.  This is how the 3D Layout modeler handles it, as running the SYZ sweep on .105mm trace widths give 85ohm TDR: Hopefully this is clear - the modeler needs a value of .105mm to see 85ohms in the TDR, but the Layer Stackup Wizard needs a value of .07mm.  Both are correct, but the side of the trace it is referring to is different between the two.  Please let me know if you need more clarification.

Title: Surface Mount 3D Component Connector S-parameters Differ Between 3DL and HFSS at Low Frequencies
Message: Surface Mount 3D Component Connector S-parameters Differ Between 3DL and HFSS at Low Frequencies The below two projects compare 3DL and HFSS for a surface mount connector on PCB.  The HFSS model was created by exporting the 3DL model and then adding the 3D component for the connector. SurfaceMountConnectorOnPCB WithResistLayers 3DL 2025R2.aedtz SurfaceMountConnectorOnPCB WithResistLayers MCAD 2025R2.aedt There is a top soldermask/resist layer in both that intersect with the connector, but both 3DL and HFSS seem to handle the overlap.  The S-parameters above a few GHz match well, but below 1GHz, the 3DL model appears to have an open circuit.  Green is S21.  Red is S11.  HFSS is solid lines and 3DL is dashed lines.  The red circled part shows the 3DL green dashed S21 sharply coming down at low frequencies.  At 100MHz, the 3DL S21 = -2.28dB, while HFSS S21 = -0.011dB. A discrete sweep from 1MHz to 1GHz with logarithmic x-axis (using the same trace colors and solid/dash representations) shows that the low frequency behavior deviates dramatically.  HFSS has the solid green S21 trace near 0dB across the frequency span, while the 3DL S21 decreases to less than -35dB by 1MHz. Plotting ComplexMagJSurf for both at 1MHz does not show a substantial difference in surface current distribution despite transmission being 35dB worse in the 3DL (left) case.  Port 1 (the coax port) is turned on for both, with port 2 (the stripline port) being turned off. However, looking closer, the ground pin currents in 3DL appear to be discontinuous: Zoomed side view of the same red arrow annotated previous image: In contrast, the currents appear continuous in HFSS: Could the connector ground pin bottom surface in 3DL be disconnected from the vias top surface, thereby creating an open circuit?   The respective via objects seem like they should span all the way to the top of the "Top" layer.

Title: ST -- Problem with display option thick shell - SpaceClaim and Ansys Mechanical shows different results
Message: ST -- Problem with display option thick shell - SpaceClaim and Ansys Mechanical shows different results Hello, I have conducted a series of tests both on the customer's model and on a simplified version to identify the root cause of the issue of the different shell thickness in Ansys Mechanical 2025 R2. Please find the details of my investigation below: 1. Simple Surface Body Test     When the face normal vector is defined in SpaceClaim and the Offset Type is set to Top, the shell thickness display in Mechanical behaves as follows: Conversely, when the Offset Type is changed to Bottom, the expected display is: 2. Initial Test on the customer's Model:   Focusing on a specific surface in the customer's model (as shown in the image below), we observe that the behavior differs from the simplified test: The key difference in the model is the use of Shared Topology via the Component Properties: When the Shared Topology option is set to None in the Component Properties, the behavior in Mechanical aligns with the expected results: Additionally, using the Share Topology tool from the Workbench tab to share the relevant edges of the component also results in the expected behavior: To summarize, the   root cause of the issue appears to be the use of the older method of sharing topology—specifically, enabling the Share option from the component's details.  The issue for this model is reproducible in both Discovery and Spaceclaim in 2025 r2. Please check system A and system B. Thanks in advance.

Title: SIwave import EDB -> some nets will not recognize in SNA
Message: SIwave import EDB -> some nets will not recognize in SNA Hi DEV a customer find this issue in 25R2 CADFEM  reported this snipp Hello, a customer (Quentin Chinal, EREMS France, not listed here) came with a layout with DDR4 channel. He wanted to check for line delays by Signal Net Analyzer, which gives an error message "Could not find any path on net with pins at both ends. Perform Sanitize Layout..." for some of the nets. For some nets it works then doing the Sanitize, but there is still one net "DDR 72b 1 adr o7" having an issue. For that net, the Sanitize converts a larger section of the traces into a plane, which is on the one hand misaligned with the traces (see attached screenshot) and on the other hand not taken into consideration for the Signal Net Analyzer (which runs then without error, but gives "wrong" delay). The customer and me tried a lot to fix the line manually, e.g., conversion into plane and back to trace, partly substracting and re-drawing or using "Connect Selected Traces" from the Advanced tab. Latter converts the split traces into a single trace, looking well, but also failing with the Signal Net Analyzer again. I will attach the edb data the customer sent me, which is a reduced version of his full board (for debugging). I performed there also the Validation Check to a stage where there are no errors shown. Nevertheless, the issue described above could not be fixed. Do you have an idea why that happens and how to fix that specific line (adr o7), in order to make it run with Signal Net Analyzer (so not conversion into planes)? snipp I checked the EDB short and found that  DDR 72b 1 adr o5,  DDR 72b 1 adr o6 and  DDR 72b 1 adr o7 have the same problem so I believe that the export out of the EDA system do something wrong or we misinterpret these data I can't fixed the issue ;-( EDB is attached Bye Ronaldo

Title: Issue with failed designs with OCO when MC is restarted (and optimization resumed)
Message: Issue with failed designs with OCO when MC is restarted (and optimization resumed) Issue summary: Customer (BAE Systems) noticed that OCO, once halted, attempts to resume from the very start of a trade study, while they are expecting it to resume from the last completed run. Original Email to   @Mike Belcher  with more technical details to ask if this is the intended behavior for OCO: Technical Context ModelCenter Configuration: MC 25R1 Workflow: Control a CATIA parametric model, which is then used in an in-house CFD code Optimizer: OCO Max Number of Design Evaluation: 5000 Seed = 1 Use MOP = True A lot of failed designs in the first iteration (with 501 Design Evaluation). Observed Behavior The customer runs MC on a box, which communicates with other boxes. This control box crashed and was restarted, leading to a relaunch of MC. Upon restart, MC recovered the data, the optimization GUI appeared with the 'Resume' option and the Design Explorer Table. The last recorded entry in the design table was column # 34 . Resume Issue When the customer pressed 'Resume', the counter restarted from 1/501 instead of 34/501. CATIA attempted to reopen but almost immediately failed. A successful run typically takes ~5 minutes, while a failed one takes ~1 minute (because CATIA crashes). The customer reported that 19 out of 34 runs failed in the first iteration, estimating a ~20-minute latency between hitting the 'Resume' button and resuming from column #34 with a newer design point. I asked him to provide this quick time estimate, as I felt it could be useful for understanding the behavior and diagnosing the issue. Reproducibility The same behavior occurs when pressing 'Halt' followed by 'Resume'. Additional Notes The customer cannot share the model and described the issue verbally while testing live, without screen sharing. Internal Test on Toy Workflow on MC25R2 Please see the image below, along with the attached model and video. Objective: To verify whether the initial setup completes quickly up to the point where the trade study was previously halted—suggesting that cached values are being reused. Setup: Very simple function,   y =log( x ), to be minimized, with   x  defined in the range [−5,10] and a starting value of 5. Since   y  cannot be evaluated when   x <0, the solver fails in those cases. Results: It appears that when OCO is halted and resumed, it restarts the initial run. Moreover, the first set of runs   takes just as long to complete (10 seconds) as the subsequent ones , indicating that caching may not be working as expected.

Title: Override Unit Fail in any Properties Edit Table
Message: Override Unit Fail in any Properties Edit Table The bug was identified during the use of the SPH Mass Flow Rate module. Basically, when the “Add Formula / Edit Formula” option is used and the “Override Unit” checkbox is selected, if the new unit belongs to the same property unit group (for example, t/h → kg/s or kg/min ), it is displayed correctly for an instant, but then reverts back to the original unit. However, if we select a unit from a different property unit group (for example, K – Kelvin ), it behaves differently: the unit is incorrect, but the GUI keeps the selected unit displayed correctly. A video showing the issue is attached (in 24 seconds the BUG happens). Steps to reproduce: 1º - Using  SPH Mass Flow Rate enable, get the Time Plot curve in Geometries | Data Editors | Curves | <Geometry name>: Mass Flow Rate  2º - In Table tab, Add Formula and Enable (Override Unit).   When it is applied the Expression values works, but the unit continue the same Rocky Build Number: 38459 Triaged

Title: i9 Template Field Winding and Airgap Value Error in v2025.2.2

Title: Meshing Fails After Sharing Topology Between a Surface and a Solid Body
Message: Meshing Fails After Sharing Topology Between a Surface and a Solid Body I was able to reproduce the issue on my end , even with simplified models. Specifically, in a structured setup like following, when using the "Share Topology" tool from the Prepare tab, the common surface body is merged into the solid body. As a result, it is not imported into Mechanical. (System C of attached project)   Following this, the mesh generation process fails and becomes stuck at 5%.   Given that this behavior appears to be problematic ,I am raising this bug report for further investigation.  In the meantime, a workaround is available: In ANSYS Discovery, locate the two or more surface bodies within the same component. Set the Transfer Sharing Option to "Share Topology."   Ensure that the "Merge" option is disabled under the Share Topology settings. With this configuration, the geometry will be imported into Mechanical with shared topology, but the surface body will remain unmerged. This allows the mesh to be generated without issues.     I hope this explanation is clear. Please let me know if you need any further clarification. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Wrong oSL setup when same physical quantity defined multiple times in MCAD export tool
Message: Wrong oSL setup when same physical quantity defined multiple times in MCAD export tool Two situations where the MCAD-oSL export is wrong: when the exact same parameter is defined in both the Requirements and the Objective section, it is calculated twice in the script, which can resullt in a big waste of time depending on the parameter in question, e.g torque ripple with fine mesh and calculation settings when the same quantity is calculated at the same speed but different torque level, both responses take the naming. One cannot differentiate them later on in the oSL integration. I suggest to add "xNm" after "xrpm".

Title: Import fails and Incorrect commands logged in APDL log when importing CATIA V5 file in 25R2 (continuation of Bug #1241442)
Message: Import fails and Incorrect commands logged in APDL log when importing CATIA V5 file in 25R2 (continuation of Bug #1241442) Hi Team,  Earlier this year I logged a bug, Bug 1241442: Path is not considered correctly in ~CAT5IN command  where the path provided in the CAT5IN command is not correctly taken.  Now, in 25R2, there seems to be a new bug, where the path itself is not being written correctly in the log when importing the CATPART via GUI mode as shown below. Also, the actual import fails. This was working correctly in 25R1. Steps to reproduce: The error happens only when the geometry file is stored more than one folders down the current working directory as shown in the Examples below: CWD for APDL: D:\del17\pointmass (1) If the CATPart is located in  D:\del17 --> No problem in the log (as shown below) ~CAT5IN,'02-7403216','CATPart','D:\del17\pointmass (1)\..',SOLIDS,0 If the CATPart is located in D:\ --> PROBLEM in what is printed in log. ~CAT5IN,'02-7403216','CATPart', 'D:\del17\pointmass (1)\D:/ ',SOLIDS,0 In v25R1, the import works, but the log is printed with forward slashes (if the geometry file is located some folders below the CWD) ~CAT5IN,'02-7403216','CATPart','D:/',SOLIDS,0   If the geometry is located some folders above the CWD, the path printed in the log will have backward slashes  ~CAT5IN,'02-7403216','CATPart','D:\del17\pointmass (1)\gui test',SOLIDS,0   Running the APDL commands instead of GUI: in v25R1: Absolute path with forward slashes work, but absolute path with backward slashes fail (was fixed in bug 1241442) in v25R2: Absolute path with forward slashes will not work (new bug?), but absolute path with backward slashes work. I attached a catpart for testing. Customer  Set the current working directory to any folder in D drive

Title: Installing 25R2 over 25R1 corrupts installation; SAM Connector fails; registry state not recovered by uninstall/reinstall
Message: Installing 25R2 over 25R1 corrupts installation; SAM Connector fails; registry state not recovered by uninstall/reinstall Installing 25R2 on top of 25R1 leads to a broken environment. Indicators point to missing/incorrect registry keys after the upgrade. Notes:     - Uninstalling 25R1 and then installing 25R2 does not fully repair the system; issues persist.     - In at least one case, the SAM Connector installer failed within the installer (appeared not to unzip a sub-package), preventing SAM from working.     - Applying registry exports from a “good” machine to a broken machine increased errors, suggesting fragile or environment-specific keys. (Note: this was done as a potential workaround for Kyunghun (ACE) and is not advised for end-users)  - Impact:         - Users can easily enter a non-functional state during common upgrade behavior.     - SAM Connector and potentially other connectors fail to install or run.     - Field users already impacted; more reports likely as 25R2 adoption increases.     - Recovery unclear; may require full cleanup of products and registry, which is risky.       - Affected Versions/Env:         - From: 25R1 existing installation     - To: 25R2 installation on top of 25R1; also observed issues after uninstalling 25R1 and installing 25R2     - Users: Internal test machines (Ajay), field user (Kyung Hoon, South Korea)     - OS: Windows (registry-related)     - Components: ModelCenter core (MC/MCRE/MBSE mentioned), SAM Connector; other connectors appear OK in clean 25R2 (per Don’s usage)       - Repro Steps (current understanding):         1. Start with a machine that has 25R1 installed.     2. Install 25R2 over the top of 25R1.     3. Observe missing functionality and/or connector failures (MC desktop fails to start due to licensing error, SAM connector fails to start due to assembly mismatch).     4. Optional: Uninstall 25R1 and reinstall 25R2; issues may persist due to registry state. (large portions of registry under `HKEY LOCAL MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Phoenix Integration` appear to be missing in at least one case)      5. Attempt to install/use SAM Connector; installer errors and/or SAM not present/working.         - Expected Result:         - Installing 25R2 over 25R1 should either:         - Perform a safe in-place upgrade that preserves/updates all required registry keys and components, or         - Block with a clear message and guide the user through a supported upgrade path.     - Uninstall/reinstall should restore a clean, working 25R2 environment, including SAM.       - Actual Result:         - Post-upgrade environment is broken. SAM Connector fails to install or run; installer may fail to unpack a sub-package.     - Uninstalling 25R1 and reinstalling 25R2 does not reliably repair the environment due to lingering/broken registry keys.

Message: *SET SEGMENT generates duplicate segments When applying a pressure load on a solid mesh, elements are grouped into a set, and the pressure load is applied to this set. Title: 2025 R2 AEDT Icepak DE: Result mismatch when in AEDT when using bool and edb files for ecad
Message: 2025 R2 AEDT Icepak DE: Result mismatch when in AEDT when using bool and edb files for ecad This context comes from a previous customer workflow where they compared results between Classic Icepak and AEDT. The comparison involved importing a .tzr file from Classic Icepak into AEDT, which included ECAD data imported as .bool files in AEDT. They observed a temperature difference of approximately 5–6°C for a specific die, with AEDT reporting the lower value. The customer is currently testing a new workflow. They begin by importing the ECAD files into HFSS, then export them as an EDB (.def), which is subsequently imported into an existing Classic Icepak project. This project is then exported as a .tzr file and opened in AEDT. To account for the loss of the solder mask layer—originally present in the HFSS file—the customer ensures that solid blocks are created in AEDT to represent the solder mask when importing the .tzr file. This step involves the use of the .bool file Additionally, the customer is evaluating a parallel workflow. In this approach, after importing the .tzr file into AEDT, they replace the PCB geometry (originally represented by .bool files) with the original HFSS models. Since the HFSS files include the solder mask layers, the customer ensures that any existing solder mask blocks previously created in AEDT are disabled to avoid duplication. Across all workflows, the material properties, grid cut resolution, and mesh settings remain consistent In this case the AEDT result with tzr (.bool) is not matching with the one with EDB. Surprisingly the AEDT results with the edb (.def) matches with the classic results and is enquiring if the new workflow is alright and want to know the root cause of the issue. I was able to reproduce the varying results in AEDT ie. With bool and edb file for a single board. The results vary by ~ 2 oC here. Does this have to do anything with the difference in ECAD. I ‘m unable to match the mesh number even if it uses the same mesh settings in both cases. This more of the case to investigate the work flow as customer is transitioning to AEDT and the consistency of the results are critical for them. Kindly investigate. Note: For reference I am attaching a aedtz file with the bool and edb import,and the original edb file.

Title: Auto-save can break ChangeProperty() calls
Message: Auto-save can break ChangeProperty() calls Restore the attached archive in desktop, then run the attached script.  It should work fine.  Then, in general options make sure autosave is on and set the autosave interval to just 1 edit.  Close the project, reopen from the archive, and run the attached script again.  This time it shows an error that the Renorm Imped property doesn't exist. It seems like auto-save hitting on the first ChangeProperty() call in the script causes it to malfunction--it should be adding Renorm Imped as a property, but doesn't. This was first discovered in a branch by a failure in the emit regression test SBR DL Mismatch Renorm.  On that branch the number of edits triggered by the test script before the "Do Mismatch Renorm" ChangeProperty() was upped from 9 to 10, causing the test to begin failing with the error above when run in ARM as it uses 10 edits between autosaves.  So I don't think setting the autosave interval to 1 is required to trigger the error, but the script has to be such that the autosave happens during a particular call. Test Impact: EDT EMIT:Coupling/SBR DL Mismatch Renorm

Title: Through Hole Connector 3D Component Results Different in HFSS vs 3DL; Potential Artificial Short Circuit in 3DL?
Message: Through Hole Connector 3D Component Results Different in HFSS vs 3DL; Potential Artificial Short Circuit in 3DL? A through hole connector 3D component in HFSS yields expected propagation characteristics in HFSS, and unexpected apparent short circuit behavior in 3DL.  In both models, the through hole connector signal and ground pins overlap pad and via geometry. The connector launch to PCB in HFSS is shown below using a clip plane view.  The signal path is from the connector signal pin to a stripline  on the orange, metal layer 2.  The field is terminated in a wave port with 0.03mm thick metal backing. S21= -0.1dB at 1GHz, which is a reasonable response Using a clip plane view, and plotting surface currents on the signal and return path shows continuity for all surfaces as expected. The same model in 3DL, which was the source of the geometry for HFSS: Has S21 = -10.48dB at 1GHz, so appears to be short circuited? Title: Issue with Mesh Copy in Mechanical 25R2
Message: Issue with Mesh Copy in Mechanical 25R2 From the documentation:  Mesh Copy Control  it is not clear to us if this behavior is the expected. So I kindly request your opinion on that.  I am guessing that intended behavior is that Mesh Copy should recognize that it needs to re-mesh the target when the source body's methods are changing(?). The obvious workaround is to clear the mesh on the target bodies (or all bodies) before re-mesh, so it is not causing any immediate roadblock. But for a big model or an older model where the user could forget where Mesh Copy was used, it might be problematic. Steps to reproduce the behavior (find also attached a test model) Step 1: For 2 identical bodies, create mesh control(s) and then mesh copy Step 2: Make the mesh & confirm that the copy is working Step 3: Change one of the source body mesh controls Step 4: Check the mesh status, the Mesh Copy does not realise that the source has an obsolete mesh and that the target body therefore also has an obsolete mesh Step 5: After remesh, the target body indeed retains its old obsolete mesh

Title: Big discrepancy of iron loss calculation between Motor-CAD and Maxwell
Message: Big discrepancy of iron loss calculation between Motor-CAD and Maxwell Hello Team,         We have a customer to compare the core loss calculation between Maxwell and Motor-CAD.        Motor-CAD model is using "Bertotti – Maxwell" model to calculate the iron loss, and then export it into Maxwell.          The coefficients of kh,kc,kdc, etc. are correct in Maxwell model, that have corrected numbers generated by corresponding coefficients from the Bertotti – Maxwell model.         Both Motor-CAD and Maxwell models  have same 90 steps per cycle and the meshing is similar between them, and I also adjust meshing (results are same).      I use “Maxwell” and “Bx, By” as you mentioned in Motor-CAD.      Maxwell model reaches the steady state in the core loss results.            However, I find stator core loss of Motor-CAD model is about 11% higher than Maxwell’s results, and rotor core loss is 40% higher than Maxwell model.       For 40% difference, it does not make sense for the calculation tolerance.        Could you check if it is a defect? Thanks. Best regards Howard

Title: getDSMesherSweptInfo takes a lot of time -> MultiZone takes about an hour to generate ~10K mesh
Message: getDSMesherSweptInfo takes a lot of time -> MultiZone takes about an hour to generate ~10K mesh I had this case from Joao Read in ACE today where he was struggling to mesh it but I found that it was just actually taking a very long time to mesh with MZ and if he had waited (he did not)  he would have seen a really perfect mesh.  it takes 54mins on my laptop to generate this 10k element mesh but if I merge top/bottom faces I get this in 2.5mins:  So a couple of questions (1) can we make this faster? If we were to submap surface mesh the top face and use pull/thinsweep to mesh the volume would it be faster than using mapped blocks? (2) He gave up before the 54 mins was up and assumed hanging because the progress bar gets stuck at 5%. Can we add more feedback? e.g. something like preparing data/computing sizing/calculating blocking (this could take a while)/mesh generation/associating to geometry? I guess if there is one chunk (blocking) that is taking 99% of the time this is difficult but is there even steps/tries etc within there we can feedback to progress indicator? Thanks
