Title: [AEDT Circuit] Simultaneous tuning for two LNA setups does not update successfully the respective traces of a report.
Message: [AEDT Circuit] Simultaneous tuning for two LNA setups does not update successfully the respective traces of a report. Electronics Customer Bug Description Issue: See the attached archived project (“Bug Project” – please keep it CONFIDENTIAL after the customer’s request). In the Circuit design (“Circuit1” design) of the attached project, although the “Tune” box is checked/enabled for both the LNA setups of it, when you change the value of each tuning variable (moving the slider up and down) in the “Tune” window, only the traces that correspond to the first LNA setup are updated successfully in the report, as you can see in the attached screen recording (“Issue.mp4” file). If only one of the two “Tune” boxes is checked (e.g. only the “Tune” box that corresponds to the “Ch9” LNA setup), then the traces of the report, that correspond to this setup, are updated successfully, each time you change the value of the respective tuning variables. The issue above is contradictory with the highlighted text of the screenshot below (from the Ansys Circuit Help pdf for version 2025R1 of AEDT): So, based on the above, this issue seems to be a defect/bug. As a comment, this issue has been brought up to our attention by a customer and I managed to reproduce it in the current version of AEDT (2025R1), as well as in previous versions of AEDT (e.g. 2024R2.1, 2024R1.1). Could you please take a look at the issue described above and let me know if it is indeed a defect/bug or if it is the expected behavior of the software? If it is a defect, is there any workaround for the time being, until it is fixed? Thank you in advance for your time and your input! -- Reproducible: (always, sometimes, never) Always in every version of AEDT. Steps to reproduce: 1. Open the attached archived project (“Bug Project” – please keep it CONFIDENTIAL after the customer’s request) and run/analyze the two analysis (LNA) setups (“Ch5” and “Ch9”). 2. Double click on the “S Parameter Chart1” report, in order to bring it in the “Active View” window. 3. Right click on the “Optimetrics” tab in the “Project Manager” window-> select the “Tuning…” option. 4. In the pop-up window (“Tune” window), check the “Tune” box for both the analysis (LNA) setups (“Ch5” and “Ch9”), uncheck the “Browse Available Variations” checkboxes and change the value of the tuning variables using the respective slider each time. After following the steps above, you can see that only the traces, that correspond to the “Ch5” LNA setup, are being updated in real-time in the “S Parameter Chart1” report ; the traces that correspond to the “Ch9” LNA setup are not being updated in real time. -- Proprietary or confidential data: CONFIDENTIAL Other Information:   Windows Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, cores, distribution, GPU model, scheduler, etc.): • Hardware: • HPC: • GPU: • Scheduler: • Co-simulation: • VDS:

Title: Motor-CAD slowdown when multi-parallel running by OptiSlang
Message: Motor-CAD slowdown when multi-parallel running by OptiSlang Hello Devs, Attached, you will find an OptiSlang model that calls several Motor-CAD instances. The purpose is to compare the calculation times required. The analysis is system-dependent, but we can observe the same trends in the following operations: AVERAGED ->   OptiSLang Sequential (excl Design 3)   OptiSLang 2 Parallel OptiSLang 4 Parallel OptiSLang 6 Parallel OptiSLang 8 Parallel Time-Start MotorCAD 5.708 10.05425 21.215 40.2615 54.42125 The time required to simply open multiple Motor-CAD instances (with or without the black box) is increasing. For example, it takes ~6 seconds to open Motor-CAD when solving multiple designs sequentially, but it takes about 54 seconds to open a single instance when asked to open 8 in parallel. We expect some delay when solving Emag and building the Lab (no multithreading), as this is a result of CPU utilization, so it is not a concern. However, another operation that is questionable is the solution for the Duty Cycle and Efficiency Map. Regarding Duty Cycles, it is possible that customers may request a duty cycle with multiple points, which could dramatically increase the calculation time. Is there a way to make these operations scalable? Time-Lab Duty Cycle 6.996 8.707 12.24275 20.328 27.85825 Time-Lab EffMap 11.533 13.884 21.05125 32.86775 54.49625 @Dougie Hawkins   @Daniel Bachinski

Title: Possible problems with particle size check for SPH simulations
Message: Possible problems with particle size check for SPH simulations Warnings for SPH element size when it is not small enough to resolve the particle might be misleading for Custom Polyhedron and Assembly shapes in certain circumstances. The minimum sizes were over-estimated in the below tests, which might lead to simulations running without any error/warning but producing incorrect results. In all tests the SPH element size was set to 0.05 m to trigger the warnings/errors. The Rocky simulation archive and the STL file for the I-beam are attached to this report. Two trials were made with the attached case: Trial 1 : Here, an I-beam shape particle was tested, which was created as a Custom Polyhedron and imported as STL. The triangle size for this STL was set to 0.01 m. This shape has the smallest thickness at its centre as in the below screenshot: However, on Rocky Status Panel, it captures the minimum particle size as 0.1 m. Trial 2 : In this test, sphere, sphero-cylinder, and their assemblies (screenshot below) are checked. Sphere diameter is set to 0.01 m, and sphero-cylinder sieve size is set to 0.005 m with aspect ratio of 2. Rocky captures the minimum sizes of the sphere and spherocylinder correctly in the Status Panel. However, for the assembly, it prints out that the minimum particle size is 0.00999 m, while the smallest dimension in the assembly should come from the spherocylinder with sieve size of 0.005 m. QA Process

Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 BETA: FMU Plug-In does not pick up on defined bounds for variable
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 BETA: FMU Plug-In does not pick up on defined bounds for variable Not sure if this is a bug or a feature request, but basically:  Using the attached .fmu project, there is a variable named "e" that is defined in the internal .xml file, like so:     <ScalarVariable name="e" valueReference="6" causality="parameter" variability="tunable" initial="exact" description="Coefficient of restitution">       <Real start="0.7" min="0.5" max="1"/>     </ScalarVariable>     <ScalarVariable name="v min" valueReference="7" variability="constant" description="Velocity below which the ball stops bouncing">       <Real start="0.1" declaredType="Velocity"/>     </ScalarVariable> In the context of the FMU plug-in from ModelCenter wrapping it, we do pick up on the "Real start" value being "0.7", but we miss or don't pick up on the min and max bounds defined right next to it. From a user's perspective, this would probably be a welcome feature, instead of having to manually set the bounds that are already defined anyway.

Title: LSDYNA and Motion Analysis State Does Not Reflect Underdefined Children
Message: LSDYNA and Motion Analysis State Does Not Reflect Underdefined Children ACTDYNA analysis does not reflect the state of any underdefined children even when a load is added. Motion analysis does not reflect the state of an underdefined solution but does if an underdefined load is added. Behavior with analysis added as-is: Clear app data. Launch Mechanical. Add the following analyses from the context menu: Static Structural Motion LSDYNA LSDYNA Restart Note that the state of the Motion and LSDYNA analyses are "Not-Solved" instead of "Underdefined". Behavior when adding Underdefined loads: Add a load to each of the analyses. Note that now the Motion state is "Underdefined" and LSDYNA is still "Not-Solved". Notes: - Found in 25R2 and unknown when it was introduced.

Title: Page connector allowing connection between non-conservative and a conservative pin
Message: Page connector allowing connection between non-conservative and a conservative pin The attached project (Ansys SSCB 0319 25R1) is originally from Bug 1223354. In the design 4 P1 SSCB PWM14 phase closer GaN wrong= , output of PWM1 is connected to Page Port S1. And then the conservative pin (Gate) of the Spice model IGC033S101 L1 is also connected to S1. Usually UI warns such illegal connection (as far as I checked with 25.1). So I'm not sure how the AE established this connection.  In the netlist, there is no connection is actually established between PWM1.VAL and the Gate of IGC033S101 L1. But from the schematics point of view it appears both are connected.  If I try this in a new project (see PageConnNonConservative FromScratch251.aedt) in 25.1 UI, the netlist generator error outs as follows:     [error] Netlist error due to unconnected pin "GATE" for component instance "IGC033S101 L1 1", design "TwinBuilder1" This is the correct behavior. So not sure why it doesn't show it on the original project.

Title: Thermal transient class in internal scripting tool - Wrong temperatures output from Thermal
Message: Thermal transient class in internal scripting tool - Wrong temperatures output from Thermal Hi, I am running a duty cycle analysis and use the thermal transient class in the Motor-CAD internal scripting interface to extract some temperatures during or after the transient. It seems that those temperatures got stuck to some temperature values calculated from steady state analysis prior to the transient. I attached the mot file. See the results below. Duty Cycle Transient is enabled from the Calculation -> Calculation page A duty cycle is setup up in terms of torque and speed values. Machine components are at the ambient temperature at start. The transient will stop if the winding component reaches 90C Python Scripting tab The main() function is just used for testing when pressing the run button. The thermal class() function is used throughout the analysis, at start, during and at the end of the transient. Results As expected the simulation stops when the winding temperature is exceeded However wrong winding temperature values are extracted throughout the analysis as shown in the Message Display window. When pressing the run button for testing: we get good results.. I wonder whether temperatures values are not taken from the steady state analysis performed priori to the transient When running a steady state analysis we get very close results... Thanks for the help!

Title: MCD Geometry Node doesn't support "Appearance'
Message: MCD Geometry Node doesn't support "Appearance' Geometry objects have an appearance that can control their color and alpha. The Node does not support this: see a SOR, QuadFacet and Node all set to use parent color: Presumably this is because the color can be specified, but it doesn't have to be.   Node is the only geometry type where the color can be specified, but it doesn't support alpha or defaulting to the GeomInfo Appearance. Would be great if Nodes didn't specify used the Appearance, or if there was some blending of the node color and the Appearance setting. This may be a feature request, but nodes not coloring with the appearance when all the other geometry types feels like a bug. Picture came from linked model: GeomNodeIgnoresApperance.pxcz

Title: MC MBSE Ansys SAM 25R2 RC: Requirement attribute expression doesn't show Type or expression value in Analysis Editor
Message: MC MBSE Ansys SAM 25R2 RC: Requirement attribute expression doesn't show Type or expression value in Analysis Editor Screenshot is attached.  What happened? : When loading the "TIE copy CMB SAM25R2 sample model - Electric Powertrain Battery Sizing and Verification1" example into MC MBSE, the attribute "testExpression" under the "Minimum Operating Time" requirement shows "Type" as "Unknown" and the Requirements Details pane shows a blank value. The expression is only identified when attempting to link it to an Analysis variable, where a tooltip indicates that linking expressions to analyses is not supported. What should have happened? : The "Type" should show as "Real" and the expression value should be visible in the Requirements Details pane or as a tooltip. Where does it occur? : Analysis Editor in MC MBSE How often does it occur? : Always According to  User Story 1227068: Allow connecting requirement attributes to analyses as both inputs and outputs  , the expectation is that we show the value of the expression as a value or tooltip. Repro Steps : Load the "TIE copy CMB SAM25R2 sample model - Electric Powertrain Battery Sizing and Verification1" example. Search for "testExpression" in the project search bar and note that the Definition is set to "Real" and the Value is set to "1 + 1" (no quotes). Open the workflow in ModelCenter using the web File menu. In the MC MBSE window, choose to Edit the "Mater Out (Copy)" analysis from the Analyses pane. Expand the "0-1 Minimum Operating Time" requirement to the "testExpression" item and also expand the "Requirements Details" pane at the bottom. Attempt to drag the "testExpression" attribute to another variable like "inMass" and observe the tooltip indicating that linking expressions to analyses is not supported. Expected vs. Actual Behavior : Expected Behavior : The "Type" should show as "Real" and the expression value should be visible in the Requirements Details pane or as a tooltip. Actual Behavior : The "Type" shows as "Unknown" and the Requirements Details pane shows a blank value. The expression is only identified as being one when attempting to link it to an Analysis variable.

Title: File definition separator works incorrectly with only a space defined flags
Message: File definition separator works incorrectly with only a space defined flags If a comma is not specified in the separator attribute, the variable and value are not picked up in the input file.  I attached 2 examples, one is for creating a variable and the number from the input file. The second example is for reading a string from the same input file.  If the input file does not include comma separators between the string values in the line, the string values to associate with the variable are not picked up.  Commas were required to find the arguments.  This will be an issue since many standard input files will have spaces as separators between values in a single line.

Title: API for get solder info error setting calibration factor
Message: API for get solder info error setting calibration factor When invoking the API to get solder info, it can cause a NullPointerException. Steps Copy the attached solder.csv file to the user settings directory at: C:\Users\<user name>\AppData\Roaming\Sherlock. I did not edit this file. It was created by Sherlock. I don't know how it got in this state, but I assume this can happen from normal use. Launch Sherlock with the command line option: -grpcPort=9090 Invoke the SherlockCommonService.getSolderInfo API. This can be done with a tool like Kreya or from PySherlock, including running the test unit tests. Result Sherlock doesn't send a response. A NullPointerException occurs. This happens because the CC Calibration Factor is null and the generated GRPC code doesn't allow setting the string field value to null. This is an unhandled exception. Title: Model not working correctly, results conflict each other
Message: Model not working correctly, results conflict each other  In the attached project file (keep confidential), when the customer simulated only the cutout, they obtained the expected low insertion loss in the passband (5–7 GHz). However, when they simulated the full board, they observed a high insertion loss in the passband (5–7 GHz), whereas they were expecting similar low insertion loss as with the cutout. I removed the encrypted 3D component and added two 0.01 Ω resistors between the top transmission line and the two bottom transmission lines, and I got −3 dB loss at DC for each transmission line, which is expected since this works similar to a Wilkinson power divider. This experiment confirms that there is no open or short in the nets connecting the top transmission line to the bottom transmission lines. It looks there is an issue when the encrypted 3D component is added to the full board. I simulated the full board model with and without mesh fusion in both 2025 R1 and 2025 R2, and obtained the same results. I also exported the board as a layout component to HFSS and observed similar behavior, both with and without mesh fusion.  Please refer to the attached power point for more details

Title: Icepak and Q3D both behaving improperly with temperature-dependency in Joule feedback
Message: Icepak and Q3D both behaving improperly with temperature-dependency in Joule feedback Both Carlos and I have tried to run this model quite a few times. If you run a constant electrical conductivity setting, both the Icepak only Joule heating setup and the Q3D setup get similar answers. I do not like the 14 C difference, but at least they're in range over the 70 C ambient. Here's the bad part: I use a temperature-dependent input for the electrical conductivity and both behave incorrectly in this model but completely different. In Icepak, the temperature DROPS significantly. This CANNOT occure as the conductivity is decreasing with temperature over 22 C. As such, a model that's already 400+ C over ambient and almost 500 C above the reference temperature should show a significant increase in power and inherently temperature in the looped run. That's a 200 C drop!! With the looped version in Q3D, there are no changes at all even though temperature-dependency and enable feedback are both selected.  The user thinks that Icepak is more accurate than other tools (RHSC-ET, Lumerical HEAT, etc., but I'm not seeing it with these results. Please let me know if there's anything that can be done. I tried the basic tutorial model and the behavior seems correct in Icepak so this has no real explanation behind it.

Title: C_WATERCONTENT is not always visible in PEM electrolysis
Message: C WATERCONTENT is not always visible in PEM electrolysis @Chao Han   @Genong Li   Hello Chao and Genong, I have come across an issue where I needed to make the protonic conductivity a function of the water content.  For that I wrote a very simple DEFINE PROPERTY-type UDF with 3 UDMs, so that the resulting value of the protonic conductivity as well as the values of C WATERCONTENT and C T can be visualized. The interesting thing is that it worked on a Bosch case seemlessly while QuestOne's case has issue at seeing the C WATERCONTENT (c, t) macro. It is exactly the same UDF, the main options of the models are the same e.g. the osmotic drag and the water content options are chosen and enabled in the Electrolysis panel. After the client failed to make it work, I got their case on my machine using exactly the same .c file and can reproduce issue reliably. Please find attached the .c file as well as the relevant couple of the case and data files. One case file is called UDF working (can be opened on 2nodes) and the other one is bigger (it can be opened on 4 nodes) I tried to open ithe nonworking case on 35 nodes with exactly the same output. In the non-working case, the C WATERCONTENT returns zero value, despite the fact that the Water Content variable under Potential in the contours panel. This is very odd since this type of UDF does not need any parallelization considerations. The options are the same and I just wonder whether the order of their activation/deactivation might have something to do with this bug. Kind regards, Aleksey.

Title: ModelCenter MC MBSE 25R1 BETA: Mismatch between open Execution Plan tab and selected Workspace Explorer entry
Message: ModelCenter MC MBSE 25R1 BETA: Mismatch between open Execution Plan tab and selected Workspace Explorer entry I am not certain if this is a new issue or not, but it "feels wrong enough" that it may have worked differently / correctly in the past, and either way is worth noting. Screenshot attached. Basically, and this is more noticeable if you have many Execution Plans and many open Plans and Results, but from the Workspace Explorer, if you double-click on a given Execution Plan to open it for example, but then in the open tabs, click on a different one - in the Workspace Explorer, the "selected entry" does not update to the one you clicked, the currently open tab. I feel that from a user experience point of view, the currently open tab (Execution Plan or Result) should be the one highlighted in the Workspace Explorer. As you click around, or delete (and thus remove) the open tabs and you move on to the next one, the entry should follow suit.

Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Trying to use "Show Component's GUI" on inserted PACZ from Minerva throws error message Using the IT-11 deliverable, if I insert a PACZ from Minerva (like the "Core Engine PACZ.pacz" from the MC MBSE training) into a MCD workflow using the "File -> Insert Model..." menu item, it will insert into the workflow. Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Cached Minerva credentials are not used / set automatically with the "Import from Minerva" plug-in
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Cached Minerva credentials are not used / set automatically with the "Import from Minerva" plug-in If you access Minerva by way of the other new features with the IT-11 deliverable, like from the File -> Open menu, then those Minerva authentication credentials are cached for the next time you do so. However, if you then go to the "Import from Minerva" plug-in, the dialog that comes up has the default "localhost" information for accessing Minerva. I feel like if the credentials are cached, that dialog should at least pre-populate with the server address and username, if not just bypass it altogether and show the relevant Minerva location, automatically authenticating.

Title: Turning on orthotropic conductivity results in solution divergence in Explore
Message: Turning on orthotropic conductivity results in solution divergence in Explore Hi, I have a CHT solved case in 24.2. The max temperature values in Discovery Explore are 127C which matches closely with Icepak value of max 133C. In Icepak, for PCB the material uses orthotropic thermal conductivity, but in 24.2 isotropic thermal conductivity was used.  So, keeping everything else the same in 25.1 Explore and using orthotropic thermal conductivity for PCB material results in temperatures of 5.5e11 C.  It seems that the solution has diverged. Thermal conductivity value used is same as in Icepak, so material property should not be an issue behind this issue.  Please find model attached. The model is customer confidential so please do not share outside DBU.

Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 RC Alfa: "Save As" action to Minerva has blank "File Name" by default
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 RC Alfa: "Save As" action to Minerva has blank "File Name" by default Was not sure if this was a user story or a bug, but basically: If you do a "Save As" action in ModelCenter Desktop, and work with the local file system, the default name is the name of the already saved workflow you're using - which makes sense, from a modern Windows UI perspective. However, if you choose in the Save As dialog (which has the name populated) to instead save in Minerva, when you get to the Ansys Minerva save dialog, there is nothing in the "File Name" field. It feels "more correct" for the name of the workflow you're using to be pre-populated, so that if users are using the same-name file names between their local system and the Minerva setup, then having to enter in the name again just introduces a chance for a user to have a typo and then not have the file names match. Screenshot is attached.

Title: Command recorded in script for creation of line is incomplete for some models
Message: Command recorded in script for creation of line is incomplete for some models It seems that when a line is created that passes through a body and extends beyond a face, the command in a script (index) is missing some information necessary for successful replay. When the line is contained within a body, the following commands are recorded # Sketch Line start = Point2D.Create(MM(5), MM(-8)) end = Point2D.Create(MM(5), MM(8)) result = SketchLine.Create(start, end) baseSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0].Curves[0]) targetSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0] .GetChildren[IDatumLine]()[0] ) result = Constraint.CreatePerpendicular(baseSel, targetSel) However, if the line extends outside the body, the command is as shown below.  The information in bold above is missing and there is an error of "invalid selection for perpendicular constraint" on the last line shown. # Sketch Line start = Point2D.Create(MM(6), MM(-15)) end = Point2D.Create(MM(6.00000000000001), MM(19)) result = SketchLine.Create(start, end) baseSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0].Curves[0]) targetSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0]) result = Constraint.CreatePerpendicular(baseSel, targetSel) If the GetChildren part is added, the command is successful. The failure also occurs where bodies overlap as is the case with a cutter body. I have attached a project containing a simple fluid simulation and two index scripts, one of which creates a line contained within the body (Box ) and one in which the line extends outside the body (Box Line4 ).

Title: MBSE 25.1: Embedded and Decorator modes each check out mc_level1
Message: MBSE 25.1: Embedded and Decorator modes each check out mc level1 Creating a bug for this so we don't lose track of it. Starting Embedded Mode from Cameo/Rhapsody checks out an mc level1 license and keeps it checked out until the vendor tool is closed. Decorator mode also checks out an mc level1 license and keeps it until the vendor tool is closed, so if a user opens both, we check out 1 more mc level1 than desired. The proper fix for this is to create a shared licensing context in the vendor tool plug-in ode, but this is not possible with the current Java licensing implementation (the code the  Java wrapper is wrapping does not have any of the license context methods). There are a couple possible other fixes that could make this better: Make decorator mode not check out a license. Need to check that a user can't run a simulation without a license Track in the Java code whether we've opened Decorator or Embedded mode and not check out a license when opening the other one (pass empty string as the command-line arg for the license name when starting ). BLOCKED

Title: ModelCenter 25R1: OCO algorithm with multiple objectives reports error about not converging (though convergence is not expected - should be pareto front instead)
Message: ModelCenter 25R1: OCO algorithm with multiple objectives reports error about not converging (though convergence is not expected - should be pareto front instead) From Margherita Coda (ACE):  Background: I'm running an multi-opti. problem in MC (ozyczka and kundu benchmark) and selected OCO as the algo to run it But that error popped up. I'm expecting a pareto front and not a single best design as result of this opti task. This is why I'm surprised by this error but I'm missing something here. [see attached workflow file]  I'm expecting a Pareto front made of 5 regions. It should resemble the one on   this link   (from pymoo website). In one of my tests, I got the error above AND this Pareto front, which I like!   It is also quite similar to the one I'm getting in oSL (see image below).     I just need more design points to improve it but the algorithm always stops with the same error after 201 runs (elapsed time: 48/51 sec), even though it seems it is going in the right direction.  Investigation results from JED:  The algorithm appears to be done exploring the design space after 200 runs. Looking at the pareto front in the Opt Tool, it looks very similar to the result in optiSLang:   The error dialog about not converging on a best design seems to happen any time you have a result with a pareto front instead of a single best design. The message is technically correct, but is not an error - not finding a single best is expected given the optimization problem.    The OptTool code checks 'algorithm->IsConverged()'  ( https://tfs.ansys.com:8443/tfs/ANSYS ModelCenter/Plug-Ins/ git/OptTool?path=/solutions/applications/PHXSolver/Algorithms/optiSLangAlgorithms/oSLAlgorithmsOOP/&version=GBmain&line=568&lineEnd=568&lineStartColumn=13&lineEndColumn=43&lineStyle=plain& a=contents ) and throws if IsConverged is false.   The error dialog only show up if the OptTool is added to the model and "throwErrorOptRunFail" is true.   Overall, the algorithm seems to be working as expected and giving good results, but there are a couple minor things that look like bugs: We should not report an error about not converging when the result of an optimization is a pareto front. This might be a change in the oSL algorithm or in our integration. This appears to be limited to the oSL algorithms. Running Darwin Algorithm on the same problem does not error and produces a pareto front. The error dialog from the OptTool still has the red bird icon. This bug report is to fix 1. above.

Title: [Regression] Student Version (26.1) Dynamic link tests fail on cdcw11ebuqasv01 due to HFSS license exhaustion (Jul 14, 2025)
Message: [Regression] Student Version (26.1) Dynamic link tests fail on cdcw11ebuqasv01 due to HFSS license exhaustion (Jul 14, 2025) Three Circuit-HFSS dynamic link based ARM regression tests failed on Jul 14, 2025 when run using the Ansys Electronics Desktop Student Edition  only on  cdcw11ebuqasv01 . The failures are caused by HFSS simulations not launching due to the error: Maximum licensed number of demo users already reached. Simulation was terminated by license error. The tests passed on July 11. To reproduce:  Launch and solve the attached projects in SV 14th July build (log files are attached as well). To summarize: HFSS components (e.g., HFSSDesign1 , TeeModel ) fail to simulate Nexxim dynamic link fails: There is no simulation data available from the dynamically linked component Circuit simulation aborts with rejected fieldsolver:X  devices But the HFSS design solves fine by itself (if not solved from the Circuit design) The issue is only reproducible on the  official SV machine (Windows 11) which is dedicated solely for SV runs: The issue is not seen with 25.2, but only with 26.1 on  cdcw11ebuqasv01  - even after a clean install and machine reboot. Affected ARM tests: [EDT STUDENT] Circuit/UI/dynamic link/push excitation/f to freq/F to Freq Push Excitation HFSS [EDT STUDENT] Circuit/UI/dynamic link/push excitation/f to freq/F to Freq Push Excitation HFSS Thevenin [EDT STUDENT] Circuit/examples/RF Microwave/Filters/WaveguideFilterDynLink

Title: Variation solve interruption dialog not invoked for projects with embedded scripts
Message: Variation solve interruption dialog not invoked for projects with embedded scripts Embedded scripts have been integrated with variations such that when applying a variation the script is ran. It has been noticed that the variation solve interruption dialog is not invoked for projects with embedded scripts This erroneous behaviour is likely due to an issue with the dialog appearing when a DV was set and the script ran. A workaround was implemented in the `InterruptionHandler` class to not raise the dialog if an embedded script is present. This has resolved the issue of the dialog appearing at the wrong time but does mean this interruption functionality does not work at all if an embedded script is included. We should look to update this such that the interruption handler is 'disabled' at the period the variation is being set and the script run. Changes when the set is occurring are expected. The erroneous guard can be found at the start of `InterruptionHandler.IsUserChoiceNeededToContinue()` method. Steps to reproduce Open heatsink sample project Parameterize heat Add a few DVs Open the script editor from the file menu and embed any script (option in the toolbar) Run a local update all variations Edit any variation whilst the solve is on-going [BUG: Notice the interruption dialog does not appear) DAT Triaged; Disco Parameter Sweeps; Disco Script Parameters

Title: Error when computing Normal force in surfaces through SPH : Force curves with pairwise potential
Message: Error when computing Normal force in surfaces through SPH : Force curves with pairwise potential When simulating SPH with Pairwise (1 SPH element on an incline plane), there are 2 ways of calculating the normal force in the geometry : with custom Property: Area : Cell * Force : Normal with custom curve : (sqrt((SPH : Force : X)²+ (SPH : Force : Y)²+ (SPH : Force : Z)²) However, the results for the curve are not the same when using Pairwise (for CSF, for example, they are the same). It seems like for pairwise it is not accounting for the friction forces. Normal force (from property and curve) with CSF Normal force for Pairwise with capillary friction = 0 8/18/2025 2:57 PM Bug filed on "Rocky Test: Evaluate Capillary Friction model" Step no. Result Title 1. Passed Set up a case with one SPH element in an Incline Plane with Pairwise Potential as Surface Tension model and IISPH solver. Expected Result There's a simple simulation case with the new feature enabled ready to be run 2. Failed Procedure: Assume that the Pairwase Potential model is correct and solve the cinematics. Then, run the case in Rocky and compare results by extracting forces from SPH Boundary Interaction Statistics module. Criteria: Analyze the tangential force and solve any cinematic equation for the SPH element. Should be the same in Rocky and Analytical. Expected Result The tangential force measured in Rocky should be the same as the 'analytical' one. Comments: Attached ppt explains that rocky is missing for both incline planes (15 and 45 degrees). Title: uninitialized variables in PartRegionMesh::get_NumNodesEZ( int* piNumNodes )
Message: uninitialized variables in PartRegionMesh::get NumNodesEZ( int* piNumNodes ) While migrating model assembly c# code to dotnet, I came accross this issue where the code tries to add to the out piNumNodes but doesn't init it. Call stack: which calls: which calls: The issue is not seen in .net framework or cpp because values are initialized explicitely to zero before call. In dotnet, values aren't initialized in the interop layer *by design* and we can't do anything about it. In this case, I think it is a coding, at the top of the function *piNumNodes should be set to zero. Serverity of the bug is minor in .net framework or cpp but is serious for dotnet usage. EDIT: here's the COM layer in dotnet core (notice the SkipLocalsInitAttribute ) : [global::System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute("Microsoft.Interop.ComInterfaceGenerator", "")] [global::System.Runtime.CompilerServices. SkipLocalsInitAttribute ] int global::Ansys.Common.DotNet.Interop.AnsStdObjects.IBaseMesh.get NumNodesEZ() {     var( this, vtable native) = ((global::System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshalling.IUnmanagedVirtualMethodTableProvider)this).GetVirtualMethodTableInfoForKey(typeof(global::Ansys.Common.DotNet.Interop.AnsStdObjects.IBaseMesh));     int retVal;     int invokeRetVal;     {         invokeRetVal = ((delegate* unmanaged[MemberFunction]<void*, int*, int> ) vtable native[8])( this, & retVal);     }     // NotifyForSuccessfulInvoke - Keep alive any managed objects that need to stay alive across the call.     global::System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.ThrowExceptionForHR( invokeRetVal);     global::System.GC.KeepAlive(this);     return retVal; } this is equivalent to the cpp code int numNodes; // uninitialized pIBaseMesh->get NumNodesEZ(& numNodes);

Title: Regression: OSError [WinError 6] on Script Termination Using CPython261.bat and Service() Default Port
Message: Regression: OSError [WinError 6] on Script Termination Using CPython261.bat and Service() Default Port Windows 11/22H4 Unified Package Name: 2025-09-01 00:44 P00 CEI Build:   fe876fe8a1 ------------------------------------ CPython261.bat triggers an Ignored Exception error when running a script that starts and stops an ADR service, causing regression test failures. --- Description When using CPython 3.12.11 (via CPython261.bat ), a script that instantiates an ADR Service object and calls `start()` and `stop()` completes with an ignored exception during process termination. The service itself starts and stops successfully, but the error occurs at script exit. This issue does not  occur with: - Other Python versions (e.g., 3.10 , 3.12.10 , 3.13.4 ). - Interactive execution (running CPython261.bat and executing the script line by line). - Scripts where the `port` parameter is explicitly set in the Service()  constructor. --- Steps to Reproduce 1. Ensure CPython 3.12.11 is used via `CPython261.bat`. 2. Create and run a Python script with the following structure:    import os    from ansys.dynamicreporting.core import Service    nexus = Service(ansys installation=installation, db directory=database dir)  # port left undefined    nexus.start()    print("Server started.")    try:        nexus.stop()        print("Server stopped.")    except Exception as err:        raise err 3. Execute the script using:    > CPython261.bat --- Observed Behavior - Service starts and stops successfully. - Upon script termination, the following traceback appears:    ```    Exception ignored in: <function Popen. del at 0x0000022B279EE520>    Traceback (most recent call last):      File "D:\Ansysdev\Installs\v261\CEI\apex261\machines\win64\Python-3.12.11\Lib\", line 1130, in del        self. internal poll( deadstate= maxsize)      File "D:\Ansysdev\Installs\v261\CEI\apex261\machines\win64\Python-3.12.11\Lib\", line 1575, in internal poll        if WaitForSingleObject(self. handle, 0) == WAIT OBJECT 0:           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^    OSError: [WinError 6] The handle is invalid    ``` Expected Behavior - No exception should be raised when the script exits. Impact - This error causes the testing tool to return a "test failed" status, resulting in three regression test failures that rely on the CEI CPython interpreter. Workaround - Explicitly set `port=8000` when creating the `Service` object:    nexus = Service(ansys installation=installation, db directory=database dir, port=8000)

Title: In AVxcelerate Labs, using the "Sensor Labs" button to edit the sensor may lose changed done and saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view.
Message: In AVxcelerate Labs, using the "Sensor Labs" button to edit the sensor may lose changed done and saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view. DESCRIPTION: Data : Notes : Steps to reproduce: Launch AVxcelerate Labs. Delete all the sensor Layout in AVX Labs Create a new sensor layout and add a sensor to it and then save the sensor layout. Click on the "Sensor Labs" button at the top of the AVxcelerate Labs window and load the same sensor layout as in the "Sensor Preparation" view. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button. Move any sensor and click on the "Save sensor layout" button. Click on the "Edit sensor layout" button (pencil icon button at the right of the "Save sensor layout" button): the location of the sensor in the embedded "Sensor Labs" editor matches the location saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view. Change the "Manufacturer" value of the sensor layout, press the 'tab' key on you keyboard and wait for the save  icon   animation to finish. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button at the top of the window: the sensor layout is reloaded in the "Sensor Preparation" view but the sensor are still in their latest saved location. Close the AVxcelerate Labs window. Repeat steps 1 to 5. Click on the "Sensor Labs" button at the top of the AVxcelerate Labs window: the location of the sensor in the embedded "Sensor Labs" does not match the location saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view at step 5. Change the "Manufacturer" value of the sensor layout , press the 'tab' key on you keyboard and wait for the save    icon   animation to finish. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button at the top of the window: the sensor layout is reloaded in the "Sensor Preparation" view and the sensor that was moved at step 5 reverts to its initial location from step 2. Expected behavior: At step 8, the "Sensor Labs" embedded editor should have been updated with the latest sensor location and orientation values as it is the case when using the "Edit sensor layout" button. Reproducible :  always Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version). Title: MCRE 25.2 - QuickWrap: Temporary run directories not completely cleaned up
Message: MCRE 25.2 - QuickWrap: Temporary run directories not completely cleaned up When running the attached component from a standalone QuickWrap, the .phx srun* directory won't be cleaned up after running or closing QuickWrap. This case leaks all of the files involved in the run. If adding the QuickWrap component through MCRE to a ModelCenter workflow, the run directory won't be completely cleaned up. The run files are cleaned up, but the run directory is left around. This requires the "Run Sharing / Handle parallel runs by:" field to be set to "Run each execution request in a temporary folder". The other settings don't create temp files. One thing to note is that this was on the transient VMs, so the directory the temp files are saved to are in OneDrive. If this doesn't reproduce normally, it might be worth checking with a space in the path. I also haven't tested this on linux. Steps to Reproduce: Standalone Download and unzip the attached component Open standalone QuickWrap Open the caliper.scriptWrapper file Run using the "Test Run..." button Close QuickWrap. Notice the temp directories and files all still exist. Title: Ansys Installer 25R2 RC: ModelCenter Remote Execute gets installed inside of ModelCenter Desktop folder, even when installed by itself
Message: Ansys Installer 25R2 RC: ModelCenter Remote Execute gets installed inside of ModelCenter Desktop folder, even when installed by itself I found with the Ansys all in one installer, if you install ModelCenter Remote Execute, it will be installed "under", or as a child folder of the ModelCenter Desktop folder. This happens even if you just install ModelCenter Remote Execute by itself.  What I expected, was that since ModelCenter Remote Execute is a separate application, that it would be "one level higher", in the same v252 parent directory that the other applications like ModelCenter Desktop and optiSLang get installed to.  Reproduction Steps: 1) Using the Ansys all in one installer on a fresh machine or VM, choose to install only the ModelCenter Remote Execute from the list of applications in the "Connect" group.  2) Open the Windows Explorer, and browse to the installation location of "C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v252". 3) Note that there is a "ModelCenter" folder, if you expand that, inside are the "Java Selection UI" and the "ModelCenter Remote Execution" directories.  I'm not sure where the Java folder specifically is meant to go, probably one parent level up as well, but the ModelCenter Remote Execute folder should have a directory for itself in the v252 parent level directory.

Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 RC Foxtrot: SolidWorks Configuration tool lists unsupported SOLIDWORKS versions on Windows 11
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 RC Foxtrot: SolidWorks Configuration tool lists unsupported SOLIDWORKS versions on Windows 11 The SolidWorks plugin currently displays a long list of SOLIDWORKS releases from 2016 through 2024 , including versions that are not supported on Windows 11, in the list of "Configure SolidWorks" options available to choose from. This matters because ModelCenter will not support Windows 10, due to Windows 10 EOL, starting with 26R1. Official guidance states that only 2022 SP2 and newer versions can run on Windows 11. The inclusion of unsupported options could confuse users and may lead to failed installations or support escalations.   https://www.solidworks.com/support/system-requirements https://community.goengineer.com/forums/topic/701-solidworks-support-for-windows-11   Steps to Reproduce:   Open the "Configure SolidWorks" option from the SolidWorks plug-in via ModelCenter Desktop on a Windows 11 machine. Note the "Select SolidWorks version" window that opens up. Observe that the list includes versions from 2016 up to 2024 .     Expected Behavior: The configuration window should list only the currently supported Windows 11 versions— the current SOLIDWORKS release and the two preceding releases (for example, 2025, 2024, 2023 ).   Actual Behavior: The configuration window lists all versions from 2016 through 2024 , many of which are unsupported on Windows 11 and may not even have installer packages available to customers.   Additional Context:   Official System Requirements: Windows 11 support begins with SOLIDWORKS 2022 SP2 and continues in later releases. Community recommendation: limit version list to current + two prior to align with support lifecycles and avoid user error.   Recommendation: Trim the configuration tool’s version list to only include the current SOLIDWORKS release and the two preceding releases (e.g., 2025, 2024, 2023 ), and retire all versions earlier than that from the dropdown.

Title: 3DL Export to HFSS - Warns Exported with Previous Version Despite Doing So In Same Version
Message: 3DL Export to HFSS - Warns Exported with Previous Version Despite Doing So In Same Version Using AEDT 2025R2 (or any recent prior version): 1) In AEDT, open/unarchive a 3DL .aedtz model.  You can use the attached or any other model. 2) Right click on Setup1 > Export > HFSS Model... 3) Open the .aedt HFSS project 4) Save the HFSS project Upon trying to save the HFSS project, the below warning message pops up stating "This project was created with a previous version and will be saved in Electronics Desktop 2025 R2." However, the message is wrong since the project was created in 2025R2 and opened in 2025R2.  Opening the .aedt as a text file, we see the version was written as 2021R2, which is a version 4 years old. Perhaps the old version string "Versions(2021, 2)" is written to the exported .aedt file to allow compatibility for opening with older HFSS versions?   In theory, that would allow exported 3DL models from 2025 to be opened in HFSS versions going back as far as 2021R2? But the warning message, as worded, is technically incorrect, and the pop-up is one more click that should not be required when working within the same version. In contrast, a layout component created in 3DL 2025R2, then imported and saved in an HFSS 2025R2 design, does not give any version warning when done with the same version.

Title: Difference in Frequency Prediction from Pre-Stressed Modal Analysis between SMP, MPP (Mesh vs CYCHI)
Message: Difference in Frequency Prediction from Pre-Stressed Modal Analysis between SMP, MPP (Mesh vs CYCHI) User reported that "We are Getting Different Frequencies when using Different Windows Machines for a Pre-Stress Cyclic Symmetry Modal Analysis with Force Sticking Contacts". The difference was very large: 653 Hz (PowerWulf) vs 430 Hz (MyComputer). One machine is local machine "MyComputer". The other machine is remote cluster "PowerWulf". Attached solver output files were the "solve.out" from these two machines.  These two machines used different MPI. MyComputer used Intel-MPI while PowerWulf used MS-MPI. I tried both MPIs to run user's model in my computer. Both predicted the same results: 430 Hz.  Different MPP decomposition method is used on these two machines. MyComputer used MESH while PowerWulf used CYCHI. Then I tried different MPP decomposition method: MESH vs CYCHI using a MAPDL command in my machine. CYCHI gave the same results as PowerWulf and MESH gave the same results as MyComputer. See attached slides. User and I had a discussion on the results. We all think that the natural frequency predicted by CYCHI decomposition is more realistic. Mechanical seems to have an automatic algorithm to pick the decomposition method based upon the model size and computer memory size. Now for a model with Cyclic Symmetry and Rotational Velocity BC, should we force it using CYCHI decomposition method if distributed solve is used? Finally, if we run the same model without using Distributed Solve in my computer, it gave the same results as the one with Distributed Solve -> MESH. This is confusing, since I guess it should give the same results as CYCHI decomposition. Please check.  User's original model with results is   here   (11 GB) User's model without results is   3600RPM Test Powerwulf pts-no-results.wbpz   (6 GB) My modified file with CYCHI decomposition is   here   (3 GB) My modified file with without Distributed Solve is   here   (1.5 GB)

Title: Copied Components lose local coordinate systems assigned and cannot be read into new model
Message: Copied Components lose local coordinate systems assigned and cannot be read into new model This has to do with Icepak components that are needed to assemble a package in full. Currently, a user must read in a PCB for the detailed traces, create a die block as a placeholder, create a CTM V1 or CTM V2 for the regular dies and create a 3DIC for said assemblies. Each is created based on the original origin definition and/or based on a surface coordinate system if creating on a die surface (source form CSV). These can be grouped, but the groups cannot be saved as a component nor can they be copied at once (all components in the group copy and then paste at the same time with regular objects). I've also tried creating local coordinate systems based on the global and assigning them to all objects rather than moving the objects into place. In both the move instance and the local coordinate system instance, copying and pasting the components loses the move and/or the coordinate system in the paste feature and all parts go back to global 0,0,0. The part "disassembles" and the user needs a schematic to rebuild. Please look at the attached model. AssembledPackage design is the original Icepak model with the coordinate systems assigned to the components. TestPass is the exact components copied/pasted into another design. In that design, all local coordinate systems are not recreated/reassigned and you can see the poor assembly.

Title: TAU Mesh Ignores Model Resolution Mesh Setting
Message: TAU Mesh Ignores Model Resolution Mesh Setting Similar to just submitted defect 1326699 where the TAU mesh ignores surface approximation mesh operations (normal deviation and maximum surface deviation), this submission is to report that the TAU mesher also ignores Model Resolution mesh operations.  Please see 1326699 for detailed descriptions of the model. An almost identical model setup is used as in 1326699. The difference is that the explored variable is the Model Resolution mesh operation with different values instead of a surface approximation mesh operation.   Box2/Circle2, Box3/Circle3, Box4/Circle4, and Box5/Circle5 have Model Resolution mesh operations applied to them of  0.01mm, 0.02mm, 0.05mm, and 0.1mm respectively. As expected, the Classic mesher has mostly sequentially decreasing mesh size as the Model Resolution size gets bigger.  There is a defective mesh in the corner of Box2 however, that should not change the conclusion that the Classic mesher is utilizing the prescribed model resolution settings on a per object basis.  Note the tetrahedra counts going from 434 for Box1 to 75 for Box5. In contrast, the TAU mesher in design 2 TAUModelResolution appears to ignore Model Resolution mesh operations. Design  3 TAUNoMeshOperations  is the same as  2 TAUModelResolution  except that the mesh operations have been deleted.  Indeed, the mesh is identical between the two, verifying that the TAU mesher ignores Model Resolution mesh operations. Model Resolution mesh operations, similar to Surface Approximation mesh operations, can be used to great effect with substantially reducing models to only electrically significant geometry with the Classic mesher.  These methods reduce solve time and RAM usage. The TAU mesher currently allows these mesh operations to be applied, but ignores them, and also does not notify the user that they are being ignored.

Title: Structural Optimization - Correction on doc for 'Move Limit'
Message: Structural Optimization - Correction on doc for 'Move Limit' The issue was reported by a Channel Partner on behalf of a customer. According to the doc : "Total Move Limit: This property enables you to define how far each node can move in total . It must be defined in length units, for example three times the element size. By default, this property is set to Program Controlled. Select the Manual option to change the value." According to this, the Move Limit is enforced to the displacement of each node . However, after some discussion with development it seems that the Move Limit is compared against the average displacement of all nodes . The two statements are not the same, and the documentation should be updated to avoid any confusion. Note: Please review whether this is also needed for "Move Limit Per Iteration". Thanks!

Title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1: VBScript Component "GetDirectory" returns different results depending on how you load the workflow
Message: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1: VBScript Component "GetDirectory" returns different results depending on how you load the workflow This one was reported by a customer to Subodh, for reference. To begin, the legacy Script component for MCD had built-in functions to access things related to the current MCD process's object, via the COM API calls. These were handy, but unfortunately were not available in the current CAM version of the VBScript. However, the customer reported to Subodh that using the following code: Option Explicit Sub Run      Dim objFSO, objFolder      Set objFSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")      Set objFolder = objFSO.GetFolder(".")      MCdirectory = objFolder.Path End Sub Sometimes he would get the expected result (a string for the directory path his workflow resided in), but sometimes it would instead be the path for the MCD installation directory.  Through testing, Subdoh narrowed it down to *how* you open the workflow. If you launch it by double-clicking on the saved workflow pxcz file, then when you run that component, it would return the directory that the workflow was saved in. However, if instead you launch MCD from the Start Menu / Program Files menu, then load the workflow from the UI there, then the component would return the directory for the MCD installation.  Subodh also reported that if he converted that VBScript component to a PACZ and hosted it in MCRE, then the string reports the installation directory for MCRE, not the analyses path location of the pacz file. Is the above behavior a bug, or not? I feel that it is; ModelCenter should switch the working directory to that of the currently loaded workflow regardless of how that workflow was loaded - and at the very least, having the behavior go one way sometimes and another other times leads to inconsistent behavior. Alternatively, adding back some of the functions that used to be present to access the MCD process / object via the API would work too, if they provided consistent results.  I've attached a much simpler example of the customer's workflow, that just has the one VBScript component, that I used to reproduce the behavior. ?

Message: Monitor value affected by number of cores with LiveGX CPU solver The attached very simple model shows a dependence of a heat flux monitor on the number of cores on which the LiveGX CPU solver is run.  The heat flow is predominantly in the X direction, from a high to a low temperature face, and the geometry is rectangular and so it will probably show up differences.  That is why I have given the bug a medium priority.  There is a monitor for average heat flux, Avg. Heat Flux 1, on the low temperature face.  There is also a monitor on the solid thermal body for the heat flux in the X direction,  Avg. X Heat Flux 2. When the simulation is run on 1 core, the monitor for heat flux on the face has a similar value to the value in its details plot and the value on the body (Fig. 1). When it runs on 4 cores, the value of the heat flux on the face is quite significantly lower than the details plot and the monitor on the body (Fig.2). The default for LiveGX CPU is 4 cores. In both cases energy is converged to about 2.4e-08. The issue is also seen in v251 SP1 but not in V242 SP1. Fig. 1:  LiveGX CPU on 1 core - Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 agrees with the details plot and is similar to Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body Fig. 2:  LiveGX CPU on 4 cores -  Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 (3.36e4 W/m^2) is lower than the last value in the details plot (4.03e4 W/m^2) and than Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body

Title: GUI - Vegter material: Variable Young Modulus not supported in the solver
Message: GUI - Vegter material: Variable Young Modulus not supported in the solver Hello, The LSDYNA solver only supports the Young modulus to be defined as a curve or a value. There is currently no option to define the Young modulus as "Variable", using the parameters Saturation and Saturation rate.  However, the GUI still supports this option.  To avoid issues in the material card creation, the option "Variable" should be disabled from the dropdown of the Young Modulus when the user selects Vegter as the Yield Criterion.  In the attachment, you can find the material card to be imported into Ansys Forming. You can add it to your library. When you click Runner to create the input files to the solver, it should throw an error "error in material creation" BR, Pablo

Title: Custom Verilog-A component doesn't extrapolate in HB simulation
Message: Custom Verilog-A component doesn't extrapolate in HB simulation I am trying to make an "Ansys only" workflow out of a similar workflow I used before I joined Ansys. There, we used HFSS + Keysight ADS for the HB simulation and ADS's SDD (Symbolically Defined Device) component. I found out that Verilog-A can be used to make an equivalent of such an SDD component in Ansys Circuit, so I created one ("0 Verilog component only"). It is a voltage-dependent resistor and capacitor connected in parallel, with C(U) and R(U) values taken from a lookup table. The last U value from the lookup table is around 5.5V. When a voltage source is swept at 13.56MHz in  "0 Verilog component only," it can extrapolate the C and R values beyond 5.5V. But if a port (with 50ohm termination) is used instead, the HB simulation fails. When an S-parameter block from HFSS, along with some lumped elements, is connected to the Verilog-A component ("1 Dynamic link"), the HB simulation fails as soon as the input voltage to the entire system (at PCD port) exceeds the value corresponding to 5.5V at the Verilog-A component (around 14.52V). Extrapolation is not possible, and the entire HB simulation fails. @Tony Donisi  and I tried changing some HB settings, but to no avail. If passivity on the dynamic link is enforced (IFPV), AEDT crashes. Due to the large archive (7.5GB), I cannot upload it with solutions, but you can try to reproduce the crash if you simulate on your side (or let me know how to provide the solved project). Since the DC point seems problematic, I exported the S-matrix from HFSS and manually deleted the DC point, then imported that SnP into Circuit ("2 SnP no DC point"). Enforcing passivity doesn't make AEDT crash here, but extrapolation is still impossible and HB simulation again fails. Please look into this, as it is an important topic for a customer (IFX) and could potentially displace their workflow with ADS (which can extrapolate the C and R values). Thank you very much in advance.

Title: ModelCenter 25R2 RC Foxtrot: MSC Nastran QuickWrap throws misleading error when output file is missing
Message: ModelCenter 25R2 RC Foxtrot: MSC Nastran QuickWrap throws misleading error when output file is missing In the scenario where you have licensing for MSC Nastran configured incorrectly, upon running your component, you will not get an output file to parse as expected, because the software did not run correctly in order to generate it. This is the error message you get though: Failed Component: Model.MSC Nastran An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper Line: 90 Source: "   caeOutstress3p op2.parse();" Reason: com.phoenix int.cae.ParsingException: com.vki.VKIException: An operation failed in current state Library not opened I feel that it is "misleading" to the user, or at the least feels like leading them with a red herring, to have a "Library not opened" error compared to a "missing file" sort of error message.  For what it's worth, I tried the same setup in MCD 25R1, and the error message was the same. It's probably been around for a while. What happened? : When MSC Nastran licensing is configured incorrectly, running the component does not generate the expected output file. Instead, the user receives a misleading error message indicating "Library not opened" rather than a "missing file" error. What should have happened? : The error message should clearly indicate that the output file is missing due to incorrect licensing configuration (or at least acknowledge that it is missing). Where does it occur? : MSC Nastran component in ModelCenter Desktop v25R1 and v25R2. How often does it occur? : Always, when licensing is configured incorrectly, or when there's some other sort of failure that results in the output file not being generated. Repro Steps : Configure MSC Nastran licensing incorrectly. Run the MSC Nastran component. Observe the error message: "Failed Component: Model.MSC Nastran An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper Line: 90 Source: 'caeOutstress3p op2.parse();' Reason: com.phoenix int.cae.ParsingException: com.vki.VKIException: An operation failed in current state Library not opened." Environment Details : OS version : All Windows Application version/build number : ModelCenter Desktop v25R1 and v25R2 Expected vs. Actual Behavior : Expected Behavior : The error message should indicate that the output file is missing due to incorrect licensing configuration (or at least acknowledge that it is missing). Actual Behavior : The error message indicates "Library not opened," which is misleading. As a comparison, here is the error message I get in 25R2 when I try to parse a non-existing ASCII text file: Failed Component: Model.MSC Nastran An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper Line: 111 Source: "   rowFieldOuttest out txt.parse();" Reason: java.io.FileNotFoundException: C:\Users\tester\Desktop\MSC Nastran\61c289ec-a1af-4759-a8f5-e7a9e18fbc1f\test. (The system cannot find the file specified)

Title: ThermalAdaptor move/copy issues
Message: ThermalAdaptor move/copy issues We've had issues recently and prior where customers seem to not have the Thermal Ribbon installed in Spaceclaim after installing TD. To me it seems this is most likely caused by users not running as admin, but there are other issues as well. I'll layout some of what I've seen. As far as I understand, in the TD installer, somewhere in there it runs the ThermalAdaptor.bat file, which tries to delete old versions of the Thermal Adaptor from the legacy location (C:\ProgramData) and then finally creates a CRTech directory in v242\scdm\Addins, which it gets to by navigative up a few levels from the TD install location and then moves the ThermalAdaptor folder from TD install directory to the Addins\CRTech folder. I think when customers don't use admin rights to install, either the directory creation doesn't work or the move command doesn't work and in the end they don't have the Thermal Ribbon and the ThermalAdaptor folder will remain in the ThermalDesktop install location. Would you be able to test whether this actually occurs when installing Thermal Desktop as non-admin? The other thing that I have encountered is users that install TD in locations other than C:\Program Files, for example a user today needed to install TD on their user account because they didn't have admin rights. He still had issue with the ThermalAdaptor and had to manually copy (or he could have run the batch script I think). This would be another good thing to test, see what happens when TD is installed on a user account vs C: Happy to chat more about this if you have questions.

Title: Ocean load at non-zero plane causes incorrect internal pressure
Message: Ocean load at non-zero plane causes incorrect internal pressure As part of a project for Wood Group I'm helping them move to from 16/8's to 288's etc.   There current modelling practice is to model the mudline at 0 in Z - i.e. sitting on the XY plane.  As such I've been testing a model to understand the use of the Ocean loading to define External pressure and the use of the internal fluid density.    In my test model I simply have a line of 288's on the sea floor running in X.   For the purposes of test the internal density is set to be different that if the external sea water such that I know the right density is being used.  I also set the pipe density to zero just for checking the reactions.   I do not define face 1 and face 2 loads.     I set the value of face 3 to be free surface location Sea Depth is 100m.   As such expected Rho-g-h loading should be  Internal=768.75*9.81*100=754140 External = 1025*9.81*100=1000525  From Ocdata command if the mean sea level is not a 0 then Zms1 should be used. So with a mudline following on OCADATA Depth=100 zmsl=100 Also for pressures -  SFE Face 3 = 100 I get the following reported pressures via smisc, 61 and 62 Internal = 1508300 - i.e double External =  100525 Change zmsl to zero and I get  Internal =  754140 External = 0  To my mind this is a defect.    If set the mudloor to be -100 and leave zmsl to zero it works fine.    Likewise if I don't define the ocean I get the correct internal pressure based on the Z value on face 3.   In that case I manually define the external pressure via face 2.   My workaround for the project will to set the mean sea level at zero and have the pipeline on the sea bed at -Z to work with the Ocean loading I'm attaching my test model.  It is set with zloc (on line 22) at zero and zmsl at 100 (line 53) and Ocean loading is included.  Set skip=1 on line 49 to remove ocean loading Please advise. Thanks Mark Leddin

Title: Validity of electrical simulation with a suppressed body depends on component structure
Message: Validity of electrical simulation with a suppressed body depends on component structure Not new in v261.  Also seen in v252. The detection of contacts for an electrical simulation appears to be less straightforward than for thermal or structural simulations. The attached two projects saved in v252 that contain models derived from the mixer tee example simulation.  The component structures of the model differ. MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - fluid body and pipe bodies are contained in components at the same level (Fig.1) MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - pipe bodies at top level and fluid body in a component (Fig. 2) If an electrical simulation is set up on the pipe bodies with the fluid body suppressed, the simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco is in the Cannot solve state with an error message, Unconnected bodies located as in Fig. 3.  A similar simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco, however, is valid (Fig. 4). The animation shown in Fig. 5 shows that if physics auto update is disabled for the invalid simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco, the simulation state changes to valid although the message is still displayed.  Moreover, the simulation can be solved and the solution appears to be similar to that obtained from the valid simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco (Figs 6 and 7). If the fluid body in MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco is deleted, the simulation is valid and can be solved giving a solution similar to those obtained from the other set-ups. In addition to the projects, I have attached zipped working directories for setting up the simulations on the two models with the fluid body suppressed and MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco with the fluid body deleted. Fig. 1:  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco Fig. 2:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco Fig. 3:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body. Error message about unconnected bodies Fig. 4:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body. Simulation is valid Fig. 5:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body followed by switching off physics auto update Fig. 6:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body with physics auto update disabled can be solved Fig. 7:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body.  Solution is as for  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco with auto update disabled Fig. 8:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with fluid body deleted - no messages and solution similar to previous

Title: Improving Error Handling: Targeting Specific Exceptions
Message: Improving Error Handling: Targeting Specific Exceptions DESCRIPTION: The objectif is to improve error message handling by intercepting more specific exceptions Data : \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\VSS\Bug 1177603 VSS - Camera Ground Truth with Fisheye camera error message displayed is incorrect Notes : This situation directly impacts our ability to improve logging ( Example: bug 1177603 ) Exceptions used in component APIs (not product APIs) generally follow C# framework guidelines ( ArgumentException ,   OutOfRangeException ,   OperationException , etc.), with occasional use of custom exceptions in specific cases. There is no clearly defined or structured architectural approach to error handling across components. Steps to reproduce for VSS : Set the log level of VSS and VSSSpawner to   INFO Launch provided scenario with VssTester ./VRXPERIENCE.SensorsSimulator -p 5050 Imagine.Pre.VssTester -p 5050 -s Scenario.json The error message generated is   not clear on what the error is, from a customer point of view, the cause of the error is not given here and cannot be understood. 2024-11-27 10:40:13,620 [18] ERROR SupervisionActivity-CreateAbortedMessage()  Failure detected on ISensorActivity<ICameraSensorService> located at {localhost:13001}: An error occurred while creating sensor. Couldn't create camera sensor with id 'cam3 fisheye'. 2024-11-27 10:40:13,636 [18] ERROR SimulationInterfaceActivity-MoveNext()  Failure detected on ISensorActivity<ICameraSensorService>. Closing simulation interface server... 2024-11-27 10:40:13,639 [18] ERROR SimulationCommandRpcService-MoveNext()  LoadCommand encountered an error. If you change the log level to   ALL   you get the real error underneath which is  " Camera Ground Truth production is not available for Fisheye camera. " That error is clearer, the simulation parameter defined for the sensor are not available. The user is aware the parameter are incorrect and not wondering why the sensor couldn't be created. The objective is to improve error handling by capturing more specific exceptions, so that we can address the issue and fix the bug. Expected behavior: For the current product bug :  VSS can retrieve the root cause of the error :   " Camera Ground Truth production is not available for Fisheye camera. " For the future :  A clear list of exception types used in component API. Title: One configuration of CHT simulation with an internal fan cannot be solved in Explore
Message: One configuration of CHT simulation with an internal fan cannot be solved in Explore The attached projects contain fluid thermal simulations with an Internal Fan condition based on the mixer tee sample model.   The fans are located in different inlet arms and both can be solved in Explore, as shown in Figs 1 and 2. If the outer bodies are unsuppressed so that the models are CHT, the simulation in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco fails (Fig. 3) but that in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan2.dsco can be solved successfully (Fig. 4).  The file (attached) contains the error ERROR Couldn't get unique cell zone and/or inlet face zone id associated with volumetric internal fan Exclusion of the solid thermal body surrounding the internal fan in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco allows solver to run. Fig. 1:  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco Fig. 2:  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan2.dsco Fig. 3:  CHT simulation for model in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco produces error Fig. 4:     CHT simulation for model in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan2.dsco can be solved successfully Fig. 5   CHT simulation for model in  MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco can be solved if solid thermal body around fan condition is excluded Fig. 6:  CHT simulation in MixerTeeSliced FluidThermal Fan1.dsco with all solid thermal bodies can be solved in Refine

Title: Perturbation in moment calculated from Rolling Resistance Type C Model while passing boundary triangles
Message: Perturbation in moment calculated from Rolling Resistance Type C Model while passing boundary triangles Lucas from CADFEM shared two test cases and one PDF summarising their findings. They are attached to this ticket: "rolling resistance.pdf" and "528872 rolling resistance.zip". The first test case is with finer boundary mesh, where they found the issue. Then, they tested with the coarse mesh version and the issue was not observed. The force value was at the expected value. I ran these cases as well and confirmed the issue. Then, I modified the coarse mesh case and created a version with a single particle only (attached as "Rollreibung coarseMesh rollTypeC 1particle.rocky archive"). I increased the simulation time from 1 s to 2 s and modified the motion frames accordingly. I did this test to see what happens in the coarse mesh case when the particle crosses the triangle boundary. This showed that actually the force is at the expected value until the particle crosses the boundary. Then it starts diverging from this value while it is passing it. Please see the plot below, where this issue can be seen after t~1.7 s. Development; QA Process; Triaged

Title: Specify Total Voltage option in Electrolysis is not working properly
Message: Specify Total Voltage option in Electrolysis is not working properly @Chao Han  cc   @Omkar Champhekar   @Anil Wakale   @Saurabh Patwardhan   Hello Chao, I worked with a client's PEMWE model with a dry cathode and attempted to run it for U=1.8V from the initialization file. It took me a little while to set up all the monitors and plots that I typically use. I run it overnight and it is going in the right direction and I am confident that I can converge it even better.  The mass balance between the water consumed and total mass of gases generated, is getting closer but fluctuate a bit. I will experiment with the pseudo-transient time stepping strategy for solution steering to find out whether a better steady-state convergence can be reached, or whether we are dealing with a larger time-scale transience somewhere in PTLs or PTL/channel regions or elsewhere. This might as well be the case. Having said that, I noticed an issue with the model. Typically, I monitor the volume integrals of transfer currents in the catalysts and they match up well. At the same time, I monitor the surface integrals of the wall-normal current density component at terminals. To my surprise they failed to match Please disregard the units difference between the last two plots. The transfer current integrals were in [A/(m3) * m3] whereas the last plot has inconsistency of units [A/(cm2) * m2]. I am more concerned about the difference of currents on terminals as shown in the last plot. The conservation of charge should be satisfied and I started searching for a leak, given that convergence was not perfect but it was on the right track.  To discover this, I plotted the current density plots on all outer surfaces. Please see results below: The flange side of the catalyst is the place where the leak takes place, but the boundary conditions are greyed out, because the voltage was specified in the electrolysis panel. A similar situation is observed on the other side: At the same time, this should not be the case, because the voltage and the terminals are specified in the Potential/Electrochemistry Electrolysis panel: This looks like a juicy bug to me. I will use the workaround for the time being but it feels that it is important to find the source of this bug as it can resurface unexpectedly on bigger, more complex geometries and remain unnoticed for a long time. I will share the files via the secure file transfer facility. Kind regards, Aleksey.

Title: ModelCenter STK Plugin Not Creating a Relative Path
Message: ModelCenter STK Plugin Not Creating a Relative Path MC 25r1, STK 12.10. Found during Digital Engineering Workshop planning. STK Help Document:  What's New Exert:  STK Help Whats New 12.8 Analyzer: The STK Model Center plugin now attempts to store the STK scenario location as a relative path so that you can zip the model center workspace and move it to a different location without having to relocate the STK scenario at startup after moving. This feature will work when the STK scenario is stored under the Model Center workspace location path. The Model Center user can modify the scenario associated with an STK Processing block in a Model Center model. STK will load the updated scenario when it executes the processing block. You should make changes to the STK scenario from within Model Center by using the Configure STK processing block method, to ensure passing consistency checks performed during configuration. This will alleviate runtime errors that may occur if you modify the STK scenario outside Model Center in such a way that the processing block input and outputs will be invalid in some way. Steps to reproduce: Setup a working directory ModelCenter Workflow.pxcz STK Folder STK .vdf (included in attached files) Open the MC workflow  Add in STK Component Plugin Point to the .vdf file Choose any variables from the scenario file Select ok Save the MC workflow Attempt to copy and move the workflow and STK component elsewhere and run. STK component will prompt you to select a new scenario file. Rename the original working directory STK folder as the plugin hard codes the path.
