Title: Index of Fan Pressure Rise monitor is not incremented when several are created
Message: Index of Fan Pressure Rise monitor is not incremented when several are created New in v252.  The issue did not occur with the Operating Pressure monitor in v251. As shown in Fig. 1, when a series of Fan Pressure Rise monitors are created in immediate succession, the indices are not incremented.  For other variables they are incremented as shown for Volume Flow in Fig. 2.  It seems that the issue is associated with the creation of the monitor after Fan Pressure Rise.  In Fig. 3 we see that a monitor for Volume Flow created after a monitor for Fan Pressure Rise retains the index of the previous monitor.  Variables other than Volume Flow are also affected. When the simulation is duplicated, the indices of the monitors in the duplicate simulation are incremented. The issue is also seen with internal fans (Fig. 4). I've attached: a v252 project containing a simulation with three 2-d fans (Simple-3Fans.dsco) a v251 project containing a simulation with three internal fans (Simple-3IntFans v251.dsco)   Fig. 1:  Fan Pressure Rise monitors created in succession - index not incremented Fig. 2:  Volume Flow rate monitors created in succession - index is incremented Fig. 3:  Monitor for Volume Flow rate created after monitor for Fan Pressure - index not incremented for Volume Flow Fig. 5:  Fan Pressure Rise monitors on internal fans - not incremented Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Feedback Iterator is buggy
Message: Feedback Iterator is buggy The feedback iterator seems buggy. In the properties, the "Latest Delta Temperature %" does not get printed until all iterations are done, and even then it only gets printed if the value is less than the "Target Delta Temperature %." If it reaches the max iterations and the value is internally greater, then it still prints "not available." Also "Results > Clean up solutions" in Maxwell sometimes sets the "Iterations" Completed" back to zero and sometimes it does not. It's random so hard to produce, but try it 3 times or so. If it fails, and you try to update the feedback iterator when the iterations completed are at the "Max Iterations" then you'll get an error. The only way to solve this is to delete/recreate the feedback iterator and link again to the setup cell of the Maxwell system. Also, Mechanical reports the following error if open during the feedback iterator updates, even when the iterations seem to work properly: "One or more files from the upstream system are missing. The files may not have been copied over or saved with the project." So it's best to close Mechanical during the iterations to avoid the error. There are no graceful exits. Mechanical crashes easy. 1. If you have cut out the bodies from the vacuum enclosure in Maxwell, this is not proper setup and will crash Mechanical, when using the feedback iterator, with no useful error. 2. If a body for temperature feedback in Mechanical is not meshed with pure tetrahedrals, it crashes Mechanical. This is probably something that just needs to be added to documentation, unless it's not intended to work this way, in which case, it needs fixing. In both cases above Mechanical solves but crashed at the point of sending data back to Maxwell. The crash will not happen if turn off "export after solve" on the imported load folder. There will be a "ExportDiagnostics ### ####.dat" file in the solution directory meant for error reporting but it's useless because it just has one line when the export fails and when it works it just reports number of cores and export time. See attached model, but it's just a simple model to work with to repeat the problems above. It's not unique in any way to demonstrate the problems.

Title: CASE 00440305 - KARL STORZ - Diffusion coefficient definition in UG and Material Editor
Message: CASE 00440305 - KARL STORZ - Diffusion coefficient definition in UG and Material Editor CUSTOMER BUG User Priority   P2 - Medium No Available Bypass DESCRIPTION: Data :   "Simplify large document at much as possible" No dataset required. Notes : Regression (if so, last known build/version where it was working): Steps to reproduce: Require a complete review and validation of the physics in section  " Give particles specifications " and how the scattering variation is defined in the material editor: In the UG the   Diffusion coefficient   is the inverse of the mean free path : σ d =1/ｌ with ｌ being the mean free path. In literature the scattering coefficient is defined as the probability of a photon being scattered per unit path length. Therefore, what the UG labels as the "diffusion coefficient" is, by standard definition, the scattering coefficient . In literature the diffusion coefficient (D) is defined as ( Section 2.3 ): μa​ (absorption coefficient) and μs′​ (reduced scattering coefficient) both have units of m−1. Therefore the denominator has units of m−1 and therefore D the unit m. The standard physics definition of the diffusion coefficient D is fundamentally different from the quantity the User Guide calls the "diffusion coefficient" σ d ​ . Expected behavior: What is called “diffusion coefficient” ( σ d ​ ) multiple times in the UG paragraph should be actually the scattering coefficient ( μ s ​ )? In the material editor the scattering variation is defined with the label "diffusion coefficient (mm-1)" which is not aligned with the unit from the literature.  Customer would like an answer how the term "diffusion coefficient" is defined in SPEOS in relation to the material properties and to what extent the scattering coefficient is taken into account. Customer would like a clarification whether the diffusion coefficient in the UG and Speos material definition actually refers to the scattering coefficient or the reduced scattering coefficient? Minor enhancements: The symbol choice σ d ​ is unusual and confusing for the customer. Standard notation is: μ a ​ = absorption coefficient μ s ​ = scattering coefficient μ t ​ = μ a ​ + μ s ​ = total attenuation coefficient Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): Windows 10 Version :  GPU :  GPU Driver version : CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause   (if regression set a   SPEOS REGRESSION   tag): Solution : Impacts   (if there is a risk set a   SPEOS RISK HIGH ,   SPEOS RISK MEDIUM , or   SPEOS RISK LOW   tag): Notes : Validation: Support: Doc : (NMN - 25/08/2025) KIL Documented in UG LAB 2025R2.2 Diffusion coefficient label replaced by Scattering coefficient. Title: Default Mesh for IE/Hybrid Dipole More Than 15x Slower to Run Than Common Sense Settings, 10x Slower than FEM with Defaults
Message: Default Mesh for IE/Hybrid Dipole More Than 15x Slower to Run Than Common Sense Settings, 10x Slower than FEM with Defaults This submission might be an enhancement request, but I am submitting as a defect because the default meshing for a simple dipole using the IE/hybrid solver is unacceptable from both an efficiency and consistency perspective. The IE/hybrid solved dipole with default mesh settings is 15 times slower than an IE/hybrid  mesh that uses common sense mesh settings, and over 10 times slower than the same model run in FEM.  A dipole is one of the simplest and most likely test models for a user to attempt using AEDT.  However, most users never plot mesh or have a concept of what an appropriate mesh should be, so will accept the very unnecessary slow simulation time as an HFSS metric that makes our IE/hybrid solve capabilities look bad compared to other tools. The MoM type solvers in AEDT (IE, Q3D ACRL, etc.) have significantly different mesh requirements than FEM.  MoM is MUCH more sensitive to mesh quality (aspect ratio) and element count than FEM.   In the attached project, IE Dipole 2025R2.aedt , there are three IE designs (1, 2, and 3).  From left to right we have: Z oriented dipole with default mesh settings (IE) Y oriented dipole with default mesh settings (IE) Z oriented dipole with Classic mesher and 6 sided mesh due to manual mesh settings (IE) The design summary demonstrates an extreme difference between the final mesh and solve time for the default settings and the model with custom mesh settings.  What should take 32 seconds (design 3) takes 8min13sec (design 1) with default mesh settings. IE Designs  (mesh count and solve times are up to 15x different, and default settings yield over order of magnitude worse performance) Design Name                                 Dipole Orientation           Initial Mesh    Passes      Final Mesh   Solve Time    Slowdown 1 IE DefaultMesh Z                                    Z                                 7944                 3               13426              8:13           15.4x 2 IE DefaultMesh Y                                    Y                                 2514                 2                3268              1:57           3.7x 3 IE CustomMesh Z                                  Z (mesh ops)                744                  2                  968              0:32           reference Also, in the attached project there are three FEM designs (4, 5, and 6) that replicate the setup of the IE designs, but solving as FEM.  From left to right we have: 4. Z oriented dipole with default mesh settings (FEM) 5. Y oriented dipole with default mesh settings (FEM) 6. Z oriented dipole with Classic mesher and 6 sided mesh due to manual mesh settings (FEM) The FEM design summary demonstrates that for exactly the same setup as designs 1-3, but solving in FEM, the mesh count and solve time is almost the same regardless of default mesh, orientation, or with the custom mesh.   FEM Designs  (all mesh counts and solve times are similar) Design Name                                 Dipole Orientation           Initial Mesh    Passes      Final Mesh   Solve Time     4 FEM DefaultMesh Z                          Z                                 3244                  4              6976               0:40 5 FEM DefaultMesh Y                          Y                                 4733                  3              7581                0:34 6 FEM CustomMesh Z                         Z (mesh ops)              2273                  6              7435                0:46 In summary: *Among the IE/hybrid designs, a dipole takes 15.4x to 3.7x longer to run with default settings than with the common sense custom mesh settings (6 sided cylinder).   *An IE/hybrid vertical dipole is more than 10x slower than the same FEM dipole when both use default mesh settings. *The IE/hybrid model with common sense mesh settings has a faster solve time compared to all of the FEM designs *FEM solve statistics are approximately the same with either default or custom mesh (6 sided cylinder) settings. The goal of this submission is to improve the default mesh for IE/hybrid such that it does not create high aspect ratio, inconsistent, inefficient meshes.  A simple cylinder is not representative of the range of geometries we see, but there should be more intelligence in the IE/hybrid mesher to avoid defaults yielding >10x speed penalties, and for the behavior to be so dependent on orientation.

Title: 'General Error' with Layered Section scoping when body's Material field is undefined
Message: 'General Error' with Layered Section scoping when body's Material field is undefined The issue was reported by a customer for release 2025R2. I've attached a demo Project where the issue is shown. Assume a Surface body with no definition of Thickness or Material. When we scope a Layered Section object to the Surface's body, we cannot proceed with the solution and the Thickness field is highlighted indicating that an input of a thickness value is required prior to Layered Section Scoping. To fix this, a random thickness value is specified, and the Layered Section is re-scoped. When proceeding with the solution, we get a 'general error'. Looking into the ds.dat it seems that the Materials are never sent to the Solver. To fix this, a random Material is assigned to the Surface body prior to the Layered Section scoping, similar to how it was done for the Thickness field. The Thickness and Material definition requirements for the Layered Section scoping aren't written anywhere in the documentation. I would suggest this information is included so that users know about it. If it's possible to also highlight the Material field in Mechanical if it's undefined - similar to how it's done for the Thickness - that'd be great. Thanks! Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Twin Builder: Delay Block Parameters
Message: Twin Builder: Delay Block Parameters In Twin Builder (2025R1) when using a Delay block (found under Basic Elements->Blocks->Discrete Blocks->DELAY) the main input parameters,   Delay Time   and   Samples   only allow numeric input. No variables allowed, as can be seen in the screenshot below. So, my first question is: #1   Why can the Delay block not accept variables as parameter inputs, and can this capability be added or is it a fundamental limitation? Now for the strange behavior. I   was   able to enter variables into the   TS   (sample time) and   Samples   parameters via the Properties window. As shown in the screenshot below. The program did not have an issue with this, and now when the parameters window was opened it would simply show “0” for the   Delay Time   but   Samples   would be reset to “20” which is the default value.   When run, the Delay block will correctly utilize the variables entered for   TS   via the Properties window (using variables), however anything entered for   Samples   will be ignored and run with the default value of 20. So,   as long as I was ok with a sample number of 20, I   could   parameterize the delay time with a variable, and this variable could even be dynamic throughout the simulation.   See below a plot where the sample time   TS   was set using variables as a function of time so the delay grows throughout the simulation as can be seen by the phase/frequency shift. This indicates that there is no fundamental limitation to using variables and even dynamic variables. However the experience entering parameter values via the Properties window is certainly buggy. So my question #2   Can anyone explain this observed behavior or is this a bug?

A workaround is to suppress and then unsuppress the solid thermal bodies (note that one of the bodies in the Fuse component is suppressed in the CHT simulation). Title: Time average of custom property seems off
Message: Time average of custom property seems off Please refer to "Problem 2" reported by CADFEM on the attached PPT for complete analysis. On my end, I have conducted a similar analysis, and this is my reasoning: The ShearAvgSPH custom property is created on SPH: ShearAvgSPH: sum(A[1:t+1])/(t*OUTPUT FREQUENCY) where A is Shear Stress This is a time-averaged shear stress. So, if plotted on an inspector, it should be the actual Shear Stress from the inspector, since it is a single element/value. We should at least see this with a similar magnitude as the Shear Stress grid function, but in fact we don't: Also, note that strangely, the time-averaged property is only available until 4.11 s instead of 5 s.  Deck with results available at \\CDCW16RALLY02\TFSProd\Attachments\Rocky\1332623 QA Process

Title: modelon needs to generate a better error message for error found in d1221132
Message: modelon needs to generate a better error message for error found in d1221132 this is from d1221132 to have modelon generate a better error message when a parameter is assigned a value in a function. from modelon: " It is a problem in the model, on line 530 there is an assign statement that looks like this: index := i;. Title: [AMPP] Plots don't switch to dark theme
Message: [AMPP] Plots don't switch to dark theme Plots in AMPP don't switch to dark theme when the dark theme is selected. Currently angular-plotly.js does not support the standard plotly themes,  https://github.com/plotly/angular-plotly.js/issues/157 . Once this is addressed, the layout.template field can be set to "plotly" for the light theme or "plotly dark" for the dark theme. Predefined plotly theme values:  "plotly", "plotly white", "plotly dark", "ggplot2", "seaborn", "simple white", "none" Another option would be to set plot background and trace colors whenever the theme changes. This could get a bit involved.

Message: AEDT Mechanical: Unable to export deformed mesh into. Case File Hello Dev Team, My customer has following requirement Requirement:   Waveguide filter performance analysis under harsh temp ambient conditions. EM loss of WG filter > Conduction Convection analysis in Icepak > Warpage analysis in Mechanical Structural > EM performance impact of WG filter due to warpage and high temperature. If not, how can we export the deformed mesh from AEDT mechanical so that we can import it to HFSS manually? After my investigation I have ruled out a possibility 1 of direct coupling of deformations from AEDT Mechanical (Structural) to HFSS. We are now exploring the possibility 2 where we exported the deformed mesh as .Case file and imported it in Ensight to view it and convert it into suitable format like STL so that HFSS can import it. Doing so we are facing challenges that even after I export deformed mesh into .Case file, I could see that there is no deformation in mesh after importing it in Ensight. Please check the snippet below Exported the Mesh plot Imported .Case file in Ensight I do not see deformation in Ensight, I feel AEDT Mechanical is not exporting the deformed mesh correctly or it has limitation, or I am missing something. Kindly help me with this. I have attached example model for your reference.

Title: Values for laminate layers change after import and editing
Message: Values for laminate layers change after import and editing After importing a stackup, the values for some laminate layers are not set properly. After editing and saving the layer without changing any values, the values are changed in the stackup table. Steps In order to start from a clean state, delete the laminate.csv file in Sherlock settings, located at C:\Users\<user name>\AppData\Roaming\Sherlock. Launch Sherlock. Enable the "Laminate Resin" Beta Feature. Import the Tutorial Project. Open the Laminate Manager. Import the attached laminate files (LaminateExport EM-892K.csv and LaminateExport MC24P.csv). Note that this can be done prior to importing the project. View the Stackup. Import the attached stackup file (46L Stackup.csv) Laminate layers 72, 76, 80, and 84. Note the values for layer 72: CTExy=14.000 CTEz=60.000 Exy=24.804 Ez=6634 Note the values for the stackup: CTExy=24.472 CTEz=69.382 Exy=25491 Ez=5785 Edit layer 72. The Laminate Material may be set to OAK-MITSUI, POLYMIDE, MC24P. If it isn't, change it to this. Save changes. Results Note the values for layer 72 changed to the following (which happens regardless of whether the material was set): CTExy=24.000 CTEz=25.000 Exy=2000 Ez=2000 Material name does not change for the row if it wasn't changed from importing the OAK-MITUI material. Note the values for the stackup changed to the following: CTExy=24.602 CTEz=68.843 Exy=25525 Ez=5703 There is now an Errors tab at the bottom of the Stackup tab. The error is: Unknown Material name Elite Materials (EMC) FR-4 EM-892K RESIN, using DEFAULT Similar behavior is seen if the stackup is imported prior to importing the laminate file  LaminateExport MC24P.csv. Sometimes when doing it in this order, the material for these laminate layers get set when importing the laminate. Expected The laminate material is always set in the stackup layer in the table and the layer editor after importing the missing laminate material. This is inconsistent and I haven't found a consistent way to get the values to be set. These values would be set automatically when the stackup is imported. There would not be an error. Importing the stackup again after this doesn't change anything. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Part density is not calculated correctly in Sherlock
Message: Part density is not calculated correctly in Sherlock To reproduce this defect, enable "Use Part Body Weight" advanced setting. For SQUARE, ROUND, and MITER corner shape, the same density value is used because it is based off the part weight value set. But, since the corner being cutoff will change the volume/mass, it should be using a different density value if the volume/mass is different. When exported to Mechanical, you can see this difference in the mass of the component being less than the specified weight. But in the ds.dat, you can see that they all use the same density value because they have the same material assigned that all use the same part weight. The component needs updated to the true weight entered or a new part density needs calculated based off the corner shape. Hi, I have manually defined part weight for a component. When I exported the model to Mechanical, it shows a different value than what was defined in Sherlock.  Upon further testing, I realized that it is happening when the corner shape is not square. Could you please check this?  Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Vias missing when importing IPC-2581 in SIwave
Message: Vias missing when importing IPC-2581 in SIwave Vias missing when importing IPC-2581 in SIwave Attached is an .xml file that comes from an IPC export from Altium. When importing into SIwave, some vias are missing. These vias are not missing when importing in HFSS 3D Layout, thus confirming that the issue is not with the Altium export, but the SIwave import. First, to see the correct import in HFSS: 1. Import the IPC file in HFSS 3D Layout 25R1. 2. From List, find the component with name C83CV0CG0 and fit in the screen 3. Perform a cutout around this component (include and clip all nets) 4. It is visible that the vias go from top to bottom: Now to see the wrong import in SIwave: 1. Import the IPC file in SIwave 25R1 2. Using Find Components, search for component named C83CV0CG0 and fit the screen to it 4. Perform a cutout around this component 5. Rotate so that the Z axis is visible. It is easily shown that the vias are not reaching all the way from top to bottom: Since SIwave has some visualization issues when rotating, you can export to HFSS 3D Layout and check that this is true there also. Attached are also zipped versions of the HFSS and SIwave imports. EDIT: The IPC file can't be attache because it exceeds the file limit, please let me know so that I can upload to some folder.

Title: Loading SolveHandlers.xml from Appdata may fail when multiple instances of mechanical are interacting with the file
Message: Loading SolveHandlers.xml from Appdata may fail when multiple instances of mechanical are interacting with the file This is a follow-up on recent cert failure for QK CIT BUILD1 07. The test was intermittently failing due to a timing issue regarding SolveHandlers.xml file. I quick fix was made with pr - PR 612078: Potential fix for cert QK CIT BUILD1 07  which adds handling around the exception being thrown. We need to study why this error is happening and if/how it can be fixed. Below is my email on the topic: Regarding test QK CIT BUILD1 07, I have some updates.   After discussing with @Andrei Marinescu the status of this test, it appears it has been failing inconsistently for quite some time now all the way back to June. This ruled out any changes recently.   After investigating, it appears it is a timing issue when multiple instances of Mechanical are interacting with the following file in appdata at the same time ( AppData\Roaming\Ansys\v261\SolveHandlers.xml )   I tracked the change which I believe to be the cause from a PR from June 10 th addressing bug B1274889 : Pull request 595328: Update JobHandlerManager if xml file is updated through another session. - Repos Pull request 597616: B1274889: CallScript doesn't work if method already defined in JScriptCombined - Repos (follow up)   I may have a temporary fix that Andrei is trying out.   As a resolution, I think there are two options: Revert both PR’s and re-open bug 1274889 until the root cause is investigated more thoroughly and fixed Merge the temporary fix if it is successful and open a new bug to explore a more permanent solution if necessary. Mech-Core-Architecture; Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Missing information on components' nodes/elems format in rst files
Message: Missing information on components' nodes/elems format in rst files The issue was reported by a Channel Partner. According to the doc ( 1.2. Description of the Results File ), in the rst file format for the COMP section, we first have the component type, then the component name, and then a list of nodes / elements of the components. However, for compression purposes, if the list of nodes / elements are in a continuous order from value A to value B, they are reported as A -B in the file format. This logic with the negative sign is not mentioned anywhere in the doc, and can lead to confusion when users try to process the rst files. Please include this information in the doc.

Title: Histogram y-axis label becomes misleading if weight is used
Message: Histogram y-axis label becomes misleading if weight is used In this example, what happens is that the frequency of the bins (i.e. their height) is weighted by Duration : Mean. The heights do not represent Duration : Mean in seconds, but rather the distribution of the particles' mean impact normal velocity weighted based on the mean contact duration of each particle. However, the customer was misled to believe the y-values were actually in seconds, which is not plausible. Thankfully, he realized there was a 6s mean contact duration for a 5s simulation, which does not make sense, but I wonder if it could happen to a not-so-flagrant case. Therefore, please remove this inconsistency from the y-label. Steps to reproduce 1. Run tutorial 4 2. Take inter particle collision Duration and Impact Velocity 3. Plot impact normal velocity on a histogram 4. Use Duration : mean as weight QA Process

Title: HFSS-Icepak: Excitation port shows absurdly high surface loss
Message: HFSS-Icepak: Excitation port shows absurdly high surface loss Customers: RTX, Northrop Grumman, Seattle, etc. In the attached project, please only consider the HFSS design 1a RFpcb 1way.  After solving this design as is, the Radiation> 3D> Antenna parameters shows a total of 1 W incident. Using the field calculator, we can verify that the substrate has ~ 0.776 W volumetric load, while the antenna and the Ground copper surface loads add up to 0.155 W, which gives us a total loss of 0.931 W. So far so good. Now, select all objects in HFSS and copy them. Then create a new Icepak design, and paste the copied geometries from HFSS here. Select all objects in Icepak, and assign an EM Loss from the above HF design. After solving, Icepak shows a total heat loss of ~ 2.78 W instead of 0.931 W. This is because an extra 1.85 W of surface loss comes in from the 2D terminal port surface in HFSS. If you go back to the HFSS design and check with the field calculator, once can verify that the excitation port shows a total surface loss of ~ 1.85 W. This is an absurd result. Following seem problematic: 1. If the 3D>  Antenna parameters  only reports an  incident power of 1 W, how can the port show a much higher loss. 2. Since the port is expected to have 1 W incident, why are we seeing any loss at the port at all. In this simple model, all the input power incident at the port is either useful em, or reflected, or ends up as heat losses as suggested in the 3D> Antenna parameters report. Therefore, the reported loss in the excitation port should be zero. The only resolution seems to be to recognize the port loss as spurious and exclude it from the Icepak design. This loss seems misleading.

Title: ACTDYNA Testing Interface Delamination and Contact Debonding
Message: ACTDYNA Testing Interface Delamination and Contact Debonding Interface Delamination not working  when one or more penta cohesive element is required: Please see attached model " WBLSDYNA Delamination ELFORM Testing 25R1dev . wbpz ". In Interface Delamination Scoping  exclude or include the  related  geometry face where penta elements are required.  ACP Model with Interface layers - Contact Debonding cannot get scoped to Bonded Contact with Scoping Method Pre-Generated Interface: See attached  model: " WBLSDYNA Delamination withACP Testing 25R1dev . wbpz " System B. Suppress Interface Delamination object and unsuppress Contact Debonding object and Bonded Contact. Contact Debonding Scope does not allow scoping the Bonded Contact.  Cohesive Elements not shown in Mechanical GUI: Could there be a way to expose them as a mesh feature. This would enable to do postprocessing on cohesive elements in Mechanical. Workaround is either LSPP or perhaps through PyAnsys environment. Can be checked with any of attached models. Visualization issues  of deformation plot  when Cohesive Elements in a single body (ACP): After Cohesive Elements are failed: Deformation Plot with missing visualization on solid element face adjacent to the cohesive elements.  See attached  model: " WBLSDYNA Delamination withACP Testing 25R1dev . wbpz " before cohesive element failure after cohesive element failure Visualization issues  of stress plot  when Cohesive Elements in a single body (ACP): After Cohesive Elements are failed: Stress plot with where solid element nodes on one side of the cohesive element layer are connected to the Solid element nodes to the other side of the cohesive element layer. There should be a gap instead.  See attached  model: " WBLSDYNA Delamination withACP Testing 25R1dev . wbpz " before cohesive element failure after cohesive element failure Time History Output Controls when specific time history output is selected e.g. Nodal Interface Forces (NCFORC), then *DATABASE NCFORC is present twice in the k-file. Leads to a warning when opening in LSPP. Seems all *DATABASE items are written when using program controlled anyway. When manually specifying shouldn't the default just removed from the k-file? Motivation: This allows to define a predefined zone within plies are not connected e.g. to model a predefined defect which is common practice e.g. in aerospace to account for manufacturing defects.   Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Maxwell DCBiasedEddyCurrent solver fails if Thin Layer Conductor is defined
Message: Maxwell DCBiasedEddyCurrent solver fails if Thin Layer Conductor is defined Maxwell Eddy Current solver supports thin layer boundary conditions for conductive/high permeability materials, thus allowing shell element adoption for shielding applications. For thin structures immersed in DC fields, like in magnetic signature applications, this feature would be of great benefit allowing to save time and resources. If Thin Layer conductor is defined in DCBiased Eddy Current solver and the solution is started, the DC part fails, probably because the magnetostatic solver does not support it. Please find in attachment a simple example where EC solver solves successfully but DCBiasedEC solver fails. Warm Regards, Tiziana

Title: Solar Irradiation model - Change in Absorption coefficient and refractive index is having no effect on temperature field due to identical (zero) net radiation source to energy equation
Message: Solar Irradiation model - Change in Absorption coefficient and refractive index is having no effect on temperature field due to identical (zero) net radiation source to energy equation When using Solar Irradiation model,  changing the absorption coefficient and refractive index is resulting in identical temperature field even for a wide range of material property values. Post-processing shows that although volumetric emission and absorption is changing each time, net radiation source value for the energy equation is identical resulting in no change in temperature field. The goal is to see the effect of changing glass material properties on the temperature field on the glass and interior opaque objects in order to choose the correct glass material. This issue is very critical for enterprise account like Tesla and for their Vehicle Thermal team to develop simulation workflow for their camera systems, as well as Magic Leap, Garmin and many other customers. Relevant case and solution fdat files are attached.

Title: UI issue in Winding definition for IM1PH
Message: UI issue in Winding definition for IM1PH There are couple of UI issues on the winding of single-phase induction motor, that one of our channel partner (DRD) customer pointed out during his Evalution of MotorCAD: As you can see on the attached model (and on the image below) that the first column is missing the header name, I checked the default model, and it doesn't seem to have this issue, so I am not sure what cause this in the customer's model. Also, the Main column seems to show the number of turns for the Auxiliary winding (even in the default model). I think this can be improved by having two columns the first one for Main winding and the second one for Auxiliary winding, instead of Phase 1 and Main.      Entering or modifying the coil definition on the table is not always consistent and there are several issues that I noticed, I have recorded some snaps to show some of those behavior:  The numbers change to the first entry on the table (Slot 1 Go) once you select some of cells. Once you move out of the cell, the number resets to the original value (see Number Change.mp4)   When you enter a number on cell and then move out without pressing Enter, sometimes it takes that entry and sometimes it doesn't, and it will reset to another number (see Number reset uncorrectly.mp4 and Second time it worked Fine.mp4)  Sometimes even when you change the number and press enter, it doesn't work at the first try and reset the number but works at the second try. Those issues I mentioned are not repeatable, But I would say definitely there are some inconsistencies and strange behaviors entering the information on the table, I hope there is a way to improve it to be more consistent.

Title: IM Lab Link Testing - Wrong LUT values Imported from Max. to Motor-CAD
Message: IM Lab Link Testing - Wrong LUT values Imported from Max. to Motor-CAD The issue is related to the IM Lab Link and found during the AFT. The workflow works smoothly in all the steps of the split analysis. The problem is related to the LUT values we can see are imported into motor-CAD. If we look at the phase inductance and magnetizing inductance, they are: IMLookup Phase Inductance = [1 : 0.999999999999999 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1] IMLookup Magnetizing Inductance = [0.999839060707254 : 0.999844713438522 : 0.999883511195053 : 0.999909157375598 : 0.999925833108243 : 0.999937496990208 : 0.999946113398189 : 0.999952693507017 : 0.99995784093144 : 0.999961959511273 : 0.999965323245343 : 0.999968117332725] It looks that the phase inductance is not calculated properly, even though the flux linkage calculation through the FEA model in the Maxwell file appears to be correct. The flux linkage D increases with the current correctly in the optimetrics set up by the Setup Model. The inductance values follows a saturation pattern as expected, all different from ~1H as imported later into motor-CAD. The consequence of this issue in Motor-CAD Lab post-processing are clearly visible. The too high inductance value makes the torque vs. speed being quite strange: @Sufei Li  , @Etienne Kaiser  , please let us know the solution you're working on here, so we can track better the development. @Daniel Bachinski  , FYI

The issue seems to be originating due to the port. The simulation results below and also attached the simulation file.  Please help in knowing what is causing this issue and how to resolve it.

Title: [PyAEDT] Run ignores interferer set on interaction domain
Message: [PyAEDT] Run ignores interferer set on interaction domain Set one Rx and one Tx on an interaction domain Run that domain to get an interaction Get the worst instance from that interaction Get the domain from that worst instance Get the Tx from that domain The Tx on the resulting domain may not match the Tx that was set before running. This was found as part of an ACE micro-hackathon where we were attempting to write a PyAEDT script using the results API that recreates the Scenario matrix. When building the matrix, instead of getting the worst case EMI for each cell as expected when setting one Rx and one Tx, we instead always get the worst case EMI for the entire Rx row, even when setting a different Tx.   Attached a script that reproduces the error.  Run as-is to see what should be a Scenario matrix recreation showing the worst-case EMI for every Tx/Rx pair, but every cell within a row gets the same EMI.  Uncomment the two commented lines inside the loop to see the assert verify the set domain and resulting domain don't match.

Title: LSDSO: desktopjob problem with command line arguments containing commas
Message: LSDSO: desktopjob problem with command line arguments containing commas Some of the code used by desktopjob to create ansysedt command  lines uses a comma as an argument separator. This does not work correctly if any of the command line arguments contain one or more comma characters. I have not heard of customers experiencing this issue. I ran into it when using a local build of desktopjob. My locally built copy of desktopjob could not find the Ansys registry files, so it used the fallback for the temporary directory. On Windows, the fallback directory is a subdirectory of the OneDrive directory, which includes a comma in the pathname. The code for the fallback temporary directory  calls SHGetFolderPath() to get the CSIDL PERSONAL directory. This used to be the MyDocuments directory, but with recent Windows versions, it is the OneDrive Documents directory. On my office PC, the OneDrive folder is named "OneDrive - ANSYS, Inc". The embedded comma triggers this issue.

Title: Sound pipelines - build folders numbers on DFS do not always match exe build number
Message: Sound pipelines - build folders numbers on DFS do not always match exe build number DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : The build number in the folder name on DFS may not match the build number of the exe contained in this folder. The correct value is the one of the exe. Data: Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Run two pipelines Product simultaneously (SAS, JLT, DPF Sound) Once the pipelines are finished, it is very likely that some of the binaries version numbers and the version numbers used for the dfs folders or the pipeline log files are different for a same pipeline. > build number should be the same all along a same pipeline > two different pipeline runs should use two different build numbers Expected behavior: Build number in the folder name on DFS do match the build number of the exe contained in this folder CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): The stages of the different pipelines may interlace. In the Build stage, we read and update the build number, which is the correct number in the exe properties. In the Publish stage, we re-read this number (without modification).  However, if a Build stage of any pipeline was run between Build and Publish, it modified again the build number, which is now wrong. Solution : document work-in-progress:  Management of version numbers in Sound pipelines (work in progress).pptx Store the build number inside the pipeline, to transmit it from one stage to the next one. explore the possibility to use a "pipeline variable" if 1. is not possible, maybe try to transmit the info between steps via an artifact? Impacts : QA Validation: Doc:

Title: [regression] SAS - export spectrum as txt writes "nan" in the file, and the spectrum type is always "unknown"
Message: [regression] SAS - export spectrum as txt writes "nan" in the file, and the spectrum type is always "unknown" DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : When exporting a spectrum from a window, the exported values are nan. NB: this problem only happens when there is only 1 spectrum in the window Data: Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Open any file (1 channel only) Calculate the spectrum Go to File > Export > Export data in ASCII file... Type a filename and validate Open the file you just saved with a text editor Spectrum type is: unknown Level in dB is: nan Expected behavior: Spectrum type should be: the one displayed at the moment of the export Level value should be: the real value displayed in the spectrum window After discussion (HLE/SMA): even if there is only one spectrum in the window, ask the user which data (PSD, autospectrum, RMS, ... he/she wants to export CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): In case of only one spectrum in the window, no dialog was shown to the user. So the type of data to export was not set (remained as unknown). In the case of a spectrum computed from a signal, this unknown data is not filled -> NAN Solution : We always display the dialog to the user, in which he can choose which spectrum(s) he wants to export, and which spectrum type. Title: Unexpected scale change in the contours during accelerated animation
Message: Unexpected scale change in the contours during accelerated animation I uncovered this bug while investigating a critical crash with the same model. (To reproduce the crash, follow steps 1-4 of this (step 2 is optional), and swap "Equivalent Stress" for "Equivalent Total Strain" in step 5.) DESCRIPTION: During an accelerated animation, the animation will take some time to be "created" or "prepared." During this time, the unit scale will be accurate. However, the unit scale sometimes changes afterward and will continue to have the wrong scale until the animation is stopped, where the scale will change, but not to the scale it was at previously. So far, I have only gotten the bug to occur with the attached model with the below steps. The scale changed from [1.4e-10 to 1.267] to [0 to 8735.8], which suspiciously is the conversion factor between psi and Pa. Note that even when I run the animation in metric mode, the scale will still multiply by the same factor. 1.4e-10 and 1.267 are the minimum and maximum bounds of the psi values in all frames of the animation. (SOLVED: When stopping the animation, the scale will decrease by a factor of ~10000, but there is some nuance. The maximum value in the scale does not decrease by exactly that factor, but something close to it; and the minimum value increases from 0 to some small value. I found that the reason why this happens is when upon stopping the animation, the scale changes to the bounds of the last frame of the animation. It is a coincidence that this scaling happens to be within 0.05% of a 10000x scaling factor from before.) TO REPRODUCE: Open the attached model. Go to "Expansion Settings" in the tree. Click on the one of the leftmost checkboxes to enable "expand all results." This is necessary to get the required data that the animation will iterate over. Change the units to the bottom-most one, which is U.S. Customary. This is necessary to be able to solve the model. Solve the model. Go to "Equivalent Stress" in the tree. Go to the animation graph window. Set the frames to result sets by clicking the blue button directly to the left of the frame text box in the animation toolbar (this does not affect the bug, but it makes the bug easier to see). Run an animation, making sure accelerated animation is enabled. Notice how the for the first ~4 seconds of the graph, the animation is being "created" or "prepared" and the units are correct. Then, suddenly the scale change will happen and the model will be dark blue. PICTURES: Unit scale when the animation is stopped or not playing: (The correct) Unit scale while the animation is being "created"/"prepared": (The incorrect) unit scale after the animation has been "created"/"prepared": It has been discovered that this bug does  not  appear in 242. Mechanical Graphics

Title: NCAP traffic actors not correctly positioned in Headlamp + CM Cosimulation

Other traffic actors and static objects behave correctly, so I think  the problem is on the NCAP mesh/geometry   or maybe in the Headlamp code, if  the NCAP assets are treated differently than other traffic actors... Data : 25R1 Beta7 Notes : Xingshi 07/11/2024 :  Asset team did a first investigation. Changing parameters in CarMaker asset (such as translation or offset) do not change the position of the vehicle in LS. Attached the test carried out : testrun (CM12) with NCAP Hactchback (which has not wheels ans translation parameter) positioned at (0 0 0) in CarMaker. When doing LS CM cosimulation, the asset in LS is not positioned at (0 0 0). We suspect that the bug comes from connector side. Steps to reproduce: Install Beta7 Create a new Headlamp + CarMaker cosimulation project using the static track Place the NCAP bycicle at 4.65m -> in this case it will be right next to the ego car front bumper in CarMaker You can check also the IPG Movie output Now synch in Headlamp and check the rendering You'll see how the NCAP bycicle is rendered back inside the EGO The same problem can be seen with NCAP man and kid; the NCAP hatchback cannot be simulated (see #1163716) The behavior is CORRECT using static objects or other cars (a few items have been tried...) Expected behavior: NCAP bycicle placed correctly Reproducible :  always /  randomly  /  never Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version). Host   Host Name ex: AAPL2X7TFF7 Host Domain ex: win.ansys.com OS OS Name ex: Microsoft Windows 10 Enterprise OS Version ex: 10.0.19042 N/A Build 19042 System   System Manufacturer ex: Dell Inc. System Model ex: Precision 7560 Processor(s) ex:   Intel64 Family 6 Model 141 Stepping 1 GenuineIntel ~2496 Mhz GPU   Product Name                    ex: RTX A5000 Laptop GPU Driver Version ex: 463.15 CUDA Version ex: 11.2 ============================================== CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause  (if regression set an OPTIS REGRESSION tag): The Overhang was not take into account for the walkers type (bicycle is considered as a walker) Solution : The Overhang is now take into account. Impacts  (if there is a risk set an OPTIS RISK HIGH, OPTIS RISK MEDIUM or OPTIS RISK LOW tag): The assets for walker (man, woman and kid) need to be updated with a correct overhang on X (0 seems to be the correct value). The value is in :" CM Projects\AVX LS\2025R1\DataPools\CM12\Data\Traffic\Template\XXX ", for example : " CM Projects\AVX LS\2025R1\DataPools\CM12\Data\Traffic\Template\NCAP man " Patch : set an OPTIS PATCHABLE YES, OPTIS PATCHABLE NO, OPTIS PATCHABLE TBD tag. Title: Synchronization with Live is happening twice at different times when toggling Capture Sharp Edges option
Message: Synchronization with Live is happening twice at different times when toggling Capture Sharp Edges option There are two places handling resync with Live when Capture Sharp Edges option is toggled. The one in ApplySimulation happens first, but then GeometryCaching clears and resyncs again. A side problem with that is the booleaned body's Id map is regenerated. But ordering of the body in the Linq statement is not guaranteed, the Ids are changed on regeneration (even if bodies and faces are the same). Physics are resync'd after that so they should be OK.

Title: Friction state mapping between Mechanical and STD motion
Message: Friction state mapping between Mechanical and STD motion The current mapping rule to display friction states is as follows                   STD post -------> Mechanical value = 0(non contact) -----> 0 (near) value = 1(Stiction)  ---------> 3 (Sticking) value = 2(Static)  -----------> 3 ( Sticking ) value = 3(Transient) --------> 3 ( Sticking ) value = 4(Dynamic) --------> 2 (Sliding) In this case, Static & Transient states are treated as the "Sticking" state in Mechanical. It is quite weird because a contour result of a spinning disk under the dynamic threshold velocity indicates that it is under "Sticking" state even though it is sliding. I guess that the mapping should be changed as follows.          STD post --------------> Mechanical value = 0(non contact) -----> 0 (near) value = 1(Stiction)  ---------> 3 (Sticking) value = 2(Static)  -----------> 2 (Sliding) value = 3(Transient) --------> 2 (Sliding) value = 4(Dynamic) --------> 2 (Sliding) ================ (Manual part)=========================         < Mechanical Rule >                           < Standalone Post Rule > 2025 R2 KIL

Title: Endurance limit for sine sweep loading in the Mechanical Fatigue Tool
Message: Endurance limit for sine sweep loading in the Mechanical Fatigue Tool The Mechanical Fatigue Tool (FT) uses different endurance limits for single frequency loading and sine sweep loading.     For the single frequency calculation, the FT uses the last data point on the SN curve to establish the endurance limit (e.g.,1e8 cycles at 30 MPa).     For alternating stresses below 30 MPa, life in seconds is reported as 1e8 cycles divided by the frequency (e.g. for a frequency of 375 Hz, life = 1e8 cycles/375 Hz = 2.67e5 seconds).   For the sine sweep calculation, FT sets the endurance limit to be 1e32 cycles at the lowest stress on the SN curve (e.g., 30 MPa).  So, for alternating stresses below 30 MPa, life is reported as 1e32 cycles divided by the frequency (e.g., life = 1e32 cycles/375 Hz = 2.67e39 seconds). This large maximum life creates a skewed contour plot.   The behavior of the FT should be consistent for single frequency loading a sine sweep loading, so the FT should be modified to use the last data point on the SN curve to establish the endurance limit for sine sweep loading.

Title: Bearing Property window in Motion Pre: Axial vs. Radial Direction Inconsistency (Visual)
Message: Bearing Property window in Motion Pre: Axial vs. Radial Direction Inconsistency (Visual) The bearing graphic suggests that the X direction (blue arrow) represents the axial direction. However, the stiffness matrix indicates that the Z direction corresponds to the axial bearing direction. This is confirmed by applying a deformation of 0.05 mm in the Z direction, where FxDx and FyDy values are equal—consistent with axial behavior. Conversely, applying deformation in the X direction results in unequal translational stiffness values, which contradicts the expected symmetry for axial deformation. Example: A deformation of 0.03 mm in X yields non-zero stiffness values. A deformation of 0.03 mm in Z yields the expected zero values. Conclusion: This suggests that the Z axis is the actual axial direction, despite the graphic indicating otherwise. A revision is recommended to ensure that the bearing axes and their corresponding colors are consistent with the global coordinate system.

Title: pyDFPSound - Compute third octave levels operator always returns zero value at last band 16000Hz
Message: pyDFPSound - Compute third octave levels operator always returns zero value at last band 16000Hz DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : pyDFPSound: Compute third octave levels operator always returns zero value at last band 16000Hz Data: Python files, WAV signal. Reproducible:   always Steps to reproduce: DPF operator: " compute one third octave levels from psd " Use the attached python script and the attached WAV signal. The python script will load the " White noise mono.wav "and compute PSD levels in Pa^2/HZ.     >note that path to sound dpf dll and wav file will need to be updated for local use. The output of this PSD computation is used as input for third octave level computation. It will print the Third Octave frequencies and dB levels. The last band for Third octave always returns a zero value irrespective of signal used --> BUG Expected behavior: dB value of last band somewhat comparable to what returned from SAS. CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause   (if regression include [regression] in the title): An index issue would cause the last 1/3-octave band to be empty (the loop would stop after the previous iteration). Solution : Mostly, an additional iteration is done. Also algo's indexing was changed slightly (1-based -> 0-based) for better clarity, and the last band's upper limit was added in constants, as it's needed to know where to stop summing squared amplitudes. Impacts : QA Validation: Doc: Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Dataset error for imported layout comps with dataset dependent materials
Message: Dataset error for imported layout comps with dataset dependent materials This bug is related to " 1129095: Variable error when plotting fields on a layout component. " Assume a layout component has a material which is dependent on its project dataset (e.g. $dsTest). When we import this material and try to solve it, two errors are observed: If no $dsTest dataset exists in the parent design, then the material is not able to be read properly giving out an error. If $dsTest exists in the parent design, then the parent design dataset is read instead of layout component dataset, which is wrong. Thus two issues are: Incorrect mapping of layout dataset name to something unique (may be compName datasetName). Solving this will solve issue no. 2 discussed above. Incorrect writing of dataset to the solver file. Solving this will solve issue no. 1 discussed above. I have attached a test model here, but all other steps need to be copied from the related bug D1129095. This issue has always existed, and should be considered a new development. This is not a regression.

Title: Large Initial Mesh For Maxwell ECAD Simulations
Message: Large Initial Mesh For Maxwell ECAD Simulations We have been actively testing the APhi eddy current solver in AEDT Maxwell 25R2 for ECAD component simulations, in which we are using adpative meshing. We are using Phi+ mesher and getting a large initial mesh size (i.e. 3.5 M) for a PCB shared by Seattle in the secure chamber. We have tried reducing the mesh size in 3DL (i.e. 4-segmented via, limiting the max arc points as 4, turning off the lamba refinement, and setting the adaptive frequency as 1 MHz), however, we can only reduce the mesh to 2.9 M. The initial mesh size is too large and some of the mesh elements may be redundant. As a result, the adaptive meshing may not work as efficiently as expected. We would like our developers' advice on further reducing the initial mesh. Thank you so much for your consideration!

Title: warning messages from Genequiv logfile should be pushed to message manager in AEDT for the new Q3D/Maxwell RLGC dynamic link component
Message: warning messages from Genequiv logfile should be pushed to message manager in AEDT for the new Q3D/Maxwell RLGC dynamic link component Hi, The RLGC fitting tool does few things behind the scenes. For example, if the received training data for "RL" does not form a causal pair when the impedance data is being put together then we look at the fitting error achieved if it exceeds a prescribed threshold (5%) then we correct for the causality of the data yet do another fit to the causally corrected data, compare the original fit against the fit to the causally corrected data pick the better of the two. We also write a (warning) message in the Genequiv logfile. Yet as another example, we check the fit to "R" and if it is worse than 1% (relative) error and the target fitting error chosen exceeds 1e-4 then we decrease it to 1e-5 try another fit with the hopes of improving the fit to "R". Again, we do write a (warning) message in the Genequiv logfile. The objective here is to postprocess Genequiv logfile for these messages and then push them into the AEDT message manager. Here is a sample logfile: genequiv:progress 0: genequiv:message Reading input data: genequiv:progress 5: genequiv:message starting: genequiv:progress 95: genequiv:message ending: genequiv:warning 113 R fitting error exceeded 1%. Reducing error tolerance to 1.0e-5 to achieve a better fit. genequiv:progress 5: genequiv:message starting: genequiv:progress 95: genequiv:message ending: We'd like that message to be pushed as a status message into the AEDT message manager during the circuit dynamic link simulation with the Q3D\Maxwell RLGC component.  @Ryan Schimizzi   @Matthew Young   Maxwell/Q3D Dynamic Link

Title: MCD 25R2 Charlie: Fluent plug-in not finding any variables
Message: MCD 25R2 Charlie: Fluent plug-in not finding any variables Possible regression of issue:  921451  and/or Bug 1161734: MCD 25R1 Delta: Fluent plug-in not finding any variables   Steps to Reproduce: Install MCD 25R2 and Fluent 25R2 using unified installer (I used v252 Certified, which should be equivalent to the Charlie RC)  Download \\canwinfs1\phxqa\Test Cases\Shared Files for ADO (Do not Modify or Delete)\\ fluent completed tutorial exhaust manifold .zip and unzip it Create a new Fluent component in MCD. Select `Use Existing Directory` and select the exhaust manifold directory in the extracted directory Choose the manifold solution.cas.h5 file to open Eventually the component will load and will say that no input or output parameters were defined in the status bar 11/1/2024 1:51 PM Bug filed on "Fluent Plug-In with already saved and configured project" Step no. Result Title 1. None Setup: - Have Fluent 2022R1 BETA installed (for now) - Have downloaded the already completed and set up "fluent completed tutorial exhaust manifold.zip" file, extracted to an appropriate location. 2. None 1) Start ModelCenter, and save a new model to start with. 2) Double-click on the CAM Fluent plug-in, and in the "initialize PACZ" window, click on the "Use Existing Directory" button. 3) Browse for the parent directory of the completed exhaust manifold project (that contains the saved / generated case and data / parameter files), then click the "OK" button. 4) In the "Open" dialog, click on the "manifold solution.cas.h5" file (or whatever you named the case file to be), then click on the "Open" button. 5) The Opening process may take a few minutes; given time the "Select Variables" dialog will open. 6) In the "Select Variables" dialog, select the "inlet, inlet 1, inlet 2" variables as inputs, and "mass flow rate outlet op" as an output, then press the "OK" button. 7) Press the "Apply" button in the Fluent Plug-In to save it, then close it. 8) In the ModelCenter Desktop Component Tree, expand the variables to view the Fluent Plug-In variables, and set the values accordingly: inlet: 10 inlet 1: 15 inlet 2: 10 Then run the model. 9) The model may take a few minutes to run, so wait until finished. Expected Result - The plug-in was able to wrap the case file and parse the parameter input / output variables with no errors. - The value of the output is as such: mass flow rate outlet op: -0.11015196713186 Test Configuration: All Applicable Platforms

Title: bidl.exe 'include' statement uses only current folder to solve path
Message: 'include' statement uses only current folder to solve path The binary uses only the current folder to look for the included files. The issue has been spotted with AnsImage2.idl in the interfaces folder which includes AnsysCommon.idl. When compiled using the VS projects in the interfaces folder, it works. When build from another folder, it fails.  Expected actions: -> binary uses the same folder to solve the "include" as it uses to solve the idl "import" -> When inclusion fails, make fail with an explicit error. Current, the not found inclusion is just ignored which leads to misbehavior later - not necessarily easy to spot if you ignore the initial problem.

Title: Coupled field static analysis allows NLAD (non-linear adaptive region) definition but throws error
Message: Coupled field static analysis allows NLAD (non-linear adaptive region) definition but throws error Confirmed with 2025R1--- Coupled field static analysis, that it allows NLAD definition, but throws error when remeshing happens. Documentations-wise: Mechanical User Guide:  5.1.1.1. Requirements Static Structural analyses only MAPDL manual:  2.3. The project manager doesn't allow multi selection of port, but I could go to HFSS menu >> List and then multi select there and change the properties. Title: Matrix reordering file for volumetric shell elements
Message: Matrix reordering file for volumetric shell elements This defect is spawned from DE1320438. In attached project, user sets volumetric shell elements With this setting, we will have 4 instead of 2 matrix bandwidths because this condition is frequency dependent. For instance adapt frequency 5GHz (no tree-cotree, volumetric shell elements not triggered ) bandwidth 19.7 10MHz (no tree-cotree, volumetric shell elements triggered) bandwidth 20.5 5.05MHz (tree-cotree,   volumetric shell elements triggered) bandwidth 24.7 Note that matrix dimension remains the same when  volumetric shell elements are triggered. So matrix solver will not reject the file but will lead to incorrect result or crash as matrix is different. Therefore when saving matrix reordering file, we need to record this info the same way as tree-cotree. Please also take care mesh fusion solver as well. EBU SP Candidate

Title: Mesh plot cutoff at envelope if design has postprocessing variable
Message: Mesh plot cutoff at envelope if design has postprocessing variable See attached design with two components. One is set to do mesh assembly and has priority level enabled. The higher priority's envelope will cut out lower priority component and have it meshed with the higher priority component. This is expected.  However, if design has any post processing variable, the mesh plot of the lower priority component will stop at the boundary of the mesh envelope.  Step to reproduce: Open attached design, make sure priority level is enabled and comp lumped port set to do mesh assembly and has higher priority. Generate mesh. Plot mesh on the lower priority component (metal block). Observe that, if there is no post-processing variable defined, the mesh plot will include the part that's within the envelope but not intersecting higher priority component. Delete the mesh plot. Create a post-processing variable. Plot mesh on the lower priority component again, mesh plot will incorrectly stop at envelope boundary.

Title: AIT191: "inf" for anisotropic conductivity in via group causes Prism solver failure
Message: AIT191: "inf" for anisotropic conductivity in via group causes Prism solver failure For via groups, with solve-inside set, we derive an anisotropic conductivity on-the-fly.   For one of the Seattle cases, somehow the “Conductivity Area Ratio” is getting set to “inf” for a few of the via groups.  This is resulting in an invalid material definition and the solver is failing with an obscure “process gem3d: Invalid matrix entry on tet ID = 6619655” message.   In any event, can a change be made such that we always use a finite conductivity?  If it’s “inf”, we can revert to PEC conductivity of 1e+30.   Btw, my best guess is “Conductive Area Ratio” is somehow getting a divide by zero, which really shouldn’t happen (unless, perhaps, the area calculation fails?)… just the same, we should be catching the 0 and inf cases.  We don’t have the original Seattle geometry, so figuring out how we got into this state seems unlikely, but hopefully fixing downstream is easy enough.

This is affecting the adoptability of AEDT based Tsense workflow for DTech team.  Both DTech SoC group (Ajay Vadakkepatt) and Packaging group (Luis & Julian) are asking this fix as critical for their adoption since competitor like Celsius are able to load very large powernaps within a few mins. For attached example model having CTM of just 6400 sources, 2 mill cell count (Only 1 Mesh Region), total run time (AFTER mesh generation, so mesh time is not included) is 1 hr 26 mins, out of which actual solve  time is just 19 mins. Rest of the time is just loading the case writing and reading possibly due to each tile having its own zone and the CTM powerprofile UDF  Qualcomm

Title: Flux linkages not correctly calculated when full FEA method enabled for AC loss calculation
Message: Flux linkages not correctly calculated when full FEA method enabled for AC loss calculation The below description originates from SR00126067, where some unbalances in flux linkages were reported for a 72-slot, 4-pole, 6-phase machine when the full FEA method (single slot) is enabled. The customized winding pattern is balanced: I ran the model with Motor-CAD v2025.1.1, without any FEA method enabled first, and then with the full FEA (single slot, all slots) methods enabled. It seems that the field is correctly calculated as torque values from VW method are more or less the same for all three tests. However, flux linkages get unbalanced and may be not correctly calculated as soon as the FEA method is enabled. Case 1. No FEA method: Average torque (VW) = -90Nm Balanced flux linkages: Case 2. Full FEA method (single slot): Average torque (VW) = -90Nm, same as for case 1 Unbalanced flux linkages for phases 1 & 4. Note that the amplitudes of the flux linkages is quite different from case 1 FEA plot Case 3. Full FEA (all slots) Average torque (VW) = -90.14Nm, comparable to caases 1 & 2 Flux linkages are unbalanced (phases 1 & 4) and are not correctly calculated Note the negative d-axis inductance: For reference, Maxwell results are shown below (all conductors are modelled as Solid, with Eddy effects enabled): Torque = -88Nm -> OK Flux linkages are balanced as expected and show amplitudes close to flux linkages amplitudes from cases 2.

Title: SAS - "Display" images in psycho grid table not created when open file dialog is in use
Message: SAS - "Display" images in psycho grid table not created when open file dialog is in use DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : SAS sometimes displays a warning dialog stating that it could not find an image in PNG/ folder. (name of the image may change) However, the image is in the PNG folder besides the exe. 2 cases are described bellow. Note that other cases may exist but are still not found. In that case, please create a new bug, with the name of the image not found, a screenshot of the dialog, and a screenshot of the whole state of SAS Data: No data Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Open SAS Case 1 Open temporal file Open psycho module Launch many computation (ex all indicators on several signals). The computation must be long enough to allow doing something else Set focus back on temporal file Click on Open file. WAIT long enough before selecting a file and opening it, so that some new indicators which display curves should be filled in psycho table. Select a file to open, open. Following dialog opens Some "display" icons are missing in psycho results grid (empty cell, but clickable anyway) Case2: Open a signal, at least 20seconds duration Set some gain with the volume button, so that the play will clip after 5-10 seconds Play BEFORE IT BEGINS TO CLIP:  Click on Open file in toolbar.   WAIT long enough before selecting a file and opening it, so that some new indicators which display curves should be filled in psycho table. Select a file to open, open. Same kind of dialog opens, with  PNG/Volume clipped 48x48.png cited as not found Expected behavior: No dialog, no error Dev notes: possible solutions: Option 1:  use PNGs in ressources -> OK for our code, KO for code generated from wxFormBuilder Optoin 2:  change directory before / restore after creating images in very specific places (call on timer): OK, but difficult to identify all places where this may happen. actually identified:  wxBitmap creation in  gui BatchComputationResults::OnActualizeGrid Images in GKnob (to be precised), probably at least the clipped version (see GKnob::UseClippedKnob) Others ? -> look for wxTimer objects Option 3:  Create wxImage as class attribute, initialized during ctor CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): During the display of the wxFileDialog, the currentWorkingDirectory is probably modified, leading to the relative path PNG/XXX to no longer work. Solution : Create images at a time when no "Open" dialog may be displayed: during the creation of the containing class. Impacts : QA Validation: Doc:

Title: IM Lab vs. E-Mag discrepancy with FEA Advanced + FEA Map Resistance
Message: IM Lab vs. E-Mag discrepancy with FEA Advanced + FEA Map Resistance I have to report some unexpected results for the IM. This is originally from a customer ticket. The case is related to the E-mag vs. Lab comparison for a MTPA operating point. The Lab performance are computed using the Advanced FEA method with the FEA Map option for the rotor resistance. For the considered machine, the MTPA point at 8400 rpm and 395 A (max current) is analysed. Lab gives the following results: rotor frequency is 16.5 Hz. rotor cage loss is 7200 W. torque is 205.7 N m The MTPA operating point at 395 A is searched also with E-mag approach (sensitivity analysis varying the slip with SLP FEA) and the following results are derived: rotor frequency is 19.25 Hz. rotor cage loss is 8720 W. torque is 208.3 N m. The torque value is good, is it seems that the cage resistance in the two models is different: lower rotor frequency and cage loss in Lab, meaning that the resistance is under estimated. I have checked using the analytical resistance with the FEA Advanced Lab, and in the same MTPA operating point, I get this: rotor frequency is 20.5 Hz. cage loss is 8920 W. torque is 205.7 N m. The rotor frequency and cage loss estimation is now much closer to E-Mag.  To conclude the comparison, I compared the referred rotor resistance from the two Lab methods (analytical and FEA)  with the FEA Map resistance lookup table and I got this for the analytical lab approach: It looks that the resistance used by Lab within the equivalent circuit with the analytical resistance model is very close to the values from the FEA Map LUT. Since the analytical resistance methods gives good results, this confirms that the FEA Map resistance LUT have reasonable values which should produce a good match against E-Mag FEA. However, if I now compare the referred resistance used by lab eq. circ. when the resistance FEA Map is enable, they look quite different than the original LUT: The resistance used in the equivalent circuit is quite below the LUT values (leading to lower losses and rotor frequency). I think the original LUT from the FEA Map method is correct, but somewhere in the code (maybe in the interpolation or parameter transformation) the information is changed to a wrong value. I know it's a bit long comment, but I am fully available to go through this with you and help finding the issue within the code. Let me know! I tag  @Francesco Papini  into this, since he's the direct Magna contact.

Title: GUI Mismatch in Antipad Handling and DC Shorted Error Behavior in SIwave
Message: GUI Mismatch in Antipad Handling and DC Shorted Error Behavior in SIwave Starting from version 2022, the CAD input process ensures a default clearance between vias and cutouts by recognizing the presence of antipads defined around the vias. This is a change from earlier versions (2021 and below), where the Validation Check would ignore antipads if a cutout was present, potentially resulting in a DC shorted error. To align the Validation Check with the solver setup behavior, this has been revised. Consequently, even in versions 2022 and above, if the antipad is removed from the padstack, a DC shorted error will still occur. However, this updated behavior does not immediately reflect in the GUI, and it takes effect only when the Padstack window is turned on and off once.

Title: SAS - Wrong value in the highest band when computing octave-band levels with a frequency weighting (A, B, C)
Message: SAS - Wrong value in the highest band when computing octave-band levels with a frequency weighting (A, B, C) DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : The last octave band (16000 Hz) is wrong if computed with a frequency weighting. The issue does not occur with other bands, or if no weighting is used (ie when using SPL). Data: Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Open the attached signal Compute its spectrum Switch to 1/3 Octave Apply weighting A Pick up the levels of the 2 highest bands (12500 & 16000 Hz) >> 38.82 dBA & 27.46 dBA Switch to Octave Pick up the level of the highest band (16000 Hz) >> 27.46 dBA Expected behavior: If you repeat this without the A-weighting, you get a value that is larger than both the last 2 1/3 octave bands, which is what you would expect So here, the value should be larger than 38.82 dBA. 39.13 dBA to be precise CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): The last band is assigned the last 1/3-octave band value, instead of summing the last 2 bands A similar fix was done for non-weighted computation, but weighted case was omitted Solution : Replicate the same fix for the 3 weighted cases (that is, sum the last 2 1/3-octave bands) Impacts : QA Validation: Doc: Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: [LPE] Raytracing GPU crash when node visibility is set to false during simulation
Message: [LPE] Raytracing GPU crash when node visibility is set to false during simulation DESCRIPTION: Data : Based on the test "ReflectionTests.WithRaytracedReflection" Notes : When no point light is in the scene, there is a crash Steps to reproduce: Run the test  " ReflectionTests. WithRaytracedReflection" by replacing with this code [Theory] [MemberData(nameof(EnvData))] public void WithRaytracedReflection(string envName, string envRootPath) {     simulationParameters.BetaFeatures.RaytracedReflection = true;     var outputType = ImageOutputType.XYZOutput;     var scene      = LoadTestScene(envRootPath);     var scene = LoadTestScene(envRootPath);     var (tester, simulation) = CreateSimulationTester(scene,                                                         simulationDebugParameters,                                                         2048,                                                         1024);     // Bug 1322721: [LPE] Raytracing specular does not work properly     // If no point light is present in the scene, the test crashes     var lighting = scene.FindNodesContainingName("Lighting01");     foreach (var sceneNode in lighting)     {         sceneNode.IsVisible = false;     }     var camera01 = scene.ExtractCamera("01");     camera01.Adaptation = 36792.89f;     var poseCamera01 = camera01.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky {envName}", outputType);     var camera02 = scene.ExtractCamera("02");     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky {envName}", outputType);     var camera03 = scene.ExtractCamera("03");     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky {envName}", outputType);     var camera04 = scene.ExtractCamera("04");     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky {envName}", outputType);     tester.CompareResults(PixelTolerance, ImageTolerance);     var textureId = simulation.CreateTexture(Path.Combine(FileUtils.RootDataDirectory, "Input/Resources/Textures/HDR forest.hdr"), ColorSpace.Automatic).objectId;     simulation.ActivateImageBasedSky(textureId, 10000, 0);     var direction = new Vector3D(0.1, 1.0, 0.1);     direction.Normalize();     simulation.SetDirectionalLightVisibility(true);     simulation.SetDirectionalLightDirection(direction.X, direction.Y, direction.Z);     simulation.SetDirectionalLightExitance(10000.0);     simulation.EnableDirectionalShadows(true);     camera01.Parent.Pose = poseCamera01;     tester.Execute($"HdriSky {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"HdriSky {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"HdriSky {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"HdriSky {envName}", outputType);     simulation.DisableSky();     simulation.SetDirectionalLightVisibility(false);     camera01.Adaptation = 10.89f;     foreach (var sceneNode in lighting)     {         sceneNode.IsVisible = true;     }     Bug 1322721: [LPE] Raytracing specular does not work properly     HDRI sky is still rendered into the specular reflections, whereas it should not     camera01.Parent.Pose = poseCamera01;     tester.Execute($"Night {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"Night {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"Night {envName}", outputType);     camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;     tester.Execute($"Night {envName}", outputType);     tester.CompareResults(PixelTolerance, ImageTolerance); } Expected behavior: HDRI must be not visible into the specular reflections User texture coordinates channel must be picked according the user's provided ones Texture of the ground plane must be visible (anisotropic sampler?) MultiPoint lights must contribute into specular reflection When no point light is in the scene, the simulation must run Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): OS : N/A GPU : N/A Driver GPU : N/A Hardware specific :  N/A ============================================== CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause (if regression set an VRXP REGRESSION tag): Instead of setting PhysicalPointLight node object visibility to false the test was hiding a group containing multiple nodes. The real cause was that sfs have their geometry in acceleration structure and index/vertex buffers. When we set visibility to false the geometry is removed but the top acceleration structure don't have the geometries indexes updated accordingly. A crash was occuring in raytrace helpers function when fetching the bindless buffers based on the index offset and the index of the instance hit by the ray. Solution : When a modelInstance is added or removed the top acceleration structure is now rebuilt. Impacts (if there is a risk set an AVX RISK HIGH, AVX RISK MEDIUM or AVX RISK LOW tag): Notes : A second crash was occurring when running the test, this time linked to the validation layers. "GPU Assisted Validation". By default the layer setting "Generate warning on out of bounds accesses even if buffer robustness is enabled" is set to true. In SDK version (1.4.304 and maybe more) this feature has a bug that hardly slow the program and can lead to a crash. The feature has been removed in latest SDK version: 1.4.321 and the issue is now fixed. QA Validation: Doc :

Message: Samtec Connector Models on PCB Mesh Failures - 24.2, 25.1, 25.2 w/Beta flag @Bryan Boots @Sara Louie   Samtec sent two encrypted 3D component connector on PCB models that fail to mesh in 3DL.   AMD 1p35mm...aedt AMD 1p85mm...aedt Different encrypted 3D component connector models are in each.  They also sent the unencrypted 3D component for the 1p35mm project.
