Title: Q3D Prime Mesh Made Finer for Length Based Mesh Operation Than Requested
Message: Q3D Prime Mesh Made Finer for Length Based Mesh Operation Than Requested Using Q3D with the Prime mesher on a Samtec model of a 20x20 array of 0.9mm square pins with 0.1mm gaps, a 6mm mesh operation was added in design 5 , which was meant to improve the DCRL mesh from the left to the right images below.  The concern after seeing the mesh in the image on the left was the DCRL solver accuracy with such high aspect ratio elements.  Later I found that the DCRL result appears insensitive to DCRL mesh quality with answers appearing by eye to be well within 1%.   However, the 6mm length mesh operation is very important for the ACRL solve efficiency.  The 6mm mesh operation reduced the ACRL mesh from the left image below to right image (so more dense seeding for ACRL than DCRL).  The original ACRL RMS mesh length ~ 3mm, yielded good answers and a fast solve time.  After the 6mm mesh length operation was added, the ACRL RMS mesh length reduced to <1.3mm.   The ACRL solve time approximately went up 3x from 11 minutes to 31 minutes as a result of something I didn't ask to be done.   Why does the ACRL mesher take a 6mm mesh operation and reduce the ACRL RMS edge length from ~3mm to <1.3mm?  Look for "WORKS" or "FAILS" in design names as well as other description in the design name. 2025.1 Project 2025.2 Project A March 7, 2025R2 build was used for the results above. Ravi suggested this be assigned to Werner.

Title: [SSH Remote] Empty file created on download, handle not removed until optiSLang closed
Message: [SSH Remote] Empty file created on download, handle not removed until optiSLang closed See BugBash line 45 "If the download fails, sometimes a file with the name of the 'to be downloaded file' is created with 0 KB size that cannot be deleted until the optiSLang instance is closed!" Solution: The root cause is that libmssh creates the empty file but does not remove it on error. The fix needs to be implemented in libmssh. Additionally, the version needs to be increased and the package needs to be rebuilt and consumed in optiSLang.

Title: [SSH Remote] Input file from slot via files tab doesn't work
Message: [SSH Remote] Input file from slot via files tab doesn't work See BugBash feedback line 46 1. define an input file in the files tab as absolute path 2. Select use path from slot 3. The uploaded file is always the same from the absolute path definition Solution: We need to implement a custom PLM for the Files tab for Remote Profiles or at least SSH Remote Profile. The current implementation is too specific and not in line with how optiSLang behaves, e.g. you currently don't need to specify specifically that a file should be sent or received. We should decouple this whole Files tab functionality from the Operator part of the Remote Profile functionality and instead integrate it directly into the Files Tab. This would also allow any node (that supports the Files tab) to send/receive files using a Remote Profile. 2025 R2 Must Fix

Title: Not all conductive mask layers have correct material after import
Message: Not all conductive mask layers have correct material after import In 25.2, if "Import Shield Layers" is selected for brd import then these layers will be defined as conductors and have the material defined in the source design including nonzero conductivity if present.  However, other mask layers with conductive materials are still converted to dielectric.  In addition, without enabling "Import Shield Layers" even the EMI SHIELD * layers will be converted to dielectric with conductivity removed.  Customers expect that material properties set in the source design will be honored and conductor/dielectric type be chosen appropriately based on conductivity, even if they are not importing the shield layer geometry. To reproduce: Import attached design either with "Import Shield Layers" turned off or with it turned on with custom layer names EMI SHIELD S BOTTOM for the bottom shield and EMI SHIELD S TOP for the top shield. Note in the Messages window warnings from anstranslator about materials with non-zero conductivity and the associated layers being converted to dielectric: With "Import Shield Layers" off this will apply to both EMI SHIELD S * and SEL PLT * With "Import Shield Layers" on as described above this will apply only to SEL PLT *

Title: Multistage Analysis - If the number of surface effect pressure is equal to the real constant of a contact the solver generate an error

For example: If the real constant of the first contact is 5 and I generate 5 pressure, the real constant of the fifth pressure will be equal to the real constant of the firth contact after the duplication of the base sector (using CDWRITE and CDREAD). Consequently, the solver will generate an error: After duplicating the sector, we shouldn't have the same real constant for the contact and the SURF154 element I am adding the DS.DAT file, the CDB file and an archive of the project. Title: Need to mark Fluid specific result variables invalid when scoped to solid side of fluid solid interface with per face results option
Message: Need to mark Fluid specific result variables invalid when scoped to solid side of fluid solid interface with per face results option Enable the beta option 'Results on individual faces' and restart discovery Make sure 'Settings -> Results -> Monitor -> Monitor location for fluid simulations' is set to 'Individual faces' option Open attached model 'fluid variables on solid side.dsco' which is Mixer Tee sample model with velocity, static pressure and total pressure monitors scoped to solid side of fluid-solid interface.  Solve with LiveGX and notice that these monitors do not generate any value and there is a SID message:  "Monitor data failed to generate. Possible fixes include re-solving, reducing the fidelity, suppressing small features, and/or reducing anti-aliasing (in settings)". These monitors should be marked as invalid with a warning message stating they should be scoped to fluid side of the interface. We already throw a similar warning for force monitors: "Select one or more faces on a wall or the fluid side of a fluid-solid interface location for X Force 7" and the force monitor is marked invalid. Issue is not seen with Explore stage, Fluent solver and with per condition results. So it is specific to the combination of LiveGX and per face results. Issue found while investigating test:  Fluid NodalPriority VelocityAndSurfaceHeatFlux. DiscoPerFaceMonitors

Title: Share topology for tank-like geometries results in bad mesh if dynamic tolerances are not used
Message: Share topology for tank-like geometries results in bad mesh if dynamic tolerances are not used Consider the following geometry, a hollow tank with thick walls split in two: Using share topology with the default settings such that the interface between the two halves is shared results in a bad mesh. With multizone meshing, the mesher stalls until it fails with the error message: With tetrahedral meshing, the outer edge of one of the halves attempts to connect with the inner edge of the other half, resulting in an unphysical mesh: The workaround I found was to, when performing the share topology operation, enable the "Force Share" option, reducing the "Not-shared face pairs" number to zero: The mesh is then created correctly - for example, with multizone meshing: Perhaps this isn't really a bug, but is more of a potential pain point for users that should be documented/recommended. See attached file for example geometry where the topology share is not performed correctly. Found in TD 26R1 build 2025-06-11.

Message: AVX Sensors Sim : Fisheye camera rendering with fog feature shows dark artifacts DESCRIPTION:  Data : \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\LPE\AVX Sensors Sim  Fisheye camera rendering with fog feature  shows dark artifacts Notes : Steps to reproduce: Run the scenario  ScenarioColorFisheye.json given to you in data BUG : The fisheye rendering shows some dark artifact Expected behavior: Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): OS: N/A GPU: N/A Driver GPU: N/A Hardware specific: N/A ============================================== CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause (if regression set an VRXP REGRESSION tag): For day fog simulation we need the sky luminance which is fetched in the sky map at runtime using the curring view direction. For the fisheye we rendered a cubemap to simulate the wide field of view and each face is rendered separately. Therefore for each face we fetched a different sky map lumiance without interpolation. Solution : Fetch the sky lumiance once using the camera direction. Impacts (if there is a risk set an AVX RISK HIGH, AVX RISK MEDIUM or AVX RISK LOW tag): Notes : QA Validation: Doc : AVX COMPONENT SUSPICION; AVX INVESTIGATED

Message: AVX Sensors Sim : Fog rendering color changes based on the maximum visibility distance value in the init command DESCRIPTION: Data : \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\LPE\AVX Sensors Sim  Fog spectrum data rendering change depending of the value of maximum visibility distance given on the init command Notes : Steps to reproduce: Run the scenario given to you in data  Observe the rendering output ,all outputs images will be in a blue color  Edit WorldModel Spectrum t0.json and put  the value 50 for the maximum visibility distance parameter Run the scenario BUG : The outputs are all in dark rendering Expected behavior: we expect the distance change how transparent the rendering is but not the color  expectation is this image below :  Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): OS: N/A GPU: N/A Driver GPU: N/A Hardware specific: N/A ============================================== CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause (if regression set an VRXP REGRESSION tag): At first frame, when initiating the for pass, the diffuse sky map is not yet rendered so the fog binding is set to a black texture. Solution: Ensure that the fog pass binding are correctly updated when the sky has been updated or computed. Title: Forces in Eddy current solver
Message: Forces in Eddy current solver Dear Team, I have a case where the customer says that the help document was unclear on forces in the eddy current solver. The force experienced by a body in which there are induced eddy currents is the instantaneous force; the AC and DC forces are just a decomposition of that into a constant part (the time average) and an oscillating part (the full signal minus the time average). However, if the period of the oscillation is much shorter than the structural response time of the structure, then the structure will effectively feel the DC force, whereas if the period of the oscillation is similar to or longer than the structural response time of the structure, then the structure will effectively feel the instantaneous force. The instantaneous force and hence the AC force oscillate at twice the frequency of the input signal (that bit is clear in the documentation), but they are not necessarily in-phase with the input signal (that bit was not clear). If there is a phase shift, it is due to the impedance (inductance and/or capacitance) of the body. This also causes the instantaneous force to get offset vertically, leading to a non-zero DC force. This point caused particular confusion, because the oscillations were always about zero, hence a time average would always be zero. The phase shift above is between the induced EMF (in-phase with the input signal) and the induced current (phase shifted). This can be anywhere between + 90 degrees (purely inductive) and -90 degrees (purely capacitive). The corresponding vertical shift in the instantaneous force is such that the DC force can be anywhere between +/- the amplitude of the AC force. These are the points that were not clear in the documentation. Can we add more information to make the document clear?

Title: TAU Mesh Ignores Surface Approximation Normal Deviation Mesh Operation for Angle > 30deg
Message: TAU Mesh Ignores Surface Approximation Normal Deviation Mesh Operation for Angle > 30deg The below/attached test project was created to test the TAU and Classic mesher regarding mesh operation defeaturing.  This submission is focused on the Surface Approximation mesh operation. The surface approximation mesh operation Normal Deviation is applied to each of Box2/Circle2, Box3/Circle3, Box4/Circle4, and Box5/Circle5 with values of 30deg, 45deg, 60deg, and 90deg respectively.  For example, here is for the 30deg setting for Box2/Circle2. The classic mesher creates expected faceting for the 2D circles and for the filleted edges.  See design  1 ClassicNormalDeviation. For the filleted edges, 45deg and 60deg settings both yield 45deg arc resolution (2 edges around the 90deg bend) because a 90deg angle can only be broken evenly into 22.5deg, 30deg, 45deg, and 90deg increments.  However, Circle4 is able to be segmented as a hexagon.  The 90deg setting yields a single segment chamfered edge as expected for Box5 and a square for Circle5.  Significantly, the tetrahedra count drops from 680 for the default to 371, 344, and 104 tetrahedra for the 45deg, 60deg, and 90deg cases.   In contrast, the TAU mesher does not respect the surface approximation normal deviation setting greater than 30deg.  See design 2 TAUNormalDeviation . As shown in red, boxes 3, 4, and 5 have 30deg arc resolution (3 edges around the radiused bends), and the 2D circles use 12 facets (30deg resolution). Comparing the defeaturing of Classic vs TAU up close, the 90deg and 45deg Classic cases provide a substantial mesh reduction, but also good aspect ratios on the filleted edges.  TAU has a poor aspect ratios on the filleted edges and does not reduce the mesh. A further study in designs: 3 Classic90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation 4 TAU90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation uses the manual settings combination that I have used for many years as my "go-to", which is to enable both normal deviation with a big arc resolution value (45deg or 90deg) and max   surface deviation that ultimately controls the angular resolution.  This combination allows defeaturing electrically small radii while preserving larger rounds within mechanical tolerances. For this study, I set normal deviation to 90deg for Boxes/Circles 2 through 4, and set surface deviation from 0.01mm to 0.1mm.   The Classic mesher in  3 Classic90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation (except for an outlier for Box3) demonstrates the ability to combine these mesh operations as expected.  Note the circle objects (the electrically larger objects) demonstrating a facet count smoothly decreasing from 16 to 4 as the maximum deviation increases. The TAU mesher in design  4 TAU90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation  ignores the 90deg normal deviation setting, which makes the maximum surface deviation setting irrelevant/ignored as well.  The initial mesh and final mesh for this design is exactly the same as for  2 TAUNormalDeviation , despite the mesh operation settings being completely different. The findings are that: 1) the TAU mesher cannot be used to defeature geometry with the surface approximation mesh normal deviation operation higher than 30deg. 2) the aspect ratio of the TAU mesh on the small radiused features is substantially worse than the Classic mesher, which could lead to less accurate/reliable solutions at low signal levels. 3) the Classic mesher can reduce the mesh size of models with electrically small radiused features dramatically compared with the TAU mesher.  The 90deg case for Classic is over 3.5x less mesh than TAU. Many customer CAD models have electrically small, but long radiused features which severely impact the mesh size, run time, and RAM usage.  The capability to defeature is extremely important, but TAU does not offer defeaturing like Classic.  Unfortunately, Classic often fails and has been reported as increasingly failing in 2025R2.  TAU should either respect the mesh operation setting (this is what should happen given the huge gains), or if the development of that improvement will take more than one release, then a warning message should be issued during the interim, alerting the user that the mesh operation is being implemented as 30deg despite the user setting >30deg. If TAU can work as expected with the surface approximation mesh operation, the mesh could be reduced >3x on standard CAD features such as electrically small fillets.

Title: VCollab Parameter Report Differences
Message: VCollab Parameter Report Differences Created one bug to keep track of all current param report issues on VCollab's end. Investigated the others and a lot of them ended up not being bugs.  General - the <file> section has a "title" attribute. The content that appears in this section is correct; however, it should be called "label" instead of "title" scdocx native support - reports do not have the Spaceclaim version included. We would like this to be included if this is possible. General - the <section> format should be used over <table> unless the data is tabular. Taken from our schema: Metadata   MUST   be stored as   <text> / <number> / <boolean> / <date>   values in   <section> s instead of in   <table> s where feasible. Tables   SHOULD   be reserved for metadata that would make sense to display in a chart. Tables should be used to describes sets of data (such as parameter tables, charts, etc.). They MUST NOT be used to describe key-value-pair data. That should be done using the value elements grouped into sections. CylAbaqusInput.odb - components section is missing information

Title: SIMPLORER_HOME and SIWAVE_INSTALL_DIR environment variables are not available right after 25.2 Unified Install
Message: SIMPLORER HOME and SIWAVE INSTALL DIR environment variables are not available right after 25.2 Unified Install The environment variable SIMPLORER HOME is created by the installer pointing to the installation directory. Until 25.1, we hadn't seen any problems. However, in 25.2, even though this environment variable is added to the System Variable (can see by Start > Edit the system environment variables), it is not available to any other programs including Windows Power Shell and Command Prompt. But other environment variables like ANSYSEM ROOT252 do not have is problem - right after the installation they are readily available for all the programs. SIWAVE INSTALL DIR also suffers the same problem. Do you know if these environment variables are handled differently (like added at a later stage or something) than the regular environment variables like ANSYSEM ROOT252? If so, could this be fixed? If I restart the PC, then both SIMPLORER HOME and SIWAVE INSTALL DIR are available for all programs.  But we don't think asking customers to restart every time after the installation is not a good idea since the installer doesn't require a restart. We use this SIMPLORER HOME for Simulink Coder (to build Twin Builder model DLL for users' Simulink design). We could use ANSYSEM ROOT<Ver> instead, but the build script needs to be updated for every release.  Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Title: Bringing up the HUD for materials takes 6-7 seconds when Algoryx add-in is loaded
Message: Bringing up the HUD for materials takes 6-7 seconds when Algoryx add-in is loaded Bring up the material HUD is almost instantaneous but when Algoryx add-in is loaded it takes 6-7 seconds. The reason for the slowdown is the initialization of mediators done on the fly when the HUD is opened (for the purpose of collecting custom properties).  The problem had not reported so far and is probably due to the fact that Algoryx dll that contains the add-in is very large. While it could be broken up for other performance reasons as well, the initialization of mediators can only be done once.

Title: Analysis Editor Trees show Units for types that don't support units

I believe that these units don't show in the ExecutionPlan because the SME has been converted to a Variable/VariableMetadata, and Units aren't supported for those for Bool/String. The Bug I am reporting is the consistency of the display. Preference for what to show / how to handle / desired behavior is left to someone else at this point.

Title: Camera GT metadata when serialization is disabled are duplicated
Message: Camera GT metadata when serialization is disabled are duplicated DESCRIPTION: Data : Notes : QA DATA : \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\VSS\camera GT output data entries duplicated per time stamp in shm Note CGR: Ensure "serialize data": false in simulation parameters to disable serialization. Steps to reproduce: Run vss with arguments - p 20000 -d 50000 Run the scenario given to you in data Use a dataaccess client to get notification from databyidentifier (you can use for QA validation the sample in data ) BUG  : we have two ids with same metadata Expected behavior: As quoted in the fix of bug  Bug 1260145 : camera GT output data entries duplicated per time stamp in shm "with serialisation disabled we store raw image bytes and a separate serialised ground-truth (we must serialise GT because there is no raw representation)." so the metadata should reflect what we get from the output it means : one metadata for raw format  one metadata for GT format Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Machine configuration: Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): OS: N/A GPU: N/A Driver GPU: N/A Hardware specific: N/A ============================================== CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause (if regression set an VRXP REGRESSION tag): When serialization is disabled, the metadata information was duplicated when creating the metadata for the color map (which is the only output which can be non-serialized), and the metadata for the other outputs (which are serialized). Solution : Fix how the metadata are produced, by totally separating the color map from the other outputs.  Impacts (if there is a risk set an AVX RISK HIGH, AVX RISK MEDIUM or AVX RISK LOW tag): Notes : QA Validation: Doc : GDR 22/05/2025 KIL documented in 2025 R2 in AVxcelerate Sensors Simulator Users Guide Content: "Camera - When  Camera Ground Truth Parameters are set in the camera simulation parameters, and the serialize data parameter is set to false, the metadata sent in the notification to the data access client does not  precisely indicate the format of the data according to the dataId.  Metadata relevant to both Ground Truth Output Data and RAW image data is present for each notification. (TFS 1270686)" Preview link - for internal use only:  Known Issues  > Sensor Outputs Link to official helpsite that will be up-to-date on 2025 R2 FCA (leads to 404 page before FCA):  Known Issues  > Sensor Outputs 2026 R1 Must Fix; AVX INVESTIGATED; AVX KIL 25R2; AVX RISK LOW

Title: Speos tester tool - Simulation containing separation by sequence and LXP neverending with HPC CPU [BLOCKING]
Message: Speos tester tool - Simulation containing separation by sequence and LXP neverending with HPC CPU [BLOCKING] DESCRIPTION: Data : "Simplify large document at much as possible" \\tfsattach\TFSProd\Attachments\1301xxx\1301663 \ Notes : Issue found while creating auto tests for customer  Bug 1233639 Issue reproduced when scenario executed remotely with VPN and from office without VPN Issue specific to tester (not reproduced with speos core HPC outside of tester as described on Bug 1233639 ) Blocking creation of automatic test for customer  Bug 1233639 FDS:  Problem not limited to speos tester, can happen with any HPC simulation with sequence layering Regression (if so, last known build/version where it was working): Issue reproduced on 25R2 (2025.2.1.31394) and 26R1 (2026.1.0.31522-beta) Steps to reproduce: run with speos tester tool the test attached (DATA.zip) select CPU HPC run ; the test neverends: issue not reproduced with speos tester CPU local, and from speos tester CPU or speos tester CPU HPC Expected behavior: Simulation should end and give similar result than CPU run without HPC Reproducible  (always, never, often, sometimes):  always Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version): Windows 11 24H2 CLOSING SUMMARY: Cause   (if regression set a   SPEOS REGRESSION   tag): Mishandling of sequence merge when a large number of sequence is handled but not all process have yet reached this maximum number (eg: max seq = 500 but different HPC process have only identified 200, 450 bc they have not yet converged) Solution : Broadcast final number of threads from rank 0 to force all rank to have same number of layer in case found sequence is lower than number of sequence given by user Impacts   (if there is a risk set a   SPEOS RISK HIGH ,   SPEOS RISK MEDIUM , or   SPEOS RISK LOW   tag): HPC CPU simulation with sensor separated by sequence with number of sequence lower than number of sequence given by user Notes : FDS 07302025: reproduced the infinite test but was not systematic, when a break point in CreateFile was set the test ran without any issue Simulation stops around 90% and then gets stuck. Debug with child processes --> mpi thread seems to be lost --> mergesensors seems to be the point of problem --> 4 maps with diff layered map sizes Able to bypass this issue by using 40 000 000 rays instead of 10 000 000 --> each HPC process should have the same number of rays as the equivalent CPU simulation Problem not limited to speos tester, can happen with any HPC simulation with sequence layering Validation: Thanks to dev bypass (increasing rays nb to 4Mrays), I could capitalize the iniital test whose capitalization had conduced to this bug (speos tester 2106) even if the issue is not yet fixed   PR 14294 Support: Doc : SPEOS AUTOTEST; SPEOS RISK LOW

Title: DPF Sound: Octave/Third Octave levels computed by DPF Sound using time signal do not exactly match with SAS levels
Message: DPF Sound: Octave/Third Octave levels computed by DPF Sound using time signal do not exactly match with SAS levels DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : pySoundDPF: Octave/Third Octave levels computed by DPF using time signal do not match with SAS (little differences, and some higher differences in the upper frequency bands) Data: Python files, WAV signal and exported levels from SAS. Reproducible:   always Steps to reproduce: SAS Usage: Start a new session of SAS, open the attached WAV file "Acceleration with Tacho.wav". Compute spectrum and convert to octave band.  This octave levels can be exported to text file. Exported text files for Octave and Third Octave are attached here. DPF usage: " compute one third octave levels from signal" Use the attached python script to use the same signal and compute octave levels using the signal. Path to sound dpf dll and wav file will need to eb updated for local use. It will print the Octave/Third Octave dB levels. When compared with values from SAS we can see a mismatch in last band for Octave and last four bands for Third octave.--> BUG Third Octave comparison: Expected behavior: As we are using the same time signal to compute Octave/Third Octave levels should be same from SAS and DPF Sound. CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause   (if regression include [regression] in the title): The differences were due to the fact that in SAS (and not in DPF Sound), a fade-in is applied before computing the 1/3-octave levels in order to avoid artificially inflated higher-frequency band levels when the input signal does not start at 0 (because, typically, they could be calculated on a chunk of signal, that could then start at any value; but technically any opened signal could also start at a nonzero value). Solution : This fade-in operation is now moved into the framework such that it is always applied regardless of the application. SAS-returned values are not affected, but DPF Sound-returned values are now adjusted to match SAS values. Impacts : Although it should probably go unnoticed in the large majority of cases ,in DPF Sound, the modified (1/3-)octave levels calculation may also affect returned values for: Loudness ISO532-1 (stationary and time-varying) Sharpness   (stationary and time-varying) Articulation index (AI) Sound power level (SWL) The extent of the deviation depends on the signal.  As it only affects the first 10 ms, the effect is expected to be larger for shorter signals.  It also appears to be larger as the overall level decreases:  hardly noticeable (less than 0.1 dB) for "usual" acoustic levels (eg 50-80 dBSPL),  a few dB for absolute levels in the range 0-20 dBSPL,  up to 10 dB when the absolute level is around -20/-30 dBSPL. QA Validation: Doc:

Title: Trane on-demand expansion (disp) is 3.3x longer
Message: Trane on-demand expansion (disp) is 3.3x longer With 26.1 unified build + pydpf (master, Aug 27), run the lines below: (Assuming you already have access to the "Trane" files) import os from ansys.dpf import core as dpf from time import perf counter wd = r'C:/ANSYSDev/confidential/Trane' os.chdir(wd) op = dpf.operators.serialization.import symbolic workflow() op.inputs.string or path.connect(r'Trane disp.swf') # Frequency Response Function wf = op.outputs.workflow() t = perf counter() disp = wf.get output("contour", dpf.types.fields container) time for on demand expansion = perf counter() - t print(f"\n Time to compute Disp: {time for on demand expansion:.3f}s") => It was taking ~85s until the build of 2025-07-31. And s ince the build of 2025-08-20, it takes ~285s I was able to reproduce after a machine reboot, by comparing 25.2 vs 26.1 with the same pydpf (master). It consumed about 35GB of RAM in both cases without reaching the max of my machine.

Title: Effect of high velocity on Magnetic flux density in TEAM Problem 9 Simulation in Maxwell
Message: Effect of high velocity on Magnetic flux density in TEAM Problem 9 Simulation in Maxwell In the TEAM problem 9, the objective is determining the effect of high velocity on normal and tangential magnetic flux density (B) for both ferromagnetic and nonmagnetic material for two models. The model is set for different velocities: 0 m/s, 1 m/s, 10 m/s, and 100 m/s, as shown in the figure below (an example of the case for ferromagnetic material and measurement of Bz along L2), B does not follow the data points in the reference at higher velocities, specifically at 100 m/s.  It seems Maxwell results do not  accurately show the effect of high velocity. Here is how I obtained the results from Maxwell:  For example at V= 100 m/s, the time step is 1 ms. The velocity in MotionSetup is set to 100 m/s. Therefore, after 1 ms, the coil moves 100 mm. In the table of results for Br and Bz, I get (100 mm + x ) points where x is the required distance from the surface of the coil (0.1r, 0.5r, etc.) at the time B is at its maximum value (Bpeak/ sqrt(2)) which is 5ms in this simulation. We also enabled the eddy current setting but it didn't affect the results.  The aedt files as well as the ppt file explaining the results are attached for your reference.  I appreciate your consideration on this issue.   @Hui Niu   @Mohammad Shahabbasi

Title: [devops] JLT and SAS non-CI pipelines do not update build number
Message: [devops] JLT and SAS non-CI pipelines do not update build number DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : NON-CI Builds produced by pipelines for SAS and JLT do not update version number Data: Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Go to \\win.ansys.com\dfs\RG-EUROPE\Aix\Product Builds\Sound Compare build numbers (in folder names) for SAS, JLT and DPF builds, in 2025R1 folders, for builds created during the night Before 5th July 2024: build numbers are different for SAS, JLT and DPF After 17th July 2024: build numbers are the same for SAS, JLT and DPF Expected behavior: build numbers are always incremented, and can NEVER be the same for two folders (even for different applications) CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): DPF Sound pipeline was still correctly updating build number, and was executed first (at 1 am) SAS and JLT were not updating build number correctly, because of a wrong (?) syntax leading to only READ (and not UPDATE) the build number. Title: JLT - Build pipeline problem: impossible to run the pipeline if Agent Name is set and CI_BUILD is selected - might be more general (all yaml build pipelines)
Message: JLT - Build pipeline problem: impossible to run the pipeline if Agent Name is set and CI BUILD is selected - might be more general (all yaml build pipelines) DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : In JLT build pipeline, if CI BUILD is selected in ADO's GUI, and if AgentName is set different from Any, we get an error when clicking on Run. If CI BUILD is selected and AgentName is Any: everything is OK. Not tried: CI BUILD not selected, AgentName set SAS or DPF Sound pipelines EDIT AMD 2025/04/09: Issue is reproduced in SAS and DPFS, and regardless of CI BUILD state Data: Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Create new run of the JLT, SAS or DPFS pipeline Check the setting CI BUILD Check AgentName setting to AEPBUILD001 (or AEPBUILD002 ). you get this error: -> pipeline cannot be run Expected behavior: No error, pipelines run with the specified settings. CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): Wrong demands syntax in yaml scripts: two demands section must not be encountered twice in the same stage in pipeline run. But when you select a specific agent, you would encounter a first section with the common requirement (eg VIsualStudioBuilds) and then, passing an if condition on the agent, you would encounter a second testing agent name, which caused the error Solution : Restored old syntax where the two demands sections are defined under two mutually exclusive if conditions, such that you can never encounter both section within the same pipeline run Impacts : QA Validation: Doc:

Title: von Mises Stress Values from Abaqus .odb File in oSL ETK node cannot be used as either internal variable or response
Message: von Mises Stress Values from Abaqus .odb File in oSL ETK node cannot be used as either internal variable or response Hi All, I am currently working on a workflow (see image below) to extract von Mises field values from an Abaqus .odb file using the ETK node in oSL 25R1 (as part of oSL AFT). Specifically, I aim to retrieve von Mises stress values for S4R elements at a specific location, namely the SNEG (shell bottom surface). While I am able to check and visualize the extracted values in oSL (as in the two images below), I encounter an issue when attempting to use them as either an internal variable or a response (see red box below). The following error is returned:     ``` CODBFieldOutputVariable::Initialize : Exception : No data available for this selection (from RPC dispatch side). ``` Notably, this issue does not occur when working with nodal fields — it seems to be specific to stress invariants derived from the S tensor. I confirm I am able to extract von Mises stress values by means of the attached python code ( extractVonMises ) and by automatically generating a report by means of "Generate Report" batch node in the attached workflow (see   CrashTest Cyl Box.rpt   file attached for an example of generated report). Can you help me identify where the problem originates from? Thank you! Margherita

Title: GenerateModelDef generates u1_model.mesher_result file with slightly wrong Metrics for some LC
Message: GenerateModelDef generates u1 model.mesher result file with slightly wrong Metrics for some LC This is the followup bug after the fix of Bug 1209403: GenerateModelDef generates wrong mesher result file with zero Metrics My test shows that the metrics in the new U1 model.mesher result file is slightly bigger than the original metrics for some layout components. This is affecting HFSS simulation since we rely on this information to create mesh fusion envelopes, and the inaccurate size may cause error during mesh fusion. Here is an example. The attached LC1 1 edbWorkflow.aedtz is the project that we originally used to extract information by calling GMD. This project is created by directly   importing the edb file. The output file is model.mesher result In comparison, LC1 1 aedbcompWorkflow.aedtz is the project that we created using the new workflow where we convert the edb file into .aedmcomp file and then import it in to an empty layout design. We call GMD on this project and the U1 model.mesher result is the output. The GMD command used in both cases are: variation = oDesign.GetNominalVariation() oModule.GenerateModelDef(setups[0], variation, """$begin 'options' Output='some output location' NoAirBox=true ModelUnits='meters' ELCIntegration=true $end 'options' """)

Title: Display Cell Residuals using cell registers
Message: Display Cell Residuals using cell registers Method 1 – Cell Register via Threshold Percent (GUI-based): Via   Solution → Cell Registers , it is possible to create a   residual register   for specific equations (e.g., continuity, x/y/z velocity, kkk, ω\omegaω). By specifying a   Threshold Percent   (e.g., 90), Fluent includes the   top 10 % of cells with the highest local residuals   in the register. Method 2 – Residual Field Activation via TUI (/solve/set/expert): Using the TUI command: /solve/set/expert and enabling the option   “Keep temporary solver memory from being freed” , Fluent makes   cell-wise residual values available as a field variable   for post-processing. In the   Cell Registers   panel, one can then define a register using the   “Field Variable → Residuals”   option and select from various types (e.g.,   Top Value Cells ,   Above Value , etc.). Our question: We have noticed that, even when selecting equivalent criteria (e.g., "top 10 % of cells with the highest residuals"), the two methods result in   different sets of cells   being included in the register for x-velocity residue. Any reason for this?

Title: [regression] SAS - Sound Composer: for a source of type Spectrum, the display of the spectrum imported from a PSD in a txt file with AnsysSound_Spectrum header is incorrect
Message: [regression] SAS - Sound Composer: for a source of type Spectrum, the display of the spectrum imported from a PSD in a txt file with AnsysSound Spectrum header is incorrect DESCRIPTION ---- Text description : The spectrum imported as a Source of type Spectrum in the Sound Composer is not displayed correctly, which can make the user think the data used for the sound generation of this track is not the correct one (and actually the sound generation looks correct). Note: works well in 2024 R2 . Broken since 2025 R1. Data: Example 00 AnsysHeader PSD (PSD in dB/Hz) Example 00 AnsysHeader PSD (PSD in Pa2/Hz) Reproducible: always Steps to reproduce: Open the Sound Composer. Create new track. Select new source, with type Spectrum. Load the attached file  Example 00 AnsysHeader PSD . In the Source tab, click the Display button:  The displayed spectrum is not the one expected: the levels are incorrect, and the maximum frequency is 214 Hz instead of 3002.5 Hz. When the same file is imported from the menu File > Import > Import spectrum from text file..., the displayed spectrum is correct : Same problem with the second file attached :  Example 00 AnsysHeader PSD Notes: The same problem probably happens for every unit corresponding to a PSD in the txt file. I have not checked if the same issue happens with an Autospectrum -> NO Looks like the signal generated by the Sound composer has the correct spectrum! Expected behavior: The spectrum displayed is the same as the one in the source file. The display is done with the same unit (and hence the same type) as the one in the source file. CLOSING SUMMARY ---- Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title): Data causing this bug are not regularly spaced. For display, they are considered as if they were regularly spaced, starting at 0Hz -> wrong display Solution : As PSD data may not be regularly spaced, we choose to display the same data as the one used for sound generation: the regularly spaced interpolated PSD. Impacts : QA Validation: Doc: Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Prism Solver (defeaturing): Small Planes Removed Despite Connections
Message: Prism Solver (defeaturing): Small Planes Removed Despite Connections In some cases, small planes are being removed despite connecting to multiple vias. All structures are GND net. In the screenshot, the vias are being replaced with line vias to nowhere because the small horizontal plane also gets removed. This is from the Small Plane/No Void element in the SmallVias Padstack design of the attached project. Oddly, if the via on the right sits within a small void, then the plane sticks around and everything works as expected. Also, there is no issue when via removal is disabled (see KeepVias Padstack design). It is not necessary to look at the StackedVias Padstack design for this defect, but it does demonstrate the same plane removal behavior with some different via configurations. I also ran the same designs with classic vias drawn in a via layer and the behavior was identical. Via Groups look a bit different, but I suspect they are not drawn correctly (no pads). I'll check with @Aman Samaiyar  on those next week and follow up once we have a good Via Group design.
